Contents

Consolidated volume · 17 documents · the complete contract

Nizam-e-Qanoonنظامِ قانون

Pakistan’s first intelligent legal infrastructure: a bilingual, offline-capable platform over the statutory corpus and judicial precedent of the federation and four provinces. This volume binds every specification document into one reference.

Volume 1.0 Compiled 30 August 2026 Parts 17 Sections 224 Figures 88 Project FYP · GIKI FCSE

The five invariants

These are rejection criteria, not aspirations. A design that violates one is wrong regardless of how well it performs. Every part of this volume inherits them.

  • INV-1No generated citation.

    Section numbers, article numbers, case citations, dates and URLs are rendered from database records. The model emits identifiers only.

  • INV-2No answer without a passing gate.

    retrieve() returns GroundingContext | Abstention — two-valued. No third return, no retry at a lower threshold, no fallback to model knowledge.

  • INV-3Every answer is replayable.

    Query, filters, retrieved IDs with scores, gate decision, prompt hash, model version and verifier result are persisted for every response.

  • INV-4Provisions are the citable unit.

    No chunk identifier above L2. Re-chunking must never break a stored citation.

  • INV-5Law is answered as at a date.

    Every retrieval carries as_of. Read operative_provision, never the base table.

Layer rule. A layer calls only the layer immediately below it, plus the shared inference worker. L1 corpus → L2 storage → L3 retrieval → L4 generation → L5 services → L6 API → L7 clients.

The corpus, measured

Measured from data/ on 28 August 2026, not estimated. These figures set the sizing, the hosting ladder and the scope of OCR; Part 03a shows the method.

4,595distinct source PDFs archived; 4,716 official observations
128.6 Mactive extracted characters across 63,047 pages
512,094active provision nodes across 4,788 legal expressions
106 docscarry accepted OCR evidence; clean extraction remains the primary path
1,682 MBhot statutory build after multi-expression materialisation and safe compaction
~10 GBwith case law included
14.2 GBRAM for production at 50k MAU
~3%share of the bill that is infrastructure, at scale

§0Purpose
& map

What this document is

This is the root of the specification set. It fixes the layer boundaries, the domain model, and the interface contracts between layers — and nothing else. Each layer then gets its own document that may change freely inside its boundary without amending this one.

This document decidesThis document deliberately does not
Layer boundaries and what each layer owns · the domain model and its vocabulary · the contract crossing every boundary · the deployment topology · the quality attributes every layer is held to · module ownership Internal design of any layer · class-level design inside a module · API endpoint catalogue · database DDL · UI screens · prompt text · test plans — all of these belong to the layer documents below

0.3Standing rules

Five invariants hold everywhere. A design that violates one of these is wrong regardless of how well it performs, and reviewers should reject it on that basis alone.

#InvariantEnforced by
INV-1No generated citationSection numbers, article numbers, case citations, dates and URLs are always rendered from database records. The generator emits identifiers only. L4 schema validation drops any block whose identifier does not resolve.
INV-2No answer without a passing gateThere is no code path from an abstained retrieval to a generated answer. L3 returns either a grounding context or an abstention; L4 accepts only the former.
INV-3Every answer is replayableL6 persists query, resolved filters, retrieved provision IDs with scores, gate decision, prompt hash, model version and verifier result for every response.
INV-4Provisions are the citable unitNothing outside L2 may reference a chunk identifier. Re-chunking must never invalidate a stored citation, bookmark or generated document.
INV-5Law is answered as at a dateEvery retrieval carries as_of, defaulting to today. No query path may read provision_version without a validity filter.
§1Context
& drivers

Context and quality attributes

Architecture is the set of decisions that are expensive to reverse. Those decisions are driven by quality attributes, not features — so the measurable targets come first, and every structural choice later in this document traces back to one of them.

1.2Constraints taken as given

KindConstraintArchitectural consequence
BusinessAdvocates and law students are the paid tier; citizens use a free tier with a simple UITwo client presentations over one grounded payload. Depth is a rendering concern, not a separate pipeline.
BusinessB2B and institutional access deferred until the platform is establishedThe API layer is designed with metering and key scoping from the start, but not exposed publicly in v1.
TechnicalTeam of four, ~24 weeks, no dedicated opsModular monolith, one datastore, no orchestrator. Complexity budget spent on the corpus, not the platform.
TechnicalSub-$100/month running costSelf-host every small model; rent GPU by the hour for batch only; zero-egress object storage.
EnvironmentalMobile-dominant, intermittent connectivity, Android-majorityOffline is a mode, not a cache. Signed delta updates. Android-first testing.
LegalLegal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act — information, not adviceOutput register is enforced structurally (QA-13), not left to prompt wording.
LegalReporter series (PLD, SCMR, YLR) headnotes are third-party copyrightOnly official court text is ingested. Reporter references stored as identifiers only.
RegulatoryPersonal Data Protection Bill anticipatedDeletion propagates to backups; data minimisation and anonymous mode designed in, not retrofitted.
§2Actors
& use cases

The use-case model

Built around the advocate, because that is the actor who pays, who exercises the deepest paths, and who finds our errors fastest. Citizen use cases run over the same services with a simpler presentation — not a reduced pipeline.

2.2Primary scenario — UC-03, expanded

The one use case worth writing out in full, because every invariant shows up in it.

PreconditionCorpus published for the resolved jurisdiction; actor authenticated or in an anonymous session.
Main flow1. Actor submits a question.  2. L3 resolves language, jurisdiction, as_of and intent.  3. If an explicit citation is detected, UC-02 runs instead and the flow ends.  4. Four candidate generators run in parallel; results fuse by RRF.  5. Cross-encoder reranks.  6. Gate evaluates against τ.  7. Context assembles whole provisions with validity and repeal state.  8. L4 generates a structured answer carrying citation identifiers.  9. Citation text is rendered from L2.  10. Verifier checks each claim against its cited span.  11. Answer streams to the client with per-claim provenance.  12. Audit record persisted.
A1 — gate failsAt step 6, no candidate clears τ. System returns an abstention naming what it searched, plus non-passing results explicitly labelled as unconfirmed. No generation occurs.
A2 — identifier unresolvedAt step 9, a citation identifier does not resolve. The block is dropped, the event logged as a defect, and the remaining answer is returned with a completeness note.
A3 — verification failsAt step 10, a claim is not entailed by its span. Below the drop threshold the block is removed; between drop and pass it is shown with a visible qualifier.
A4 — repealed law matchedRetrieved provision is repealed or was not in force at as_of. It is returned with a prominent status banner and never as the operative answer.
A5 — provider unavailableL4 provider port fails over; if all providers fail, the system degrades to UC-01 results plus stored explainers and says so.
PostconditionAn audit record exists sufficient to replay the answer exactly (INV-3). In anonymous mode, no record of query or answer content is written.
§3Domain
model

The law as data

Get this wrong and no amount of retrieval quality rescues the product. The model has to represent three things most legal databases do not: that a provision is a node in a tree, that its text changes over time, and that a citation points at a provision rather than at a page.

3.1Provision identity

Public, stable, human-readable, and resolvable without a database round trip for the common case.

pk:fed/act/1860-45/ch-XVI/s-302/cl-c
|   |    |         |        |     |
|   |    |         |        |     +-- clause      ProvisionKind, ordinal within parent
|   |    |         |        +-------- section     label preserved verbatim: 302, 337A, 365 A
|   |    |         +----------------- chapter     roman numeral as printed
|   |    +--------------------------- instrument  year-number, the gazette identity
|   +-------------------------------- kind        act|ord|order|rules|sro|notif|const
+------------------------------------ scope       fed|punjab|sindh|kp|balochistan|ict|ajk|gb

Stored as ltree.  Subtree query: path <@ 'fed.act.1860_45.ch_XVI'
                  Ancestor query: path @> 'fed.act.1860_45.ch_XVI.s_302.cl_c'
                  Both GiST-indexed. Neither needs a recursive join.

3.2Enumerations

Jurisdiction    fed · punjab · sindh · kp · balochistan · ict · ajk · gb
InstrumentKind  constitution · act · ordinance · order · regulation · rules · sro · notification
ProvisionKind   part · chapter · section · article · subsection · clause · proviso
                explanation · illustration · schedule · preamble
LifecycleState  in_force · repealed · spent · lapsed · not_yet_commenced
VersionOp       original · inserted · substituted · omitted · amended
Court           SC · FSC · LHC · SHC · PHC · BHC · IHC
Treatment       cites · applies · interprets · follows · distinguishes · doubts · overrules
Disposition     allowed · dismissed · partly_allowed · remanded · disposed
§4Container
view

Container architecture

Nine deployable units. The count is deliberately low: a team of four cannot operate a service mesh and also build a corpus, and nothing here needs to scale independently except inference.

4.1Layer interface contracts

These are the only calls that may cross a layer boundary. Anything else is a violation and should be caught in review.

InterfaceProviderConsumersShape
ICorpusWriteL2L1publish(instrument, provisions[], versions[], edges[], gate_report) → PublishResult — one transaction per instrument, all-or-nothing
ICorpusReadL2L3 L5 L6getProvision(id, as_of) · getSubtree(path, as_of) · getVersionChain(id) · getJudgment(id)
IIndexSearchL2L3lexical(q, filters, k) · dense(vec, filters, k) · graphExpand(ids, depth) — all filter on as_of and jurisdiction
IRetrieveL3L4 L5 L6retrieve(QuerySpec) → GroundingContext | Abstention — the gate lives here; there is no third return value
IInferenceWorkerL3 L4embed(texts[]) · rerank(query, docs[]) · entail(premise, hypothesis)
IGenerateL4L5 L6answer(GroundingContext, style) → VerifiedAnswer — citations already resolved and verified on return
ILLMProvideradapterL4 onlycomplete(prompt, schema, cache_key) · stream(...) — the only place a vendor SDK may appear
IPrecedentL5L6treatmentsOf(provision_id, filters) · summarise(judgment_id) · goodLawSignal(judgment_id)
IDraftL5L6startInterview(type, jurisdiction) · submitAnswers(session, answers) · render(session) → PDF + provenance
IProcedureL5L6guide(procedure_id, jurisdiction) · limitation(cause, date) · courtFee(value, relief) · forum(matter)
IPublicAPIL6L7REST + SSE, versioned, OpenAPI-described. The only surface any client may call.
ISyncL6L7packManifest(current_version) → signed patch chain — corpus distribution, one way, signed, never merged. Patches also carry INVALIDATE operations for stored answers whose cited provisions changed.
IUserSyncL6L7push(outbox[]) · pull(since_cursor) → {records[], tombstones[], cursor} — bookmarks, matters, drafts and history. Bidirectional, last-writer-wins on a server-assigned version. Separate engine from ISync, separate trust model (ADR-1b).
ILexicalSearchL2L3lexical(q, filters, k) → ranked[] — the seam that keeps the database host swappable (ADR-1a). Two implementations: pg_search BM25 and a tsvector fallback, benchmarked against each other on the golden set.
§5Data
flow

Data flow decomposition

Three levels, Gane-Sarson notation. The value of the DFD view here is that it makes the stores explicit — and the store boundaries are where most integrity bugs in a system like this will live.

specs

§7Runtime
interactions

Sequence views

Three interactions worth pinning to the message level: the one that carries the grounding contract, the one that produces a legally operative artefact, and the one that has to work with no network.

§8Modules
& ownership

Module decomposition

Ownership is by layer, not by feature, so each person owns an interface they must keep stable rather than a screen they can change freely. That is what makes four people working in one repository tractable.

8.1Ownership and the review rule

OwnerPackagesAccountable forMust review
Data engineercorpus · storage · workersQA-4 corpus integrity, QA-5 temporal correctness. The hardest seat and the one the whole product rests on.Any migration; any change to a QA gate.
Retrieval engineerretrieval · generation · evalsQA-1 groundedness, QA-2 abstention, QA-3 retrieval quality, QA-6 bilingual parity.Any prompt, threshold, or scoring change; any golden-set edit.
Application engineerdomain · apiQA-7 auditability, QA-13 legal safety, correctness of every deterministic calculator.Any change to a clause rule or a statutory table.
Client engineerclientsQA-9 offline capability, QA-14 accessibility, bilingual and RTL presentation.Any change to IPublicAPI or ISync.
All fourshared · ops · golden setInterface contracts in §4.1 and the invariants in §0.3.Any change to this document. Two approvals required.

The one automated rule worth enforcing: an import-linter configuration in CI that fails the build if a package imports across a forbidden layer boundary. It is about twenty lines of configuration and it is the only thing that will keep the dependency graph in Figure 8 true six months from now.

§9Runtime
operations

Deployment and degradation

A single-node system with an honest availability target is more useful than a distributed one nobody can operate. What matters architecturally is not uptime but what the system does as pieces fail.

9.1The degradation ladder

Each rung names a component failure and the capability that survives it. Every rung is a code path that must be tested, not a hope.

FailureLostRetainedUser sees
LLM provider unreachableAnswers to questions outside the stored set, judgment summarisation, interview phrasingAll search, citation lookup, precedent lists, stored explainers, calculators, procedure guides — and every answer in the pre-generated answer tierA banner naming the degraded capability. Because answers were batch-generated and verified ahead of time, the head of the query distribution is unaffected by a provider outage.
Inference worker downDense retrieval, reranking, entailment verification → therefore all generation (INV-2 blocks ungated answers)BM25 search, citation fast path, whole-provision browsing, everything deterministicLexical search only, labelled as such. The system does not silently lower τ.
Database unreachableEverything server-sideThe entire offline pack on any device that has oneApp falls through to local pack automatically; web shows a status page.
Ingest worker downNew and amended law does not arriveAll servingNothing, until staleness exceeds the threshold — then a corpus-currency notice appears.
Object store unreachableSource PDF viewing, new document downloads, pack updatesAll text, all search, all answersSource-PDF links disabled; nothing else changes.
No client connectivityGeneration, precedent, drafting, anything requiring the serverFull statutory search and browse, stored explainers, offline calculatorsOffline mode, entered automatically and stated plainly.

The rule that makes this coherent

Degradation is always announced and narrower, never silent and approximate. The system may say “I can only search the text right now”; it may never quietly answer with a lower confidence bar. This follows directly from QA-2 and is why no failure path anywhere is permitted to lower τ, skip verification, or substitute an ungrounded answer.

9.2Environments and promotion

EnvironmentShapeCorpusPromotion gate
LocalDocker Compose, one Postgres, seeded subsetPPC + Constitution only, ~40 instrumentsUnit tests, import-linter, migration reversibility
CIEphemeral Postgres per runFixture corpus with hand-labelled ground truthGolden-set NDCG@10 and faithfulness must not regress; red-team suite green
StagingSame host as production, separate database and schemaFull corpus, restored from last night’s backupSmoke suite over the 16 use cases; a manual pass over 20 golden answers
ProductionTwo nodes (app, database) + edge + R2Live, published only through the gate runnerMigrations applied ahead of code; every deploy tagged and rollback-tested

9.3Observability requirements on every layer

  • Trace — one span per pipeline stage, carrying its scores. A retrieval trace without candidate scores is not debuggable, and most of the hard bugs in this system will be retrieval bugs.
  • Replay — INV-3 makes every answer reconstructible. This is the mechanism behind UC-16 and the only credible response to “the system told me the wrong thing.”
  • Corpus currency — per-source last-successful-fetch, exposed as a metric and surfaced in the UI when stale.
  • Gate telemetry — abstention rate by intent and language, tracked continuously. A sudden drop means τ is drifting or the corpus changed shape; a sudden rise means retrieval broke.
  • Cost per answer — a first-class metric, since QA-10 is an architectural target and not a footnote.

Appendix B — Architecture decision records

All twelve are accepted. Each has a one-line consequence that is checkable in code, which is what distinguishes a decision from a preference.

ADRDecisionDrivesCheckable consequence
ADR-1One Postgres for relational, vector, lexical and graphQA-10 QA-11No second datastore client library appears anywhere in nizam/. Chunk row and its vector are written in the same transaction.
ADR-1aHosting is a four-stage ladder, not a single choiceQA-3 QA-10 QA-11Stage 0 local Docker with the full corpus and every extension; stage 1 a managed free tier publishing federal statutes only (measured 248 MB against a 500 MB ceiling); stage 2 a self-hosted node once case law lands; stage 3 vertical then replicas. Real BM25 needs ParadeDB pg_search, which no managed host permits, so lexical retrieval sits behind ILexicalSearch and the tsvector fallback’s ranking delta is measured against the local baseline. Moving rungs changes a connection string, a bound implementation, and the published scope — nothing else. Sized in the capacity plan.
ADR-1fFull-scale target is a single self-hosted nodeQA-3 QA-8 QA-10Managed Postgres hosts the database, not the system: inference workers, ingest workers, the LaTeX sandbox and the staging filesystem still need a second host, and every query then crosses the public internet. One node runs all of it with pg_search available and the database on a loopback socket, at roughly a fifth of the cost. The self-hosted Supabase stack may run on top of it for the same developer surface without the extension lock-out. Sized in the capacity plan §5.2.
ADR-1gSchema is migrations in git; engine is a pinned imageQA-11The production database is built locally at full scale — every statute, judgment, embedding and index — on the same pinned Postgres image the server will run. Moving to the own-node target is then a pgBackRest restore rehearsed by the monthly drill, not a migration. A schema created by hand in a GUI is reproducible nowhere and is treated as a defect.
ADR-1dVectors stored binary-quantised as bit(1024)QA-3 QA-1032× smaller than float32 — 51 MB instead of 1,577 MB at full statutory scale. Safe only because a cross-encoder already reranks by reading provision text, so stage-1 dense retrieval need only preserve recall; candidates are over-fetched 10×. Ships only after an ablation reporting Recall@50 and NDCG@10 at float32, halfvec(384) and bit(1024); if binary costs more than two NDCG points after reranking, fall back to halfvec and narrow the corpus scope.
ADR-1ePublished corpus scope is a deployment parameterQA-10 QA-11The gate runner promotes instruments to the live index by scope tag. The same schema and migrations serve a 248 MB demo and a 10 GB pilot, so narrowing scope to fit a host is a configuration change and never a schema compromise.
ADR-1bTwo sync engines: signed one-way corpus, merged bidirectional user dataQA-9 QA-11Corpus patches are server-authored and signed, so no merge logic exists and the device is never a writer. User data syncs last-writer-wins on a server-assigned version with tombstones. Specified in document 08 §3.5.
ADR-1cOffline answers ship as verified artefacts, not as an on-device generatorQA-1 QA-9 QA-10L4 batch-generates and verifies answers to the head of the query distribution; they ship in a 12 MB pack tier with their citations and the provisions they depend on. A patch that amends a cited provision invalidates every dependent answer. Specified in document 08 §3.4.

Part 02 — Corpus and Ingestion

02Layer L1

Corpus and Ingestion

How official Pakistani law becomes a versioned, citable and quality-gated corpus—once per source revision, never during a user query.

Version 1.0Layer L1Provides ICorpusCandidateConsumes official publications onlyBaseline 4,710 PDFs · measured 28 Aug 2026
↑ Contents
§0Mandate

The corpus is evidence, not a folder of PDFs

The five downloaded archives are a strong baseline: 4,710 official-code PDFs, 1,857 MB on disk and about 243 MB after text extraction. They are not yet a legally dependable corpus. A dependable corpus also knows where each file came from, when it was fetched, what publication it represents, what it changes, where every provision appears on the source page, and whether the result passed objective gates.

Non-negotiable rule

PDF extraction is performed once for a new content hash. Search, RAG and document generation read structured rows from Document 03. They never open or parse a PDF. A file is reprocessed only when its bytes change, the parser version changes, or a curator explicitly requests repair.

This layer ownsThis layer does not own
Source discovery, respectful fetching, immutable blobs, manifests, text/OCR extraction, layout recovery, legal segmentation, metadata and relationship candidates, QA gates, curation packages and publication requestsProduction database constraints and indexes (03), ranking (04), answer generation (05), legal tools (06), APIs (07), or client presentation (08)
Evidence for every derived fact: source URL, file hash, page, span, parser version, confidence and review stateDeclaring a provision legally operative from an uncertain inference. Unresolved commencement or invalidation remains explicitly unknown
§1Authority
model

Keep the publication, consolidation and cross-check separate

Several official sites may carry the same Act, but they do not play the same evidential role. The pipeline records each observation and resolves them by authority and date; it never silently overwrites one official copy with another.

RankSource roleUseConflict policy
A1Official Gazette publicationEnacted text, notification number, publication date, commencement notices, rules and SROsPreserve as the publication event. Escalate a byte/text conflict; never auto-merge
A2Official legislature recordAct number, passage, assent, Gazette date and newly enacted PDFCross-check A1; useful as the fastest new-law signal
A3Government law-code consolidationConvenient current text, amendments incorporated, subject and chronology indexesServe only with its consolidation date; verify changes against A1/A2
A4Court or regulator publicationJudgments, orders, rules, regulations, circulars and sector instrumentsAuthoritative for that issuing body; connect to the enabling law and later appellate treatment
A5Secondary discovery sourceFinding a missing citation or documentNever publish from it. Use it only to locate an A1–A4 copy

A source is “official” because it is controlled by the issuing government, legislature, court or regulator—not merely because its domain looks governmental. Every adapter is manually approved once with organization, jurisdiction, TLS status, publication role and terms recorded in the source registry.

§3Acquisition

Every fetch is reproducible and non-destructive

3.1Fetcher contract

  • Identify the client and obey published robots and rate constraints; one host-specific token bucket, jitter and exponential backoff.
  • Use If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since where supported. A 304 records freshness without downloading or parsing.
  • Accept a PDF only when HTTP succeeds, MIME sniffing and %PDF- agree, size is plausible and the full-stream hash completes. Preserve HTML source snapshots as well as document bytes.
  • Write to a temporary object, verify, then atomically promote to raw/{source_id}/{sha256}. Never overwrite a prior source blob.
  • Record missing links and parse errors as first-class observations. A disappearing official file triggers review; it does not delete the published corpus.
source_observation
source_id, canonical_url, referring_url, discovered_at, fetched_at,
http_status, etag, last_modified, media_type, byte_length, sha256,
object_key, scraper_version, source_metadata, outcome, error_code
§4Extract
& recover

Use the cheapest faithful lane for each page

OCR is a fallback, not the default. Many legal PDFs already contain usable text, while some mix born-digital pages with scanned schedules or Gazette stamps. Routing is page-level so one bad page does not force OCR across an entire Act.

LaneDetectionProcessingAcceptance
E1Official HTMLDOM blocks retained with heading/list/table semanticsHeading sequence and text checksum stable after boilerplate removal
E2Born-digital PDFLayout-aware glyph/text extraction with coordinates≥95% printable characters; no missing-page or repeated-glyph anomaly
E3Mixed PDFE2 on good pages; render and OCR only failed pagesEvery page assigned a lane; page order preserved
E4Scanned PDF300 DPI render, deskew, denoise, script-aware OCR; English and Urdu/Sindhi models selected per regionLegal-token checks plus human review below threshold
E5Image/table scheduleRegion detection; cell grid and row/column recovery; source image retainedTotals, headers and row counts reconcile or route to curation

4.1Never destroy the page evidence

The canonical output is not a plain text file. Each block carries {page, bbox, reading_order, script, extractor, confidence}; every provision stores page anchors back to the immutable source. Hyphen repair, ligature expansion and whitespace normalization create derived text while the exact extracted form remains available for audit.

No translation in ingestion. English, Urdu and Sindhi publications are separate official expressions linked by instrument identity. Generated translation belongs to the explanation layer and must never replace statutory wording.

§5Legal
structure

Parse the law, not arbitrary token windows

5.1Numbering grammar

Parse headings and labels with a jurisdiction-aware grammar: section 3, 3-A, 3AA, dotted labels such as 10.3.3, whitespace-padded forms such as 6 . 2 ., (1), (a), (i), provisos, explanations, illustrations, schedules, forms, appendices, annexures and CPC-style Orders. Decimal rates, tariff codes, years and amendment-footnote citations are explicit negative cases. Indentation and coordinates are evidence, not truth; numbering, punctuation, font changes and table-of-contents reconciliation vote together.

5.2The printed contents list as source evidence

Preserve the contents list as an ordered relation, not a label-to-heading dictionary: repeated printed labels are real evidence and must not collapse. Every instrument_toc_entry stores the exact source block and physical PDF page, plus the provision it resolves to. Use it to locate the body boundary, repair only OCR-fused labels supported by the printed heading, score tree coverage, and create an explicit v_toc_gap worklist. A late contents page or an unmarked numeric run may be an index, schedule or table; it cannot move the body boundary unless the marker, page position and document-relative boundary tests agree.

5.3Chunking for RAG

  • Chunk only after the legal tree exists. Default boundary is a complete subsection or a group of adjacent clauses under one subsection.
  • Repeat compact context—instrument title, jurisdiction, section heading and defined-term scope—in chunk metadata, not by altering quoted text.
  • Never split a proviso, exception, explanation or definition from the rule it qualifies. Oversized schedules use row-aware chunks.
  • Each chunk retains ordered character spans into one provision version. Regeneration may change chunk IDs without changing citations or bookmarks.

& link

Extract candidates; require evidence before legal effect

CandidateDetected fromResolutionPublish rule

Models may propose classifications and spans. Deterministic resolvers verify the target, while a curator approves any candidate that can change legal status. Every accepted edge keeps the source page and exact words that support it.

§7Versioning
& identity

Never confuse a new file with a new law

IdentityKeyPurpose
Source observationsource_id + canonical_url + fetched_atProves what the portal exposed at a time

7.1Change classification

  • Mirror change: URL or filename changed but hash did not—link a new observation, do no extraction.
  • Presentation change: hash changed but normalized legal text did not—retain the new expression and page anchors; do not create a legal version.
  • Consolidation change: legal text changed on a code portal—diff at provision level and require an amending authority before publication.
  • New enactment or notification: create the publication event, resolve affected provisions and publish atomically only after gates pass.
  • Parser correction: transaction-time correction, not a claim that the law changed on that date.
§8Quality
gates

Nothing reaches retrieval because a script finished

GateCheckAutomatic thresholdFailure route
G1Source integrityOfficial registry match; successful fetch; valid MIME/header; hash and blob durableRetry or source review
G2Page completenessExpected page count equals processed pages; no empty internal page without image evidencePage OCR or curation
G3Text qualityPrintable/script ratios, legal-token dictionary and OCR confidence above lane thresholdAlternate extractor or OCR review
G4Structural integrityUnique ordered section labels; balanced hierarchy; contents reconciliationSide-by-side tree correction
G5Metadata identityJurisdiction, type, number/year or a documented historical exceptionLegal metadata review
G6Relationship integrityAll status-changing targets resolved; inverse edges and dates consistentLegal review
G7RegressionGolden documents, provision counts and known difficult pages unchanged or approvedBlock parser release
G8Publish transactionAll rows, versions, edges, chunks and audit record commit togetherRollback; live corpus unchanged

8.1Curation is an auditable patch

The curator sees the rendered source page and parsed tree together. Allowed operations are typed—split/merge block, relabel node, correct text with source span, resolve identity, accept/reject relationship. Each correction stores before, after, operator, timestamp, reason and page evidence. Re-running the same parser applies approved patches after extraction, so manual work survives rebuilds.

Sampling is risk-based: every OCR document, status-changing relationship, commencement/invalidation candidate and parser regression; a stratified sample of clean born-digital documents by source and era.

As built: the gates became thirty criteria

The gate table above states what must be true. Implementation turned each into a query with a named threshold, and adding the checks the corpus itself demanded took the set to thirty. They live in docs/CORPUS-CRITERIA.md and run against the candidate as ./nz audit.

Measured on nizam_clean, 10 September 2026 — 4,595 documents, 63,047 pages, 128,636,469 characters. 29 of 30 criteria pass; only S7 remains open. The fail-closed scopes contain 4,594 documents and 3,720 legal expressions.
FamilyAsksState
C1–C8 completenessEvery file becomes a blob, every blob is read, every block is accounted for, every character reachable, no failure silentall PASS
A1–A9 accuracyCharacter recall and precision against an independent extractor, no invented provisions, contents/source-anchor agreement, the as-at query returns the corpusall PASS; one malformed source remains explicitly unverifiable and quarantined
S1–S10 structureNo orphans, no cross-instrument tree, unique paths, dense order, unambiguous sibling citations, exact patch replay, exact candidate itemization, exact real-provision ancestor closure, and no unresolved internal-instrument boundary9 PASS; S7 has 2,312 pending decisions in 406 observations
Q1–Q3 quality evidenceOCR, word order and text plausibility measured for every applicable document and accepted under the evidence policyall PASS; document release is 4,594/4,595

Four of these deserve naming because they did not exist as concepts when this document was written:

  • C4/C5 — every block accounted for, every character reachable. §5 says segmentation must not lose text. It did not say how that would be proved. provision_block gives every block a role, and the role unassigned is the defect counter: it must be 0. Before this existed, 18.6% of extracted characters were in no provision and nothing distinguished “correctly classified as apparatus” from “silently dropped”.
  • S7 — automatic decisions must be adjudicated. Migrations 0035–0037 keep every decision source-anchored and fail closed. Of 6,684 current canonical-expression candidates, 4,372 are adjudicated and 2,312 across 406 observations remain pending; aggregate-to-item mismatch is zero. All retained decisions came from one evidence-driven machine adjudicator and are not a substitute for human legal review. Parser /24 adds detached heading/body and explicit contents-layout proof. No text or alternative is deleted.
  • Residual structural class. Some PDFs split a numbered marginal heading and its same-number operative body into consecutive source blocks. Those pairs are preserved but remain blocked because they require a source-span-preserving merge and corrected tree revision, not an accept_non_citable decision. Compiled instruments and uncontained schedules remain separate legal-review classes.
  • S9 — acceleration must contain legal nodes only. provision_ancestor is checked against the exact recursive parent_id closure. Migration 0027 removed 1,563,444 synthetic jurisdiction/type/instrument path prefixes; the current closure is 1,208,678 self-and-real-ancestor rows with no missing, extra or stale rows.
  • S10 — one PDF may contain many laws. Migration 0040 gives every legal expression a stable ordinal, primary/embedded role and guarded source-block span. The Constitution appendices, Estacode, PEF sets and other reviewed compilations are now 131 active expression manifests across 11 observations. A full span-aware detector rerun and the persisted queue both report zero unresolved boundaries.
  • Release is narrower than active. Migration 0030 exposes independently passed source evidence through v_release_document, v_release_page and v_release_text_block. Migrations 0035–0040 add the legal release views and expression model, excluding pending S7 candidates, 109 identity-linked redundant trees and 1,988 unresolved entries promised by printed contents across 607 canonical expressions. The provenance-inclusive contents view retains 2,120 gaps. The current legal release contains 3,720 instruments and 300,137 provisions.

A gate that encodes a measurement is a tripwire, not a test. Two criteria were written as fixed counts and both failed on healthy data within a day: one compared landed observations to blobs with a hardcoded offset, the other capped unstructured documents at nine. Both now assert the rule — every landed hash has a blob and every blob has a source; every unstructured document has a recorded reason — and the count is reported rather than thresholded.

§9Operations

One historical build, then small deltas

JobCadenceScopeAlert
Legislature and Gazette watchDailyNew Acts, ordinances, rules, SROs and commencement noticesFeed stale >48 h; numbering gap; official copies disagree
Code-portal reconciliationWeeklyNew or changed consolidated statutes and rules across jurisdictionsUnexplained text change or source disappearance

9.1Idempotent job graph

discover(source_cursor)
  → fetch(observation)                 # no-op for 304 or known hash
  → extract(sha256, extractor_version) # cached by exact inputs
  → segment(extraction, grammar_version)
  → enrich(tree, resolver_version)
  → gate(candidate, gate_version)
  → curate?(failure package)
  → publish(candidate_set)             # single L1 → L2 boundary

Every stage is content-addressed and retryable. Queues provide work delivery, not truth; the durable stage record decides whether work has already succeeded. A dead-letter item names its source, stage, attempt count and stable error code.

§10Delivery
plan

Build in the order that removes legal risk

PhaseDeliverableExit condition
1Harden existing five adaptersUnified manifest, immutable blobs, respectful fetch policy and source-level completeness report for all 4,710 local PDFs
2Extraction and legal treeAll pages assigned a lane; provision tree and page spans; G1–G5 pass; difficult-document golden set locked
3Legislature + Gazette deltasNew enactments discovered daily; assent/publication/commencement recorded; code changes reconciled to authority
4Supreme, FSC and High CourtsJudgments linked to provisions with explicit court hierarchy and review for invalidation/status edges
5GB and AJKSeparate jurisdiction identities, completeness reports and client coverage labels
6Demand-led regulatorsEach instrument resolves to enabling law; draft/final/superseded status verified

10.1Definition of done for Document 02

  • A complete rebuild from immutable blobs and versioned code produces the same published corpus hash.
  • No user request reads or parses a PDF; production serves only published L2 records.
  • Every displayed quotation resolves to official URL, content hash, page and source span.
  • Every source has a currency and completeness status visible to operations and expressible to users.
  • A failed or partial ingest cannot change the live corpus.
  • Unknown commencement or judicial status is represented as unknown, never guessed from silence.
ROfficial
sources

References

Only issuing-government, legislature, court and regulator sites are used below. Access and page structure were checked on 28 August 2026; adapters must treat URLs and markup as changeable.

  1. Federal statutes: Pakistan Code; National Assembly—Acts of Parliament; Senate—Acts. The Senate index records Act number, assent date and Gazette-publication date.
  2. Gazette: Printing Corporation of Pakistan, whose official domain publishes Gazette PDFs.
  3. Provincial codes and legislatures: Punjab Code, Punjab Assembly, Sindh Laws, Sindh Assembly, KP Code, KP Assembly, Balochistan Code, and Balochistan Assembly.
  4. Other territories: Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly—Acts; AJK Legislative Assembly—Acts.
  5. Superior courts: Supreme Court judgments, Federal Shariat Court, Lahore High Court, Sindh High Court, Peshawar High Court, Balochistan High Court, and Islamabad High Court judgments.
  6. Delegated and sector law: FBR SROs, SECP laws, SBP laws and regulations, PPRA regulations, ECP legal matters, and Competition Commission rules.
  7. Local measurements: 4,710 PDFs, 1,857 MB source data, approximately 243 MB extracted text and 113,158 top-level sections; measured from the five local archives on 28 August 2026. Detailed method: Document 03a §1.

Part 03 — Data and Storage

03Layer L2

Data and Storage

The schema that makes temporal correctness a database property, the indexes that make retrieval fast, and the single transaction that is the only way law enters the live corpus.

Version 1.0Layer L2Provides ICorpusWrite · ICorpusRead · IIndexSearch · ILexicalSearchFigures 3
↑ Contents
§1Extensions
& types

What the database must provide

Four extensions, each earning its place by making something structurally impossible rather than merely convenient. Any host that cannot supply them changes what this layer can guarantee, which is why the substitution is modelled rather than hidden.

ExtensionUsed forIf unavailable
vector (pgvector)Binary-quantised embeddings and HNSW indexes over themNo dense retrieval. There is no substitute; this one is non-negotiable
pg_search (ParadeDB)True BM25 with length normalisation over provision and paragraph textFall back to tsvector + GIN behind ILexicalSearch (§6). Ranking quality drops by a measured amount
ltreeProvision tree paths; subtree and ancestor queries without recursive joinsRecursive CTEs over parent_id. Correct but materially slower on deep trees
btree_gistThe exclusion constraint that makes overlapping validity intervals impossibleApplication-enforced temporal integrity, which is to say no integrity at all. This is the reason SQLite was rejected as a server engine
pg_trgmFuzzy matching for romanised Urdu aliases and misspelled act titlesExact matching only; Roman Urdu recall drops
 
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;       -- pgvector
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_search;    -- ParadeDB BM25; shared_preload_libraries below PG17
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS ltree;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;   -- required by the EXCLUDE constraint in 2.3
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- asserted by a migration; the build fails loudly rather than drifting
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF current_setting('server_version_num')::int < 170000 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'PostgreSQL 17 or newer required';
  END IF;
  IF (SELECT datcollate FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database())
     <> 'en_US.UTF-8' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'collation mismatch: index ordering would differ from the build host';
  END IF;
END $$;

1.1Enumerated domains

CREATE TYPE jurisdiction     AS ENUM ('fed','punjab','sindh','kp','balochistan','ict','ajk','gb');
CREATE TYPE instrument_kind  AS ENUM ('constitution','act','ordinance','order','regulation',
                                        'rules','sro','notification');
CREATE TYPE provision_kind   AS ENUM ('part','chapter','section','article','subsection','clause',
                                        'proviso','explanation','illustration','schedule','preamble',
                                        'form','appendix','annexure','order');
CREATE TYPE lifecycle_state  AS ENUM ('in_force','repealed','spent','lapsed','not_yet_commenced');
CREATE TYPE version_op       AS ENUM ('original','inserted','substituted','omitted','amended');
CREATE TYPE court            AS ENUM ('SC','FSC','LHC','SHC','PHC','BHC','IHC');
CREATE TYPE treatment        AS ENUM ('cites','applies','interprets','follows',
                                        'distinguishes','doubts','overrules');
CREATE TYPE disposition      AS ENUM ('allowed','dismissed','partly_allowed','remanded','disposed');
CREATE TYPE publish_scope    AS ENUM ('core','federal','provincial','judgments','all');

publish_scope is the mechanism behind ADR-1e. Every instrument carries one, and the live index contains only the scopes a deployment has enabled — which is how the same schema and the same migrations serve a 248 MB free-tier demo and a 10 GB pilot.

§2Core
schema

The legal core

2.1Instrument

CREATE TABLE instrument (
  id                  uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  jurisdiction        jurisdiction    NOT NULL,
  kind                instrument_kind NOT NULL,
  number              text            NOT NULL,   -- "XLV", "12", "745(I)"
  year                smallint        NOT NULL,
  short_title         text            NOT NULL,
  long_title          text,
  preamble            text,
  enacted_on          date,
  commenced_on        date,
  gazette_ref         text,
  status              lifecycle_state NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_force',
  repealed_on         date,
  repealed_by_id      uuid REFERENCES instrument(id),
  scope               publish_scope   NOT NULL,       -- ADR-1e
  published           boolean         NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  source_sha256       char(64)        NOT NULL,
  source_url          text            NOT NULL,
  extraction_conf     real,
  created_at          timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT uq_instrument UNIQUE (jurisdiction, kind, number, year),
  CONSTRAINT ck_repeal CHECK ((status = 'repealed') = (repealed_on IS NOT NULL))
);

source_sha256 is not decoration: it is how the ~48 duplicate documents measured in the federal corpus are detected, and how a re-scrape proves a source has genuinely changed before an ingest run is triggered.

2.2Provision — the citable unit

CREATE TABLE provision (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  instrument_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES instrument(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  parent_id     uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  path          ltree NOT NULL,        -- fed.act.1860_45.ch_XVI.s_302.cl_c
  kind          provision_kind NOT NULL,
  label         text NOT NULL,         -- "302", "337A", "(c)", "Proviso" — verbatim
  heading       text,
  marginal_note text,
  ordinal       integer NOT NULL,      -- sort order within the parent
  CONSTRAINT uq_provision_path UNIQUE (path)
);

-- ON DELETE CASCADE on both foreign keys is the composition in the domain model:
-- a provision cannot outlive its instrument, a child cannot outlive its parent.

2.3Provision version — where temporal correctness is enforced

CREATE TABLE provision_version (
  id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  provision_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  validity           daterange NOT NULL,   -- '[1860-10-06,2005-01-01)' ; upper NULL = in force
  text_en            text,
  text_ur            text,
  text_normalised    text NOT NULL,
  operation          version_op NOT NULL DEFAULT 'original',
  amended_by_id      uuid REFERENCES instrument(id),
  amendment_note     text,                -- "Subs. by Act XLIII of 2016, s.3" — verbatim footnote
  extraction_conf    real,
  verified_by        text,
  verified_at        timestamptz,

  CONSTRAINT no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (
    provision_id WITH =,
    validity     WITH &&
  )
);

The four lines that carry INV-5

That exclusion constraint makes two overlapping validity intervals for the same provision impossible to insert. A buggy amendment resolver fails loudly at commit rather than quietly producing a corpus where section 302 has two simultaneous texts and a point-in-time query returns whichever the planner reached first. It is the single most important line in this schema, and it is the reason SQLite — which has no EXCLUDE constraint — was rejected as a server engine despite matching the mobile pack.

2.4Amendment events and cross-references

CREATE TABLE amendment_event (
  id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  amending_instrument_id uuid REFERENCES instrument(id),
  target_provision_id    uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  operation              version_op NOT NULL,
  footnote_marker        text,          -- the superscript digit as printed
  raw_note               text NOT NULL,  -- unparsed, always retained
  effective_on           date,
  resolved               boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  resolution_error       text
);

CREATE TABLE provision_xref (
  src_provision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst_provision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  raw_text         text NOT NULL,        -- "under section 304"
  PRIMARY KEY (src_provision_id, dst_provision_id, raw_text)
);

raw_note is retained unparsed forever. When the amendment grammar improves, every unresolved event can be reprocessed without re-reading a single PDF — and resolved = false rows are a queue, not a failure.

2.5Judgments

CREATE TABLE judgment (
  id                uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  court             court NOT NULL,
  bench             text[],
  judges            text[],
  decided_on        date NOT NULL,
  case_no           text NOT NULL,
  neutral_citation  text,
  reporter_refs     text[],            -- "PLD 2016 SC 1" as an identifier only
  parties_raw       text,
  parties_redacted  text,
  disposition       disposition,
  subject_tags      text[],
  source_sha256     char(64) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id, decided_on)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (decided_on);

CREATE TABLE judgment_paragraph (
  id          uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  judgment_id uuid NOT NULL,
  decided_on  date NOT NULL,       -- carried down so the partition key is local
  para_no     integer NOT NULL,
  role        text,                  -- facts | arguments | reasoning | holding | order
  text        text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id, decided_on)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (decided_on);

CREATE TABLE citation_edge (
  id               uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  src_paragraph_id uuid NOT NULL,
  dst_provision_id uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst_judgment_id  uuid,
  treatment        treatment NOT NULL,
  confidence       real NOT NULL,
  method           text NOT NULL,   -- grammar | model | human
  quoted_span      int4range,
  verified_by      text,
  CONSTRAINT ck_one_dst CHECK (
    (dst_provision_id IS NOT NULL)::int + (dst_judgment_id IS NOT NULL)::int = 1)
);
§2ACorpus
layer

The tables below the legal core

§2 begins at instrument. Everything that produces one — the bytes, the extraction, the evidence that the extraction was faithful — is specified in document 02 and was not given a schema here. It has one now, and it is more than half the database. The authoritative dump is docs/SCHEMA.md, read from pg_catalog; this section states the shape and the reason for each rung.

The identity ladder (doc 02 §7)

source_observation   what a portal exposed, when          observation identity
      ↓ sha256
blob                 bytes                                 byte identity
      ↓ sha256
document — page — text_block                          one extraction of those bytes
      ↓ source_observation_id
instrument                                                 the legal expression
      ↓ instrument_id
provision ← provision_block                              INV-4, the citable unit
      ↓
provision_version                                          INV-5, law as at a date

Accounting and evidence

Tables added during implementation, each to make a correctness claim checkable rather than asserted.
TableWhat it holdsThe claim it makes provable
provision_blockevery text block, its role, and the provision it becameNothing is discarded. Roles are body, contents, preface, preamble, heading, footnote, running_header, schedule_row, unstructured, unassigned. unassigned must be 0 — it is the defect counter.
instrument_toc_entrythe statute’s ordered printed contents list, its exact source block/physical page, and the resolved provisionSegmentation is validated against the document’s own words; repeated printed labels survive, and an unresolved entry is a named gap rather than a hidden count.
extraction_attempt, segmentation_run, acquisition_attemptevery attempt, successful or not, with its reasonFailures are never silent. Ledgers are append-only and never pruned.
extraction_verificationper-document metrics against an independent extractorFidelity is evidence with a row behind it, not a corpus mean.
block_assignment_setwhich segmentation run produced which block rolesRe-segmentation retires an assignment set; it does not overwrite one.
segmentation_curation_patchsource page, stable locator, exact before/after text, evidence and review stateA PDF-verified correction changes only derived parser input, applies exactly once or fails closed, and never mutates extracted text.
segmentation_structural_candidateone immutable repeated-label decision with candidate/canonical provisions, source blocks, physical pages and parser evidenceS7 is item-level and reconstructable; an aggregate counter can no longer hide a missing decision.
segmentation_structural_adjudicationappend-only machine, source or human resolutions with method, rationale, evidence and supersessionStructural uncertainty can be reviewed without editing source text or destroying rejected interpretations.
revision_archive_batch, instrument_revision_archive_manifestdump path/hash, restore proof and a row-level map from each pruned revision to its retained successorSuperseded derived trees leave the hot database only after recoverability is demonstrated; source evidence remains in place.
provision_ancestorone row per provision and real parent_id ancestorQuery acceleration only. Disposable, regenerable, not source evidence — synthetic path-identity prefixes are excluded.

Correction to §4: the ltree GiST index does not work at corpus scale. §4 lists a GiST index on provision.path for “subtree and ancestor queries without recursive joins”. Once the corpus became append-only, retired revisions legitimately repeat their paths, and the duplicate-heavy history made the index pathological: writes first exceeded max_stack_depth, and with the ceiling raised they wedged the database mid-run.

It is replaced by provision_ancestor, an explicit ancestor closure answered by ordinary B-tree equality. Migration 0027 corrected its extent: closure is generated recursively from real parent_id edges, not from the three synthetic ltree labels that identify an observation. This removed 1,563,444 unreachable rows without touching canonical data. provision.path remains ltree and remains the canonical, immutable lineage; exact historical lookup is covered by uq_provision_instrument_path. Migrations 0017, 0018 and 0027.

Correction to §6: the write path is retire-and-append, not delete-and-rebuild. §6 describes one materialisation per document replaced in a transaction. Migration 0012 made document, instrument and block_assignment_set revision-bearing: is_active, supersedes_*_id, retired_at, verification_state. A re-run retires the previous revision and appends a new one, so a regression is diagnosable rather than lost.

Every current-state view and every audit query must therefore filter is_active. A query that reads the base tables directly counts every generation ever produced — which is a real defect this project shipped once and caught in review.

Active is still not the publication boundary. It means the newest evidentiary revision and deliberately includes quarantined material. Migrations 0030 and 0035–0040 require passed source evidence, canonical identity, complete printed contents, no pending S7 candidate, and no unresolved multi-instrument boundary. On 10 September 2026 the legal views contain 3,720 instruments, 300,137 provisions and 285,156 versions. Production retrieval must use these views; reviewers retain every active revision and archived proof of safely pruned superseded derived trees.

One observation can materialise several expressions. Migration 0040 replaces the old one-instrument-per-observation assumption with uniqueness on (source_observation_id, expression_ordinal). Each expression stores a guarded first/last source block and a versioned instrument_expression_manifest; one active assignment set still accounts for every source block exactly once. save_many() retires and appends the whole expression set atomically, so a partial split cannot publish.

Instruments are keyed on source_observation_id, not document_id: the same Act published on a federal and a provincial portal is two official observations of one work, and doc 03b §3 requires both to remain separately segmentable until identity resolution is reviewed.

§3Chunks
& vectors

Chunks store offsets, not text

A chunk is an index artefact with no independent existence. Storing its text would duplicate the entire corpus — 158 MB at statutory scale, 2 GB with judgments — for nothing, since the provision text is already stored and already indexed.

CREATE TABLE chunk (
  id             bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  version_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES provision_version(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  seq            smallint NOT NULL,
  char_start     integer NOT NULL,     -- offsets into provision_version.text_normalised
  char_end       integer NOT NULL,
  context_prefix text NOT NULL,        -- act short title + chapter heading, ~80 chars
  embedding      bit(1024) NOT NULL,   -- binary-quantised; 136 bytes on disk
  CONSTRAINT ck_span CHECK (char_end > char_start),
  CONSTRAINT uq_chunk UNIQUE (version_id, seq)
);

Why bit(1024) is a column and not an expression index

pgvector’s documented binary-quantisation pattern keeps the full-precision vector in the table and indexes binary_quantize(embedding)::bit(n) as an expression, so the table still pays 4,104 bytes per row and only the index shrinks. We store the bits directly instead — 136 bytes per row — and do not retain the full-precision vector at all.

That is only safe because we never rescore inside the database. Precision is recovered one stage later by the cross-encoder, which reads the provision text, not any embedding. A system without a reranking stage could not make this trade; ours was built with one as the gate. The consequence for storage is 21.5 MB of chunk rows instead of 649 MB at full statutory scale.

Re-embedding is therefore a full rebuild of chunk rather than an in-place update — which is correct, because a new embedding model produces a differently-shaped space and mixing two generations in one index would be silently wrong. The rebuild is a TRUNCATE plus a batch pass, and it never touches provision_version.

3.1Glossary, definitions and the answer tier

CREATE TABLE glossary_concept (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  concept       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  terms_en      text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  terms_ur      text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  terms_roman   text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',   -- talaq, talak, tallaq …
  provision_ids uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

CREATE TABLE stored_answer (                    -- the offline answer tier, doc 08 §3.4
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  canonical_question text NOT NULL,
  question_embedding bit(1024) NOT NULL,
  jurisdiction      jurisdiction NOT NULL,
  blocks            jsonb NOT NULL,           -- [{text, cites:[provision_id], span}]
  cited_provisions  uuid[] NOT NULL,          -- drives INVALIDATE on amendment
  corpus_version    bigint NOT NULL,
  verifier_score    real NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT ck_verified CHECK (verifier_score >= 0.97)
);

The check constraint is the point: an answer that did not clear the entailment threshold cannot be inserted into the shippable set. And cited_provisions is what makes invalidation mechanical — a publish that amends any provision emits a delete for every stored answer depending on it, in the same transaction.

§4Indexes

Every index, and the stage it serves

-- lexical: BM25 where available
CREATE INDEX ix_provision_bm25 ON provision_version
  USING bm25 (id, text_normalised) WITH (key_field='id');

-- lexical: the portable fallback, indexed as an expression (not a stored column)
CREATE INDEX ix_provision_fts ON provision_version
  USING gin (to_tsvector('english', text_normalised));

-- dense: HNSW over the bit column
CREATE INDEX ix_chunk_hnsw ON chunk
  USING hnsw (embedding bit_hamming_ops) WITH (m=16, ef_construction=64);

-- tree
CREATE INDEX ix_provision_path ON provision USING gist (path);
CREATE INDEX ix_provision_instr ON provision (instrument_id, ordinal);

-- temporal: the EXCLUDE constraint already created a gist index; this covers the common read
CREATE INDEX ix_version_lookup ON provision_version (provision_id, validity);

-- graph
CREATE INDEX ix_xref_src ON provision_xref (src_provision_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_xref_dst ON provision_xref (dst_provision_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_edge_dst_provision ON citation_edge (dst_provision_id, treatment);

-- roman urdu
CREATE INDEX ix_glossary_roman ON glossary_concept USING gin (terms_roman);
CREATE INDEX ix_glossary_trgm  ON glossary_concept USING gin (concept gin_trgm_ops);

4.1The two queries that must be fast

-- point-in-time provision read. Every client read goes through this shape.
SELECT p.path, p.label, p.heading, v.text_en, v.validity, i.status
FROM provision p
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = p.instrument_id AND i.published
JOIN provision_version v ON v.provision_id = p.id
                          AND v.validity @> $as_of::date      -- gist, INV-5
WHERE p.path <@ $subtree::ltree                            -- gist
ORDER BY p.path;

-- dense candidates with over-fetch, jurisdiction- and time-filtered
SELECT c.version_id, c.char_start, c.char_end
FROM chunk c
JOIN provision_version v ON v.id = c.version_id AND v.validity @> $as_of::date
JOIN provision p ON p.id = v.provision_id
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = p.instrument_id
                  AND i.published AND i.jurisdiction = ANY($juris)
ORDER BY c.embedding <~> $qbits::bit(1024)                 -- hamming, hnsw
LIMIT 500;                                                -- 10x over-fetch for 50 kept

As-built release correction: the conceptual queries above use published, but the current implementation has stronger evidence boundaries. Chunk creation and application reads must start from v_release_provision_version joined to v_release_provision and v_release_instrument; base-table active rows include retained S7 uncertainty. The second query filters and orders by an index, which is exactly the shape that used to over-filter in pgvector before iterative index scans landed. Verify the plan uses the HNSW index rather than falling back to a sequential scan whenever the jurisdiction filter is narrow — and raise hnsw.ef_search per session rather than globally.

§5Lexical
port

ILexicalSearch — two implementations, one benchmark

This is the seam that keeps the hosting decision reversible. No managed Postgres permits pg_search, so the fallback must exist, must work, and must have a measured quality cost rather than an assumed one.

class LexicalSearch(Protocol):
    def search(q: str, filters: Filters, k: int) -> list[Candidate]: ...

# implementation A — ParadeDB, true BM25 with length normalisation
SELECT id, paradedb.score(id) AS score
FROM provision_version
WHERE id @@@ paradedb.match('text_normalised', $q)
ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT $k;

# implementation B — portable, ts_rank_cd
SELECT id, ts_rank_cd(to_tsvector('english', text_normalised),
                        websearch_to_tsquery('english', $q), 32) AS score
FROM provision_version
WHERE to_tsvector('english', text_normalised) @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', $q)
ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT $k;
-- normalisation flag 32 divides by (rank + 1); the closest ts_rank_cd gets to
-- BM25 length normalisation, and still materially different on long provisions
The benchmark is a required deliverable, not an optional experiment. Run it once on the local pg_search baseline before any managed host is considered.
PropertyA — pg_searchB — ts_rank_cd
Length normalisationProper BM25 b parameterApproximated by a division flag. Our provisions range from one line to three pages, so this matters
Term saturationBM25 k1None — term frequency accumulates linearly
Phrase and proximityNative, with slop<-> operators; workable, clumsier
Index size~121 MB~121 MB
Available on managed hostsNoYes
Measured NDCG@10 deltaTo be filled from the golden set. Report it in the thesis whichever way it falls — a small delta justifies the managed path, a large one justifies self-hosting
§6Publish

The only write path into the live corpus

CREATE SEQUENCE corpus_version_seq;

-- scope gating (ADR-1e): the live view a deployment actually serves
CREATE VIEW live_provision AS
SELECT p.* FROM provision p
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = p.instrument_id
WHERE i.published
  AND i.scope = ANY(current_setting('nzq.enabled_scopes')::publish_scope[]);

-- a 500 MB free-tier deployment sets:  nzq.enabled_scopes = '{core,federal}'
-- a full pilot sets:                   nzq.enabled_scopes = '{core,federal,provincial,judgments}'
§7Partitions

Judgments are partitioned; statutes are not

-- yearly partitions from 2010; everything older in one catch-all
CREATE TABLE judgment_p_pre2010 PARTITION OF judgment
  FOR VALUES FROM (MINVALUE) TO ('2010-01-01');
CREATE TABLE judgment_p2015 PARTITION OF judgment
  FOR VALUES FROM ('2015-01-01') TO ('2016-01-01');
-- … created ahead of time by a scheduled job, never on demand

CREATE INDEX ON judgment_paragraph USING bm25 (id, text) WITH (key_field='id');
-- indexes declared on the parent propagate to every partition, existing and future
§8User data
& RLS

Operational tables

CREATE TABLE app_user (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  phone_e164   text UNIQUE,          -- phone-first; email optional
  email        text UNIQUE,
  tier         text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted_at   timestamptz            -- soft delete; the erasure job is separate
);

CREATE TABLE bookmark (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_user(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES provision(id),
  as_of        date,
  note         text,
  version      bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT nextval('user_version_seq'),  -- LWW key
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted      boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false                          -- tombstone
);

CREATE TABLE answer_audit (                -- INV-3: every answer replayable
  request_id     uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id        uuid REFERENCES app_user(id),   -- NULL in anonymous mode
  query_text     text,                            -- NULL in anonymous mode
  filters        jsonb NOT NULL,
  retrieved      jsonb NOT NULL,                -- provision ids with stage scores
  gate_decision  jsonb NOT NULL,
  prompt_sha256  char(64),
  model_version  text,
  verifier       jsonb,
  corpus_version bigint NOT NULL,
  created_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
) PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at);

8.1Row-level security

ALTER TABLE bookmark ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE bookmark FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;   -- applies to the table owner too

CREATE POLICY bookmark_owner ON bookmark
  USING (user_id = current_setting('nzq.user_id', true)::uuid)
  WITH CHECK (user_id = current_setting('nzq.user_id', true)::uuid);

-- the corpus is world-readable to the application role and writable only by the
-- publisher role; there is no policy that lets a user session write to it at all
REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON instrument, provision, provision_version,
                                  chunk, citation_edge FROM app_role;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_role;

FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY matters more than it looks: without it, policies are bypassed for the table owner, which is exactly the role a migration or a careless connection string is likely to use. And the corpus grants are the database-level expression of “there is no second write path” — the application role physically cannot publish.

8.2Sync, server side

-- corpus sync: one-way, signed. The client is never a writer.
SELECT patch_id, from_version, to_version, sha256, signature, url
FROM pack_patch
WHERE from_version >= $client_version AND tier = ANY($installed_tiers)
ORDER BY from_version;

-- user-data sync: bidirectional, last-writer-wins on a server-assigned version
SELECT * FROM bookmark
WHERE user_id = $uid AND version > $cursor
ORDER BY version LIMIT 500;                  -- tombstones included, filtered client-side

The cursor is the sequence value, never a timestamp. Device clocks are wrong often enough that a timestamp cursor silently loses writes, and the failure is invisible until a user notices a bookmark they deleted has returned.

§9Migrations
& recovery

Discipline

RuleWhy
Every object comes from a migrationADR-1g. A schema created in pgAdmin is reproducible nowhere, and the move from laptop to server stops being a restore
Migrations are reversible or explicitly irreversibleA downgrade that silently drops data is worse than no downgrade. Mark destructive steps and require a backup assertion before them
Index creation is CONCURRENTLY in productionA plain CREATE INDEX takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a 158k-row chunk table that is seconds; on judgment paragraphs it is an outage
Extension and collation asserted§1. Silent divergence in lc_collate changes index ordering and text comparison, and is genuinely hard to diagnose after the fact
Backfills are separate from schema changesA migration that rewrites 4.8M rows inside a transaction holds locks for the duration. Add the column, deploy, backfill in batches, then add the constraint
Re-embedding is a rebuild, never an updateTwo embedding generations in one index is silently wrong. TRUNCATE chunk, re-embed, rebuild HNSW

Recovery

  • pgBackRest to R2 — weekly full, daily incremental, continuous WAL archive, fourteen-day window. This is the point-in-time recovery that Supabase charges $100/month for.
  • Monthly restore drill into a scratch container, with the golden set run against the restored copy. A backup nobody has restored is a hypothesis.
  • The corpus is rebuildable from R2 blobs plus the scraper manifests plus the migrations, without any backup at all. That is the deepest safety property in the system: the database is derived data, and only user content is genuinely irreplaceable — which is also why user tables are tiny and easy to protect separately.
RSources

References

  1. pgvector binary quantisation — bit_hamming_ops, the expression-index pattern this document deliberately departs from, and the storage arithmetic (vector(n) = 4n+8 bytes; bit(n) = ⌈n/8⌉+8; 4,104 → 136 at 1024 dimensions). deepwiki.com/pgvector/pgvector
  2. pgvector HNSW tuning — parallel builds, iterative index scans for filtered queries, and the constraint that cluster-wide hnsw.ef_search requires ALTER SYSTEM plus pg_reload_conf(). nerdleveltech.com
  3. ParadeDB pg_search — BM25 over Tantivy; shared_preload_libraries requirement below PG 17; amd64 and arm64 packages; AGPL-3.0 Community edition. docs.paradedb.com
  4. Corpus measurements — 4,710 documents, 243 MB extracted text, 113,158 top-level sections, 4.17× compression; storage model and index footprints. Capacity plan §1–§2, measured 28 Aug 2026.

1.1You are right that these are not all the laws

What is on disk is the statutory backbone of five jurisdictions. What is missing is larger than what is present, and the largest missing piece is the one that matters most commercially.

MissingEst. textMultiple of currentConsequence for sizing
AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan statutes~25 MB0.1×Negligible. Two more scrapers on the existing skeleton.

Note the ratio: judgments are roughly twelve times the raw text of every statute in the country, and because they are chunked at paragraph level they generate about thirty times as many vectors. Any hosting decision that ignores them is a decision about the demo, not about the product.

1.2Two measured facts that shape the design

  • Legal text compresses 4.17× under gzip — measured on 21.5 MB of core statutes. It is highly repetitive prose, which is good news for the offline pack and for object storage, and only partly good news for Postgres, where compression applies to values above the TOAST threshold and most provisions sit just under it.
  • The average top-level section is ~1.9 KB of text, about 480 tokens. That is almost exactly one embedding chunk, which is why chunking at section level rather than at fixed token windows is both cheaper and more faithful to the citation model.
§2Storage
model

Where the bytes go

Raw text is the smallest part of a searchable corpus. Indexes, the provision tree, and vectors together outweigh it roughly three to one — which is why “243 MB of law” and “a 500 MB database” do not mean what they appear to mean.

Two modelling choices that save about 350 MB

Chunks store offsets, not text. A chunk row carries (provision_version_id, char_start, char_end) and derives its text on read. Storing chunk text separately would duplicate the entire corpus — about 158 MB at full scale — for no benefit, since the provision text is already indexed and served.

The tsvector column is not materialised. Indexing the expression rather than storing a generated column halves the full-text cost. It is slightly slower to build and identical to query.

§2AAs
built

What it actually cost

The model in §2 was written before a single row existed. The corpus has now been built and repeatedly revised against source evidence. Superseded derived trees have been archive-first compacted, while source evidence, active trees and proof manifests remain; this forensic build must still not be confused with a compact release export.

Measured on nizam_clean, 10 September 2026: 4,595 active documents, 63,047 pages, 128,636,469 extracted characters. Statutory corpus plus retained derived revision history and evidence — no chunks, vectors or case law.

Tree expansion, sections → nodes3.2×4.83×106,021 sections yield 512,094 active provisions after compilation appendices became separate legal expressions. Clauses, subsections, forms, Orders and preserved schedule/table rows nest deeper than assumed.
provision row210 B232 Bclose

Evidence structures the original model did not contain

Most of the gap is not underestimation. It is tables that did not exist when §2 was written, each added to satisfy a correctness requirement:

TableRowsTotal sizeWhy it exists
provision_ancestor1,208,678431 MBThe B-tree closure stores only self plus real active parent_id ancestors. Disposable and exactly checked by S9.
provision_block1,046,209172 MBEvery retained tree assigns every source block a role, so loss is a query rather than a claim.
instrument_toc_entry87,05437 MBOrdered printed contents evidence for active trees and retained proof endpoints, including exact source block/page.
segmentation_structural_candidate7,2395.8 MBImmutable item-level parser decisions tied to source pages; retired evidence is embedded in archive manifests.
segmentation_structural_adjudication4,4986.0 MBAppend-only independent decisions for retained trees; no uncertainty is erased to make a counter pass.
instrument_identity_resolution110128 kB+Exact full-tree fingerprints link redundant legal expressions while preserving every source observation.
instrument_expression_manifest142small131 active and 11 retired source-block boundary maps preserve multi-expression provenance.
instrument_revision_archive_manifest15,98960 MBHashes, counts and embedded structural evidence preserve proof for compacted superseded derived revisions.

Append-only revisions need a hot-retention boundary. Migration 0012 correctly made re-extraction and re-segmentation retire-and-append so regressions remain diagnosable. Once those revisions had immutable archive manifests and a restore-tested snapshot, superseded derived trees were safely compacted. After migration 0040 materialised compilation expressions, another isolated restore test exposed and fixed ordinal-matching and manifest-reference defects before exactly 20 additional retired trees were archived and pruned. Source PDFs, observations, documents, blocks, OCR evidence, expression manifests and active trees were not deleted. The live database now has 4,797 instrument rows: 4,788 active and nine retired identity-resolution endpoints that must remain for exact proof.

Practically: the live build database is 1,682 MB after post-prune vacuum/analyze. Its 204,509,189-byte dump was restored and signature-checked after parser /24, migrations through 0041, multi-expression materialisation and archive-first compaction. A later serving export may be smaller, but must retain source evidence and use only fail-closed release views.

The compacted forensic build is below 2 GB before retrieval indexes, operational headroom and future revisions. That is not enough margin for a production 2 GB tier; size lexical/vector indexes against the release subset before choosing hosting. The Supabase 500 MB free tier remains suitable only for a deliberately scoped subset, never this complete build database.
