Three free-tier facts that bite before storage does

  • The PDFs do not fit anywhere free except R2. 1,857 MB of source documents against a 1 GB Supabase Storage allowance. Cloudflare R2 gives 10 GB with zero egress fees, so blobs go to R2 regardless of which database you choose. That decision is independent and already made.
  • Idle pausing breaks demos. A Supabase free project sleeps after roughly a week of inactivity, which is exactly the cadence of an academic supervisor checking in. Budget for a keep-alive ping or accept a cold first request.
  • No managed host permits ParadeDB. Every managed row above loses real BM25. That is why ILexicalSearch exists in document 01 — the fallback is a tsvector implementation whose ranking delta gets measured on the golden set rather than assumed away.
§4The
unlock

Binary vectors cost us almost nothing

Vectors are the component that decides whether a corpus fits. At full precision they are the largest single line in the model; quantised to bits they are the smallest. The reason we can take that trade without paying for it is already in the architecture.

The measurement that must accompany this. Binary quantisation is a recall trade, and recall is measurable. Before it ships, run the golden set at full precision, at halfvec(384) and at bit(1024), and report Recall@50 and end-to-end NDCG@10 for each. If binary costs more than two points of NDCG after reranking, fall back to halfvec(384) and accept the smaller corpus scope. That ablation belongs in the thesis regardless of the outcome.

§5Hosting
ladder

Four stages, one schema

You asked whether to build locally or on a free tier. The answer is both, in that order — and the reason it is safe to plan it that way is that corpus scope is a deployment parameter, not a schema decision. The same migrations run at every rung.

5.1Stage-by-stage decisions

StageDoDo not
0 — LocalBuild the entire ingestion pipeline, all seven QA gates, the curation console, and retrieval against the full 4,710-document corpus. Run pg_search so the BM25 baseline is real. Back up to R2 from day one.Do not develop against a 500 MB ceiling. Ingestion is the phase that most needs headroom, and a paused free project mid-run wastes a day.
1 — Free tierPublish federal statutes only. Bind the tsvector implementation and measure the ranking delta against your local pg_search baseline — that number is a thesis result. Use the hosted auth.Do not try to squeeze all five jurisdictions in. Scope 3 at 744 MB does not fit, and the contortions needed to force it would damage the schema.
2 — Self-hostedMove when judgments land, or when a second jurisdiction does. Restore from the R2 backup, widen the published scope, rebind pg_search. Run the restore drill before you need it.Do not conflate this with needing Kubernetes. One node, Docker Compose, pgBackRest to R2.
3 — ScaleVertical first. Partition judgment_paragraph by court and year when the index no longer fits in memory.Do not shard early. At 10 GB a single node is comfortable; the corpus is read-mostly and the write path is a nightly batch.

5.2Supabase Pro or your own node, at full scale

Once every feature is on and every corpus is loaded — statutes, judgments, the citation graph, bitemporal versions, RAG end to end — the comparison stops being about the database and becomes about the whole system. The decisive fact is one most comparisons miss.

“Every feature” means the full architecture: BM25 plus dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, entailment verification, bitemporal law, the citation graph, the document factory and batch answer generation.

The recommendation, and the honest counterweight

Own node, running the self-hosted Supabase stack on top of it if you want that developer surface. A custom Postgres image gives you Studio, GoTrue and PostgREST and pg_search — the ergonomics without the lock-out, on the same €65 box.

Supabase Pro is still the right answer if nobody on the team is willing to be paged, if the FYP timeline cannot absorb learning pgBackRest and monitoring, or if you need a compliance posture you can point at rather than one you operate. Those are real reasons, and $300 a month is a defensible price for not being on call. They are just not architectural reasons — and the architecture should not be shaped around them, which is why ILexicalSearch exists.

5.3Building the whole thing locally first

Yes, and it is the right sequence. A full-scale production database — every statute, every judgment, every embedding, every index — fits on a laptop, and the build is measured in hours rather than days.

Throughput figures for an 8-core laptop with an int8 ONNX encoder and eight parallel parse workers. GPU figures assume a rented consumer card at roughly $0.30/hour.
ResourceStatutes onlyStatutes + judgmentsNotes
Database on disk~750 MB~10 GBFrom the model in §2
Source documents on disk1.9 GB~40 GBJudgment sources dominate; keep them on an external drive if space is tight
Free disk needed~15 GB~100 GBIncludes WAL, backups and staging
RAM8 GB workable16 GB workable, 32 comfortableThe index working set is what wants memory, not the build
PDF parse and segment~15 min~2 hours8 workers; embarrassingly parallel and fully resumable

HNSW index build~2 min~45 minBinary vectors build fast; raise maintenance_work_mem first
Full corpus, cold start to queryableunder 30 minone overnight run

pgAdmin4 is a fine viewer and a terrible source of truth

Use pgAdmin4, DBeaver or DataGrip to browse, query and inspect — all good. But if the schema exists only because someone clicked it into being in a local session, it cannot be reproduced on the server, and the move to production becomes a manual re-do with silent drift. Two rules make the local build genuinely portable:

  • The schema is migrations in git. Alembic, sqitch, or numbered SQL files — the tool matters far less than the rule. Every index, extension, constraint and role is created by a migration that runs identically anywhere.
  • The engine is a pinned Docker image. The same image runs on the laptop and on the server, so extension versions cannot diverge. Build it once from postgres:17 plus pgvector, pg_search and ltree, and pin the digest.

Parity checklist before you move anywhere

  • Postgres major version pinned and identical — a restore across major versions needs a dump, not a physical copy.
  • Extension versions pinned in the image and asserted by a migration that fails loudly on mismatch.
  • Locale and collation identical. A different lc_collate silently changes index ordering and text comparison, and it is a genuinely nasty class of bug.
  • The golden-set evaluation runs green on the target before traffic moves. If NDCG@10 shifts, the lexical implementation changed and you now know by how much.
  • A restore drill completed on the target from the R2 repository, with the evaluation suite run against the restored copy.
§6Offline
sizing

What fits in the phone

Same measurement, applied to the device. The question there is not a free-tier ceiling but a data-cost and storage ceiling — and it lands on a base experience of roughly 135 MB installed, which is reasonable on the phones our users own.

Derived from the measured corpus. Download figures assume zstd on the SQLite file; the encoder in the semantic tier is already compressed and dominates that row.
TierContentsDownloadOn diskDefault?
ApplicationFlutter binary, no pack bundled25 MB25 MBYes

Two things worth noticing. First, the semantic tier is mostly the encoder, not the vectors — 25 MB of model against 7 MB of index — which is exactly why it is an optional tier rather than a default, and why the answer tier that depends on it is offered alongside it. Second, the answer tier is the cheapest capability in the whole product: 12 MB of download buys grounded, cited, pre-verified answers to the head of the query distribution, working with no network and no model on the device.

The offline quality ladder, stated honestly

  • Statutory lookup and browse — identical to online. The pack is signed and authoritative.
  • Lexical search — identical to online where the online host is also on tsvector; slightly weaker than a pg_search baseline.
  • Semantic search — measurably weaker: 384-dim on device against 1024-dim on the server, with no cross-encoder. Labelled “offline search” in the UI.
  • Grounded answers — identical to online for questions the answer tier covers, unavailable otherwise. Never approximated.
  • Precedent, drafting, novel questions — unavailable, and the UI says so rather than degrading quietly.

7.1Answering the question directly

How much space do the laws take?243 MB of raw text for the 4,710 documents on disk; 58 MB compressed; 1,857 MB as source PDFs. In a searchable Postgres with vectors and full-text indexes, 744 MB with binary quantisation.
Can Supabase free hold it?Not all of it. It holds federal statutes comfortably — 248 MB against a 500 MB ceiling — with RAG fully built: vectors, full-text, provision tree, cross-references, users and audit. It cannot hold all five jurisdictions, and it is nowhere near case law.
Is there a better free option?For scope, Oracle Cloud Always Free — ~200 GB and your own Postgres with pg_search, at the cost of operating it and accepting capacity risk. For convenience, Supabase. Aiven’s 1 GB fits all statutes if you want managed and complete.
Should we build locally first?Yes. Ingest and gate the full corpus on a local Postgres with every extension available, then publish a scoped subset upward. Developing against a 500 MB ceiling would distort exactly the decisions that are hardest to reverse.
Does the phone stay reasonable?135 MB installed for app, core statutes, semantic search and pre-verified offline answers. The full statutory corpus is a 400 MB opt-in that most users will never need.

Part 03b — Legal Data Model

03bAnnex to 03

Legal Data Model

What actually connects to what in Pakistani law, the facets that classify it, and the schema — in Postgres and in SQLite — that turns both into retrieval the model cannot get wrong.

Version 1.0Engines Postgres 17 · SQLiteEdge types 14Facets 9Figures 4
↑ Contents
§1Linkage
model

Law is a graph with typed edges

A generic document store treats a statute as text with a title. A legal database has to treat it as a node in a graph where the edge type carries legal meaning — because “notwithstanding section 5” and “subject to section 5” point at the same provision and mean opposite things.

1.1The fourteen edge types

“RAG use” states what the edge does at retrieval time. Expand pulls extra context; Guard prevents a wrong answer; Rank reorders.
EdgeLegal meaningRAG use
containsStructural parent to childExpand Never return a clause without its section; never a proviso without what it qualifies
amendsInstrument closes one version and opens anotherGuard Selects the right text for as_of; surfaces the amendment chain
repealsInstrument ends the life of anotherGuard Repealed law is never operative for a present-day question
savesA repeal that preserves rights accrued, or proceedings begun, under the old lawGuard The reason a repealed act can still be the correct answer. Without this edge, repeal looks total when it is not
commencesA notification brings a section into force, often years after enactment and section by sectionGuard An enacted but uncommenced section is not law yet
empowersA section authorises rules, regulations or an SRO to be made under itExpand The highest-value edge. The Act says “as prescribed”; the prescription lives in delegated legislation. Retrieving one without the other returns half an answer
definesA term is given a meaning, scoped to an act, a part or a single sectionExpand Definitions inject deterministically when a retrieved provision uses a defined term
defaults_fromGeneral interpretation statutes supply meanings not displaced by the specific actExpand Fallback when a term is used but not locally defined
notwithstandingNon-obstante: this provision prevails over the one namedRank Order conflicting provisions correctly and flag the conflict rather than silently picking one
subject_toThis provision yields to the one namedRank The inverse. Both must be retrieved together or the answer inverts
refers_toA plain internal or external cross-referenceExpand Graph expansion at stage 1 of retrieval
interpreted_byJudicial treatment: applies, distinguishes, doubts, overrulesExpand The citator, and evidence that a reading is still good law
invalidated_byA superior court has struck down or declared a provision of no effectGuard A struck-down provision still appears in the printed statute. Serving it as operative is the worst failure available
attractsLinks a provision to a structured schedule row — offence attributes, court fee, stamp duty, limitation periodGuard Answered by SQL, exactly, with no model in the path

As-built structural release boundary

Migration 0035 makes parser uncertainty a first-class legal-model fact. Migration 0036 makes corrective decisions fail closed and records exact identity evidence. Migration 0037 blocks a tree while its printed contents promises an unresolved provision. Migration 0038 records source-evidenced internal boundaries; migration 0040 materialises each reviewed primary or embedded legal expression with a stable ordinal and immutable source-block span. Application graph reads use the release views. On 10 September 2026 this publishes 3,720 instruments and 300,137 provisions while retaining all 2,312 unresolved S7 decisions and 1,988 canonical contents gaps for review; S10 is clear.

Why empowers deserves special attention

Pakistani statutes delegate constantly: an act sets a framework and says the fee, the form, the time limit or the procedure shall be “as prescribed” or “as may be notified”. The operative number then lives in Rules or an SRO that may have been amended a dozen times since.

A retrieval system that returns only the parent Act gives a confidently incomplete answer — and it will read as authoritative because the Act is authoritative. Modelling the empowers edge means the assembler can always ask: does this section delegate, and if so is the current delegated instrument in the context? If it delegates and the delegated instrument is missing from the corpus, that is a stated gap, not a silent one.

§2Faceted
taxonomy

Categorise on nine axes, not one

Every legal database that fails does so by choosing a single category tree. Law does not have one. An instrument sits somewhere on every axis simultaneously and independently — and each axis is a different retrieval filter serving a different question.

2.1What each facet is for

FacetCardinalityQuery it answersWhere the values come from
subject_matter1–3“Show me tenancy law” · narrows dense retrieval before rankingSeeded from the Pakistan Code’s own categories, then extended. Assigned by rule where the short title is decisive, by classifier otherwise, human-reviewed
instrument_type1“Only primary legislation” · distinguishes an Act from the SRO made under itDeterministic from the source
jurisdiction1The hardest filter in the system. Punjab tenancy law is not Sindh tenancy law, and returning the wrong province is a wrong answerDeterministic from the source
competence1Whether a provincial enactment can validly cover a subject at all — and what the 18th Amendment movedConstitution’s legislative lists, curated once
doctrinal_role1–3“What are my rights” wants substantive; “how do I file” wants procedural. Routes intent to the right corpus sliceRule plus review
legal_origin1–2Explains interpretive tradition; flags where Federal Shariat Court jurisdiction is liveCurated by era and subject
life_stage1Every read. An instrument may be enacted, commenced, repealed, spent, lapsed or invalidated, and only one of those is operativeDerived from the temporal model in document 03
citizen_situation0–4The bridge from “my landlord locked me out” to the Specific Relief Act. See §5Hand-curated. The most valuable and most labour-intensive facet
forum0–3Which court or tribunal hears a matter — drives the forum finder and filters precedent by court seniorityFrom the act’s own jurisdiction clauses

Facets apply at two levels, and that matters

Most facets attach to the instrument — jurisdiction, type, competence, origin. But subject_matter, doctrinal_role and citizen_situation also attach at provision level, because a single act is rarely homogeneous: the Pakistan Penal Code is penal throughout, but the Companies Act contains substantive, procedural and penal provisions in the same chapter. Filtering at instrument granularity when the query is about a section throws away precision the corpus already has.

§3Pakistan-
specific

Constructs a generic legal schema will miss

These are the places where importing a design built for another jurisdiction produces a database that is subtly, confidently wrong about Pakistani law.

ConstructWhy it breaks a naive modelSchema response
Section-level commencement Many acts commence “on such date as the Government may by notification appoint” — and different sections can be appointed on different dates, sometimes years apart. An instrument-level commenced_on is therefore not enough commencement rows keyed to provision, with the notification that appointed the date. A provision with no commencement row and an act with none is enacted but not in force
Territorial extent, which changes “Extends to the whole of Pakistan except…” is a live, temporal attribute, not boilerplate. The 2018 merger of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa changed where a large body of law applies extent as a temporal relation: instrument × territory × validity range. Retrieval filters on it exactly as it filters on as_of
Repeal with savings A repealing act commonly preserves rights accrued, liabilities incurred, and proceedings begun under the repealed law. Treating repeal as deletion makes the system wrong about every matter that started before it The saves edge, pointing from the repealing provision to what it preserves, with the text of the savings clause. Repealed law stays queryable and is returned with its savings clause attached
Federal Shariat Court repugnancy Under Article 203-D the Court may declare a provision repugnant to the Injunctions of Islam, with effect from a stated date unless amended before it. The provision remains printed in the statute book while ceasing to have effect A distinct life_stage value and an invalidated_by edge carrying the declaring judgment, the effective date, and whether the declaration is under appeal. Never inferable from the statute text alone
Ultra vires declarations A superior court can strike down a provision as beyond legislative competence or unconstitutional. The printed text does not change Same edge, different ground. Both are guards on every read
Post-18th-Amendment competence The abolition of the Concurrent Legislative List in 2010 devolved subjects to the provinces. Federal acts on devolved subjects may continue until replaced — so both a federal and a provincial act can appear valid for the same subject competence facet plus a superseded_by relation across jurisdictions. When both surface, present both with their status rather than silently choosing
Default definitions General interpretation statutes supply meanings to every enactment unless the specific act displaces them. A term used but not defined locally is not undefined The defaults_from edge, resolved only after a local definition lookup misses. Scope order: section → part → act → general
Non-obstante precedence “Notwithstanding” and “subject to” encode which provision prevails. Flattened into an untyped link, the answer to a conflict is lost Two directed edge types with opposite polarity, used at ranking time to order and to flag
Bilingual authenticity Where an Urdu text exists, which language version governs is a legal question, not a presentation choice authentic_language on the instrument. The client shows the authentic text verbatim and labels the other as translation — never the reverse

The two edges that cannot be extracted from statute text

invalidated_by and commences both live outside the document they modify — one in a judgment, one in a gazette notification. No amount of parsing the Act will find them, which means a corpus built only from statute PDFs will confidently serve provisions that a court has struck down or that never came into force.

Practically: until the judgment and gazette pipelines land, those two facets carry a coverage flag and the UI states that invalidation status is not yet tracked. An unknown that is declared is a limitation; an unknown that is hidden is a defect.

§4Schedules
as tables

The schedules are already tables — store them as tables

Several of the most-asked legal questions in Pakistan are answered by a schedule that is literally printed as a grid. Parsed into rows, they turn a retrieval-plus-generation problem into a SELECT — exact, instant, free, and impossible to hallucinate.

Printed containers are not interchangeable. The implemented grammar retains schedule, form, appendix, annexure and order as distinct provision kinds; CPC Rules remain children of their printed Orders. A container may later own a normalized cell table, but its source blocks, printed label, page range and citation lineage remain canonical. Repeated numbers are never flattened into schedule rows merely to remove a collision: unresolved cases stay in the S7 queue.

Estimated row counts. Each of these is a bounded, one-time data-entry task with permanent value, and each removes a class of question from the model entirely.
Source scheduleRowsAnswers, exactlyWhy the model must not do it
CrPC Schedule II — offence attributes~300 Is this offence cognizable? Bailable? Compoundable? Which court tries it? Can the police arrest without warrant? These are the questions with the most direct consequences for a person’s liberty, and the answer is a grid cell. Generating it is indefensible when reading it is trivial
Limitation Act 1908 — Schedule~180 How long do I have to file? From what date does the clock run? Missing a limitation period is one of the most common and most irreversible self-representation errors. A near-miss answer is worse than none
Court Fees Act 1870 — Schedules I & II~110
× province		 What will it cost to file this suit at this value? Arithmetic over a rate table, per province, versioned by amendment date
Stamp Act 1899 — Schedule I~65
× province		 What stamp duty does this instrument attract? Drives the document factory’s duty computation. Provincial amendments diverge sharply
Civil courts pecuniary limits~40 Which civil court has jurisdiction at this suit value, in this district? The forum finder. Wrong forum means a plaint returned and time lost 
CREATE TABLE offence_attribute (            -- CrPC Schedule II, one row per offence
  provision_id   uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES provision(id),
  cognizable     boolean NOT NULL,
  warrant        boolean NOT NULL,          -- arrest without warrant permitted?
  bailable       boolean NOT NULL,
  compoundable   text NOT NULL,             -- none | by_victim | with_court_permission
  triable_by     text NOT NULL,             -- magistrate class, sessions, special court
  punish_min     interval, punish_max interval,
  fine_note      text,
  validity       daterange NOT NULL,       -- the Schedule is itself amended
  source_note    text NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE limitation_article (
  id             uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  article_no     text NOT NULL,
  description    text NOT NULL,             -- "for possession of immoveable property…"
  period         interval NOT NULL,
  runs_from      text NOT NULL,             -- the trigger event, verbatim from the Schedule
  jurisdiction   jurisdiction NOT NULL,
  validity       daterange NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE provision_limitation (         -- the "attracts" edge, made concrete
  provision_id   uuid REFERENCES provision(id),
  article_id     uuid REFERENCES limitation_article(id),
  confidence     real NOT NULL,
  verified_by    text,
  PRIMARY KEY (provision_id, article_id)
);

The rule that makes these safe

Every row carries validity and source_note. Schedules are amended like anything else, and a fee table without a validity range will silently answer 2019 questions with 2026 rates. And the calculator surfaces the article it applied, its period, and its trigger — so a user or an advocate can check the reasoning rather than trusting a number.

These tables are expert-entered and expert-verified, never model-extracted. The value here is exactness; a 97%-accurate limitation table is not 97% as good as a correct one, it is a liability.

§5Situation
bridge

The citizen taxonomy is a separate artifact

A doctrinal taxonomy serves lawyers. It does not help someone who types مالک مکان نے تالا لگا دیا or malik makan ne tala laga diya. The bridge between lived situations and legal provisions is hand-built, and it is the single highest-leverage data asset in the product.

CREATE TABLE situation (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  slug         text NOT NULL UNIQUE,        -- eviction_without_process
  title_en     text NOT NULL,               -- "Locked out by a landlord"
  title_ur     text NOT NULL,
  summary_en   text, summary_ur text,
  facet_situation text NOT NULL,            -- housing | work | family | money | crime …
  urgency      text                            -- has_deadline | time_sensitive | routine
);

CREATE TABLE situation_alias (               -- how people actually say it
  situation_id uuid REFERENCES situation(id),
  phrase       text NOT NULL,
  script       text NOT NULL,               -- latin | arabic | roman_urdu
  PRIMARY KEY (situation_id, phrase)
);

CREATE TABLE situation_provision (
  situation_id uuid REFERENCES situation(id),
  provision_id uuid REFERENCES provision(id),
  jurisdiction jurisdiction NOT NULL,       -- the same situation maps differently per province
  role         text NOT NULL,               -- primary | supporting | penal | procedural | remedy
  note         text,
  verified_by  text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (situation_id, provision_id, jurisdiction)
);
One worked example. role is what makes this more than a tag list — it tells the assembler what each provision is for.
SituationRoleProvisionWhy it belongs
eviction_without_process
Punjab		primarySpecific Relief Act 1877, s.9The direct remedy: recover possession without proving title
remedyLimitation Act 1908, the article governing s.9 suitsShort and unforgiving. Surfacing the deadline is more urgent than explaining the right
supportingPunjab Rented Premises Act 2009 — grounds and procedureThe provincial framework that governs the tenancy itself
penalPakistan Penal Code, criminal trespassA parallel criminal route the citizen would not know exists
proceduralRent tribunal constitution and filing procedureWhere to go, in what form

Roughly 200 situations covers the overwhelming majority of citizen need, and they are enumerable in advance: housing, unpaid wages, wrongful dismissal, divorce and khula, child custody, inheritance shares, property transfer and registration, refusal to register an FIR, bail, defective goods, dishonoured cheque, land encroachment, workplace harassment, domestic violence, succession certificates, nikah registration. Each takes an advocate perhaps twenty minutes to map and review.

§6Postgres
schema

Linkage and facets in Postgres

These tables sit alongside the core schema in document 03. One edge table with a typed discriminator, one facet table per level, and the temporal relations that the naive model gets wrong.

CREATE TYPE edge_kind AS ENUM (
  'contains','amends','repeals','saves','commences','empowers','defines',
  'defaults_from','notwithstanding','subject_to','refers_to',
  'interpreted_by','invalidated_by','attracts');

CREATE TABLE legal_edge (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  kind         edge_kind NOT NULL,
  src_provision uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  src_instrument uuid REFERENCES instrument(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst_provision uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst_instrument uuid REFERENCES instrument(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst_judgment  uuid,
  dst_schedule  uuid,
  validity     daterange NOT NULL DEFAULT '(,)',   -- edges are temporal too
  raw_text     text,                              -- the clause that created the edge
  confidence   real NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
  method       text NOT NULL,                    -- grammar | model | human
  verified_by  text,
  CONSTRAINT ck_one_src CHECK (num_nonnulls(src_provision, src_instrument) = 1),
  CONSTRAINT ck_one_dst CHECK (
    num_nonnulls(dst_provision, dst_instrument, dst_judgment, dst_schedule) = 1)
);

CREATE INDEX ix_edge_out ON legal_edge (src_provision, kind);
CREATE INDEX ix_edge_in  ON legal_edge (dst_provision, kind);
CREATE INDEX ix_edge_kind ON legal_edge (kind) WHERE kind IN
  ('invalidated_by','repeals','commences');   -- partial: the guards are read on every query

6.1Facets and the temporal relations

CREATE TABLE instrument_facet (
  instrument_id uuid REFERENCES instrument(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  facet         text NOT NULL,       -- subject_matter | doctrinal_role | legal_origin …
  value         text NOT NULL,
  taxonomy_ver  integer NOT NULL,    -- see §8; a value means nothing without its version
  method        text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (instrument_id, facet, value)
);

CREATE TABLE provision_facet (       -- three facets also apply at provision level
  provision_id uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  facet        text NOT NULL CHECK (facet IN
                 ('subject_matter','doctrinal_role','citizen_situation')),
  value        text NOT NULL,
  taxonomy_ver integer NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (provision_id, facet, value)
);

CREATE TABLE commencement (           -- section-level, and often years after enactment
  provision_id     uuid REFERENCES provision(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  commenced_on     date NOT NULL,
  by_instrument_id uuid REFERENCES instrument(id),   -- the appointing notification
  PRIMARY KEY (provision_id)
);

CREATE TABLE extent (                 -- where an instrument applies, and when it changed
  instrument_id uuid REFERENCES instrument(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  territory     text NOT NULL,
  included      boolean NOT NULL,     -- "except the Tribal Areas" is an exclusion row
  validity      daterange NOT NULL,
  source_note   text NOT NULL,
  EXCLUDE USING gist (instrument_id WITH =, territory WITH =, validity WITH &&)
);

6.2The guard, as one query

-- every read passes through this. It is a view so it cannot be forgotten.
CREATE VIEW operative_provision AS
SELECT p.*, v.text_en, v.validity
FROM provision p
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = p.instrument_id AND i.published
JOIN provision_version v ON v.provision_id = p.id
WHERE v.validity @> current_setting('nzq.as_of')::date
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM commencement c
              WHERE c.provision_id = p.id
                AND c.commenced_on <= current_setting('nzq.as_of')::date)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM legal_edge e
                  WHERE e.dst_provision = p.id
                    AND e.kind = 'invalidated_by'
                    AND e.validity @> current_setting('nzq.as_of')::date)
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM extent x
              WHERE x.instrument_id = i.id AND x.included
                AND x.territory = current_setting('nzq.territory')
                AND x.validity @> current_setting('nzq.as_of')::date);

Retrieval reads operative_provision, never provision. A provision that is repealed, uncommenced, judicially invalidated, or not in force in the user’s territory cannot appear in a result set — not because the retrieval code remembered to filter, but because the only view it is granted access to has already done so.

§7SQLite
projection

The pack is a projection, not a second design

Same identities, same semantics, fewer enforcement mechanisms — because the invariants were enforced upstream by the engine that has them. The pack is read-only and server-built, which is what makes that safe.

-- pack schema, abridged. Same identities as the server; no uuid type, so TEXT.

CREATE TABLE provision (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  instrument_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES instrument(id),
  path          TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'fed/act/1860_45/ch_XVI/s_302/cl_c'
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN('section','clause','proviso', …)),
  label         TEXT NOT NULL, heading TEXT, ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL,
  -- facets denormalised onto the row: the device does no analytics
  subject       TEXT, doctrinal TEXT, situation TEXT,
  -- guard columns precomputed at build time; the device never recomputes them
  in_force      INTEGER NOT NULL,       -- already accounts for repeal, commencement,
  invalidated   INTEGER NOT NULL        -- invalidation and extent, at pack build date
);
CREATE INDEX ix_prov_path ON provision(path);        -- prefix LIKE uses this
CREATE INDEX ix_prov_instr ON provision(instrument_id, ordinal);

CREATE TABLE provision_text (
  provision_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES provision(id),
  valid_from   TEXT NOT NULL,           -- ISO-8601; sorts and compares as text
  valid_to     TEXT,                    -- NULL = current
  text_en      TEXT, text_ur TEXT
);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE fts USING fts5(
  text_en, text_ur, heading,
  content='',                          -- contentless: no second copy of the corpus
  tokenize="unicode61 remove_diacritics 2"
);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE vec USING vec0(       -- optional semantic tier only
  provision_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  embedding float[384]
);

CREATE TABLE legal_edge (               -- six kinds; the rest need judgments or gazettes
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN
    ('contains','defines','refers_to','empowers','attracts','saves')),
  src  TEXT NOT NULL, dst TEXT NOT NULL, note TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY(kind, src, dst)
) WITHOUT ROWID;

The guard columns are the whole trick

The server evaluates repeal, commencement, invalidation and territorial extent at pack build time and writes the answer into two integer columns. The device then does a single indexed comparison instead of four correlated subqueries against tables it does not carry.

The cost is that those columns are as at the pack build date, which is exactly why every offline provision view is stamped with the pack version. And it is why a patch that changes a provision’s status must rewrite these columns — the same invalidation discipline the answer tier already uses.

§8Governance

The taxonomy is versioned data, not configuration

Facet values will be wrong at first and will improve. If a stored value cannot be traced to the vocabulary version that produced it, every reclassification silently invalidates every measurement taken before it.

CREATE TABLE taxonomy_version (
  version     integer PRIMARY KEY,
  facet       text NOT NULL,
  values      jsonb NOT NULL,        -- the permitted vocabulary at this version
  released_on date NOT NULL,
  rationale   text NOT NULL
);
FacetOwnerAssignmentReview
jurisdiction, instrument_type, life_stageData engineerDeterministic from source or from the temporal modelCovered by the QA gates
subject_matter, doctrinal_roleData engineerRule where the short title decides; classifier otherwiseSpot-check 5% per release; disagreements go to the advocate reviewer
competence, legal_origin, extentAdvocate reviewerCurated once against the Constitution’s legislative listsRe-reviewed on constitutional amendment only
citizen_situationAdvocate reviewerHand-mapped. ~200 situations × jurisdictionEvery mapping signed off before it ships. This is the facet users feel
Schedule tables (§4)Advocate reviewerHand-entered from the printed scheduleDouble-entry: two people enter independently, rows are diffed
invalidated_by, commencesData engineerExtracted from judgments and gazettes once those pipelines existUntil then, coverage is flagged as incomplete in the UI

8.1What ships first

  1. Deterministic facets and the guard view — jurisdiction, type, life stage. They cost nothing and prevent the worst failures.
  2. The contains, refers_to and defines edges — extractable from the statute text we already have, and they carry most of the retrieval-expansion value.
  3. Schedule tables — bounded expert data entry, immediate exact answers, no model in the path.
  4. The situation taxonomy — roughly 70 advocate-hours for 200 situations, and the thing that makes citizen queries work at all.
  5. empowers — needs the SRO and Rules corpus, which is not yet scraped.
  6. invalidated_by and commences — need judgments and gazettes. Declared incomplete until then.

One honest limitation, stated up front

Until the judgment and gazette pipelines land, this model can tell a user what a provision says and whether it has been repealed by another statute — but not whether a court has struck it down, and not reliably whether it ever came into force. Those are real gaps with real consequences, and they belong in the interface as a coverage statement rather than in a backlog nobody reads.

Part 04 — Retrieval

04Layer L3

Retrieval

The evidence-selection contract between a versioned Pakistani legal corpus and grounded generation: exact when the law is named, hybrid when the issue is described, authority-aware always, and silent when the evidence is not sufficient.

Version 1.0Date 28 Aug 2026Layer L3Provides IRetrieveRequires IIndexSearch · ICorpusRead · IInferenceFigures 4
↑ Contents
§1Mandate
& boundary

Retrieval decides what the answer is allowed to know

L3 does not answer legal questions. It converts a question into a replayable, legally scoped evidence bundle or a typed abstention. L4 may reason only over that bundle; it may never search around the gate.

Inherited invariantL3 consequence
INV-1Citations are database renderings of stable provision or judgment identifiers. Model-generated citation strings are never accepted.
INV-2Every request exits as GroundingContext or Abstention; no caller can bypass the sufficiency gate.
INV-3Persist query interpretation, filters, corpus version, every candidate rank/score, fusion, rerank, gate version and final evidence IDs.
INV-4Chunks find law; provisions and judgment paragraphs cite law. Re-chunking cannot break a public citation.
INV-5as_of is mandatory, defaults to today, and applies before ranking to versions, territory, authority relations and treatment.

Current corpus boundary. Retrieval chunks and indexes are derived only from v_release_provision_version, joined through v_release_provision and v_release_instrument. As measured on 10 September 2026, that boundary contains 285,156 versions, 300,137 provisions and 3,720 instruments. Active base tables include 2,312 unresolved S7 decisions, identity-linked provenance duplicates and 1,988 canonical contents/body gaps; indexing them would bypass the corpus gate. Reviewed multi-instrument boundaries are materialised and S10 is zero.

Non-goals. L3 does not extract PDFs, publish sources, decide ultimate legal meaning, draft advice, or hide corpus gaps. Those belong to L1/L2, L4, or an explicit human review path.

1.1Ship gates inherited from Document 01

On the locked Pakistani test set: NDCG@10 ≥ 0.75, Recall@50 ≥ 0.90, MRR@10 ≥ 0.70, point-in-time correctness ≥ 0.95, Urdu–English NDCG gap ≤ 0.05, and abstention precision/recall ≥ 0.90 / 0.85. The direct-citation fast path remains below 50 ms; full retrieval fits the existing end-to-end p50/p95 budget of 1.5/4 seconds.

§2Query
contract

Parse deterministically before searching statistically

A legal query is not just text. It is text plus time, forum, territory, source class, cited identifiers and uncertainty. The parser preserves all of it and invents none of it.

type QuerySpec = {
  requestId: UUID; raw: string; normalized: string;
  language: "en" | "ur" | "roman-ur" | "mixed";
  intent: "citation" | "provision" | "issue" | "precedent" | "procedure";
  asOf: LocalDate; knowledgeAsOf: CorpusRevisionId; eventDates: LegalEventDate[];
  jurisdiction?: Jurisdiction; territory?: Territory; legislativeOrigin?: Jurisdiction;
  forum?: CourtId; authorityPerspective?: CourtId; sourceKinds: SourceKind[];
  citations: ParsedCitation[]; terms: TermVariant[];
  unresolved: Ambiguity[]; parserVersion: string;
}

2.1Normalization without evidence destruction

  • Apply Unicode NFC, whitespace and punctuation normalization; preserve the raw query and character map.
  • Normalize Urdu presentation forms and Urdu/Arabic digit variants for matching, never for display.
  • Roman Urdu produces versioned alias candidates from glossary_concept; it is not silently translated into English.
  • Expand known legal abbreviations and spelling variants as parallel terms. Never rewrite an Act, section, court or case number to the “nearest” identifier.
  • Detect explicit dates and phrases such as “in 2020” or “before amendment”; an explicit date overrides the default and is visible to the user.

asOf is the legal-effective date; knowledgeAsOf pins what the system knew for replay. An offence, transaction, accrual and filing may require different event dates, especially for savings and limitation. A date mentioned in narrative is not silently promoted to asOf. Territory, legislative origin, forum and the court from whose perspective authority is assessed are separate fields; guessing one from another is prohibited.

2.2Citation grammar

The grammar recognizes instrument title/number/year, article or section/subsection, rules, case number, neutral citation and reporter reference. A complete parse routes to exact resolution. A partial parse narrows candidates but cannot auto-select among collisions. Reporter references are identifiers only; the system retrieves official judgment text, not copyrighted reporter headnotes.

Ambiguity is data. “Section 9” without an Act, or “LHC 2022” without a case, yields structured choices or AMBIGUOUS_CITATION. Fuzzy matching may suggest; it may not resolve.

§3Routing
& policy

One public interface, two retrieval paths

IntentPrimary routeRequired completion check
Exact citationIdentifier resolver; no ANNOne published legal unit valid at as_of, or explicit ambiguity/not-found
Provision lookupLexical + dense + definitionsWinning provision expanded to its complete citable unit
Issue / scenarioAll four generators + rerankerGoverning rule, definitions, exceptions and enabling rules covered
PrecedentJudgment lexical/dense + citator graphAuthority and subsequent treatment known; official text available
Procedure / feesProvision + delegated instrumentsRules/schedules current for forum and date; otherwise abstain
§4Candidate
generation

Four independent ways to be found

Each generator receives the same hard-filtered universe and returns ranks, not supposedly comparable scores. Independence is deliberate: exact words, semantic paraphrase, defined terms and legal relationships fail differently.

4.1Lexical

Use ParadeDB BM25 behind ILexicalSearch, with fields for title, heading, provision label, body, citation tokens and case metadata. Phrase matches and exact section labels receive field boosts. Pin the extension version: current ParadeDB SQL is version-sensitive. PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd is a supported fallback, not “equivalent BM25”; flag 32 is rank/(rank+1), not length normalization. Benchmark the fallback independently. Use fixed expression indexes per script/configuration—english for English and simple plus normalized aliases for Urdu/Roman Urdu—because a single English dictionary silently damages recall.

4.2Dense

Embed the original multilingual query directly. HNSW over the inherited bit(1024) representation returns a broad pool; retain the 10× overfetch and rerank with the full-precision query/candidate representation where available. Start hnsw.ef_search at 100, then tune from measured recall. For selective filters, use pgvector iterative scans and an adaptive planner: exact search over a small prefiltered set; HNSW otherwise.

Required L2 correction. ANN predicates hidden behind joins may be applied after index traversal. Materialize a denormalized search_projection carrying legal-unit ID, jurisdiction, validity, publication/status, territory key and embedding on the indexed row. This is a migration owned by Document 03, not an excuse for L3 to post-filter invalid results. Judgment dense retrieval likewise requires a paragraph projection/embedding before the precedent phase can ship.

4.3Definitions and graph

The definition generator resolves English, Urdu and Roman aliases to concepts, then retrieves the definition provision and provisions inside its effective scope. The graph generator starts independently from explicit citation, forum, subject and controlled-term seeds; after fusion, a second deterministic completeness pass expands the winning units. It traverses an allow-list of typed edges—defines, subject_to, notwithstanding, empowers, amends, repeals, cites, followed, distinguished, overruled—for at most two hops. Every hop is time-filtered, direction-aware, and recorded. It expands evidence; it never manufactures relevance from an untyped co-occurrence.

4.4Contents-derived aliases and coverage

The statute’s printed contents list is a high-precision vocabulary source, not answer evidence. Build per-instrument aliases from resolved v_toc rows so a query containing the official marginal heading can recall the linked provision even when OCR or typography weakened its body heading. Exact citation resolution may use the printed label as a consistency check, and context assembly may use neighbouring resolved entries to detect a missing necessary unit. Never index the contents block as substantive body text, never quote it as the governing rule, and never auto-resolve an unmatched v_toc_gap; a gap lowers structural confidence and enters curation. Retrieval traces record whether a candidate came from a body match, a contents-derived alias, or both.

§5Fusion
& reranking

Fuse ranks, then teach relevance in-domain

// generator g ranks legal unit d at rank_g(d), starting at 1
rrf(d) = Σg contains d 1 / (60 + rankg(d))

// collapse multiple chunks without letting long provisions dominate
unitScore = max(chunkRrf) + 0.15 * secondBest(chunkRrf)
candidate = { unitId, bestSpan, generatorRanks, matchedTerms, graphPaths }

RRF is the default because the four score distributions are not calibrated to one another. The constant 60 follows the original formulation and becomes a tested configuration value, not a per-query knob. Keep at most two chunks per legal unit before collapse, cap any one instrument at 40% of the rerank slate, and reserve places for each generator that produced a credible result.

5.1Cross-encoder contract

  • Rerank 50 candidates using a small multilingual cross-encoder; input is query plus heading, hierarchical prefix and the minimal matched span.
  • Return a semantic relevance logit only. Authority, validity and publication are deterministic policy fields, not tokens the model is trusted to interpret.
  • Fine-tune on Pakistani lawyer relevance labels with hard negatives from the same Act, adjacent section, neighbouring jurisdiction, expired version, lower court and later adverse treatment.
  • Version model, tokenizer, prompt template and training-set digest. Calibrate separately for English, Urdu, Roman Urdu and mixed queries where sample size permits.

Cross-encoders are slower but stronger pair scorers, which is why they are a second stage rather than an index. BEIR also cautions against assuming a dense retriever generalizes: BM25 is a strong robust baseline and reranking tends to improve quality at a compute cost. Both findings justify this cascade, not a dense-only design.

§6Legal
correctness

Legal priority is a temporal relation, not a score boost

A semantically perfect passage from the wrong province, date, court or legal version is a wrong result. Those properties constrain eligibility and presentation before relevance is allowed to order anything.

SignalPolicyFailure output
Jurisdiction / territoryhard Include applicable federal law plus the selected territorial law; never substitute a neighbouring province.JURISDICTION_UNRESOLVED or explicit multi-jurisdiction comparison
Temporal validityhard Apply as_of to provisions, amendments, commencement, territory and authority/treatment relations.NO_VALID_VERSION; show known nearest dates only as metadata
Publication / sourcehard Only published, officially sourced text enters an answer bundle.SOURCE_UNVERIFIED
Court authoritymatrix Effective-dated binding relation by deciding court, subject-matter jurisdiction, receiving forum and decision date.FORUM_UNRESOLVED or label authorities without declaring one controlling
Treatmentstatus Overruled/reversed/invalidation edges change usability; followed/distinguished explain application.ADVERSE_TREATMENT_UNRESOLVED
Semantic relevancerank Orders eligible evidence; cannot restore an ineligible source.Low score contributes to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

6.1Effective-dated authority matrix

The current Constitution reflects the Twenty-Seventh Amendment (2025). Article 189 now gives decisions of the Federal Constitutional Court on questions/principles of law binding effect over all other courts, including the Supreme Court; Supreme Court decisions bind all other courts except the Federal Constitutional Court. Article 201 governs the binding effect of High Court decisions on subordinate courts, subject to Article 189. Federal Shariat Court decisions have their own constitutional channel. Therefore court enum + numeric rank is not legally adequate.

AuthorityRule {
  decidingCourtId; receivingForumId; subjectMatter;
  validFrom; validTo; effect: "binding" | "persuasive" | "outside-scope";
  constitutionalBasis; sourceVersionId;
}

// resolve as the law of authority stood on the research date
authority = matrix.resolve(decidingCourt, forum, subjectMatter, asOf)
assert authority.sourceVersionId is official and replayable

Architecture correction required. Documents 01 and 03 predate this change and their fixed court hierarchy/enum is stale. Add court, court_alias, court_jurisdiction and effective-dated authority_rule data before precedent retrieval ships. Until then, precedent mode must abstain from claims about binding status.

6.2Commencement, repeal and continuity

Temporal expansion implements the General Clauses Act, 1897 as structured rules, not prompt lore. Its sections 5 and 6 address commencement and the continuing effect of repeal; section 8 carries references through repeal and re-enactment; sections 20A and 21 govern Gazette publication and amendment/rescission of subordinate instruments; sections 22 and 24 cover pre-commencement rules and continuity after repeal/re-enactment. The assembler must fetch the relevant commencement, savings, amendment and delegated-instrument evidence before passing the gate.

6.3Conflict bundles

Do not collapse contrary authorities into one winner using recency or similarity. When eligible decisions conflict, return the leading proposition, contrary decisions, court/bench/date, treatment edges and the authority relation to the user’s forum. The generator must describe the conflict or abstain; it may not synthesize a nonexistent settled rule.

6.4Operative evidence versus historical discovery

Expose two typed modes. operative_evidence may pass the gate only when validity, territory and status permit reliance. historical_discovery may return repealed, superseded, not-yet-commenced or adversely treated material with a prominent status banner, but it cannot ground a statement of current law. Commencement is tri-state: confirmed_in_force, confirmed_not_in_force, or unknown_due_to_coverage. Missing gazette data is never coerced to “not commenced”; an issue requiring that fact abstains.

6.5Boundary with the citator

L3 retrieves official judgment paragraphs and stored treatment edges needed for evidence selection. L5 IPrecedent owns the final treatment classification and “good law” assessment. Until that service and the effective-dated authority data are available, L3 may report recorded treatment facts but must not label a case controlling, overruled or good law on inference alone.

§7Evidence
assembly

Retrieve narrow; assemble complete

Precise spans win retrieval, but legal meaning often depends on a proviso, definition, explanation, schedule or enabling rule outside the winning chunk. Context assembly repairs that boundary deterministically.

type EvidenceItem = {
  legalUnitId; sourceVersionId; sourceUrl; sourceSha256; sourcePages[]; official: true;
  displayCitation; text; matchedOffsets[]; asOf; knowledgeAsOf;
  jurisdiction; territory; authority?: AuthorityFinding;
  treatments[]; inclusionReason; retrievalTraceRef;
}
type GroundingContext = {
  query: QuerySpec; items: EvidenceItem[]; coverage: CoverageFinding;
  conflicts: ConflictSet[]; corpusVersion; retrievalRunId;
}

Choose context by marginal coverage: governing rule first, then a necessary definition/qualification/dependency, then corroborating authority. After reranking about 50 candidates, admit at most about 20 legal units to gate/assembly, subject to token budget and necessary-set coverage. Collapse duplicate quotations and overlapping spans. Order statutes in legal structure, not relevance-score order. A source earns space because it closes a named coverage gap, not because it is the sixth passage saying the same thing.

§8Gate &
abstention

Confidence is calibrated evidence sufficiency

The gate is a small, interpretable classifier over retrieval signals, followed by non-negotiable legal vetoes. Its threshold τ is fitted on a held-out, lawyer-labelled set for the target precision/recall; it is never hand-selected from a few demos and never lowered during degradation.

8.1Features and typed outcomes

Features include top reranker score and margin, generator agreement, exact citation resolution, necessary-set coverage, language/script, query ambiguity, authority resolution, source verification, treatment conflict and corpus coverage. Test calibration error and reliability by intent and language; use group-specific thresholds only with enough held-out examples, otherwise fall back to the conservative global threshold.

type Abstention = {
  code: "AMBIGUOUS_CITATION" | "JURISDICTION_UNRESOLVED" |
        "NO_VALID_VERSION" | "SOURCE_UNVERIFIED" | "FORUM_UNRESOLVED" |
        "ADVERSE_TREATMENT_UNRESOLVED" | "MISSING_DELEGATED_AUTHORITY" |
        "COMMENCEMENT_UNKNOWN" | "CORPUS_GAP" |
        "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE" | "RETRIEVAL_DEGRADED";
  publicReason; missing: Requirement[]; suggestions: Clarification[];
  confidence; threshold; retrievalRunId;
}

Abstention must be actionable: identify the missing jurisdiction/date/Act/forum or say that the official corpus lacks the material. Never say merely “I cannot answer,” and never fill the gap from model memory.

§9Runtime
& operations

Fast enough to be cautious

StageBudgetOperational rule
Parse / policy≤ 2 msCompiled citation grammar and in-memory alias automaton; DB confirms identifiers
Query embedding≤ 20 msVersion-keyed cache for normalized public queries; no cross-user private text cache
4 generators≤ 45 msParallel, same snapshot and filters; statement timeout per generator
Rerank 50≤ 60 msONNX int8, bounded batch; fewer candidates only by measured latency policy
Validate / assemble / gate≤ 25 msBatch fetch and graph lookup; no N+1 queries

9.1Adaptive vector execution

// count estimate comes from the denormalized, prefiltered search projection
if estimatedEligible <= EXACT_SCAN_LIMIT:
    exactHammingOrFloatScan(filters, query)       // deterministic recall
else:
    SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = tunedEf
    SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order
    hnswSearch(filters, query, overfetch = 10 * k)

shadowSample: compare approximate top-k with exact; alert on recall drift

pgvector recommends monitoring approximate recall against exact search. Run exact shadow queries on a small, stratified sample and report recall by jurisdiction/filter selectivity, not only globally. A fast national-average metric can hide a failing Balochistan or historical-date slice.

9.2Degradation

  • Embedder or HNSW unavailable: lexical + definition + graph path, marked lexical_only; normal gate threshold remains.
  • Reranker unavailable: RRF order with a separately calibrated degraded-mode gate; if that calibration has not shipped, abstain.
  • Graph incomplete: provision lookup may continue, but queries requiring definitions, delegated rules, treatment or authority fail the relevant coverage check.
  • Database snapshot changes mid-request: retry the whole retrieval once; never assemble across corpus versions.

9.3Audit and privacy

The retrieval trace stores normalized filters, candidate IDs and stage scores, graph paths, model/index versions, gate features/decision, latency and corpus version. Anonymous mode does not persist raw query text or user ID; use an ephemeral request digest for aggregation. Access logs never contain evidence text. Retention and erasure follow Document 03’s user-data policy while immutable public-corpus identifiers remain replayable.

9.4Offline is a labelled lower tier

The mobile pack uses FTS5 + glossary and may add sqlite-vec with the inherited 384-dimensional device encoder. It has no cross-encoder and is presented as “offline search,” not as quality-equivalent grounded research. Targets remain p95 ≤300 ms for FTS and ≤800 ms for vector search on a 4 GB Android device. Online and offline scores are never mixed or compared as if calibrated.

9.5Exact, versioned caching

A small process-local LRU may cache query embeddings and short-lived retrieval results. The key includes normalized query, language, sorted scopes, exact asOf, source/court filters, corpusVersion, taxonomy, embedding/reranker hashes, retrieval configuration and degradation mode. Do not add Redis for the single-VPS pilot, round dates, share results across full/degraded modes, or cache an inferred jurisdiction as if the user supplied it. Semantic answer caching belongs to Document 05.

§10Evaluation
& learning

A Pakistani legal benchmark is part of the product

There is no credible launch from generic English retrieval scores. The locked set must reflect Pakistani instruments, courts, amendments, scripts, provinces, ambiguity and genuine absence.

StratumRequired labelsPrimary metric / failure
Exact citationsCanonical unit, valid version, ambiguityMRR / exact resolution; false auto-resolution = critical
Issue questionsNecessary evidence set plus optional relevant setRecall@50, NDCG@10, necessary-set coverage
Temporal pairsSame question before/after amendmentPoint-in-time accuracy; any version leakage
Jurisdiction pairsSame issue across federal/provinces/territoriesWrong-jurisdiction rate = 0 on hard-filtered cases
PrecedentForum, subject, binding/persuasive, treatmentAuthority/treatment accuracy and conflict recall
Bilingual tripletsEquivalent English, Urdu, Roman Urdu questionsPaired NDCG gap, not translated-answer similarity
UnanswerableMissing source/date/place/forum, false premiseAbstention precision/recall and reason accuracy

10.1Annotation protocol

Two trained legal annotators independently mark the minimal sufficient spans, canonical citable units, required dependencies, temporal/jurisdiction scope and authority. A senior reviewer adjudicates disagreement. Preserve alternate relevant authorities instead of forcing a single-document gold label. LegalBench-RAG’s span-level emphasis is useful, but its contracts domain is not a substitute for this jurisdiction-specific set.

10.2Mandatory ablations

  • BM25 alone, dense alone, BM25+dense, +definitions, +graph, +cross-encoder.
  • Float32 vs halfvec(384) vs bit(1024); binary ships only if reranked NDCG loss is no more than two points and Recall@50 clears target.
  • HNSW vs exact by filter-selectivity bucket; current vs historical dates; each jurisdiction.
  • Direct multilingual retrieval vs any proposed translation hop. Direct remains unless paired evaluation proves otherwise and citation-token fidelity is unchanged.
  • Gate reliability curves and expected calibration error by intent/language, plus selective accuracy as coverage falls.

10.3Adversarial fixtures that must stay green

FixtureFailure prevented
“Tenant law” with no territoryGuessing a province; require clarification or explicitly scoped comparison
Conduct before amendment; proceeding after itApplying present text retrospectively or omitting savings
Parent Act says “as prescribed” but rules are absentInventing the decisive fee, form, condition or procedure
Rules under a repealed and re-enacted ActDiscarding a still-continuing instrument or retaining an inconsistent one
Pre-/post-2025 constitutional precedent pairApplying today’s FCC/SC authority relation to the wrong period
Matching language appears only in a dissentTreating a non-majority proposition as binding ratio
No adverse edge in incomplete judgment coverageClaiming “good law” from absence of evidence
Later curator correction to an old provisionReplay failure when legal asOf is stored without corpus revision

10.4Feedback without contamination

Lawyer judgments enter a reviewed relevance-label queue, never the live index directly. Split by legal issue/instrument family before training to prevent near-duplicate leakage. Promote a model only on the untouched locked set; run the prior model as baseline and publish deltas by stratum. A click is navigation telemetry, not proof of legal relevance.

§11Delivery
contract

Implementation order and acceptance

PhaseDeliverableCannot advance until
R0QuerySpec, citation grammar, exact provision path, traces100% golden citation resolution or typed ambiguity; INV-3 replay proven
R1Statute BM25 + dense + RRF + provision assemblyRecall/NDCG/temporal/jurisdiction targets pass
R2Definitions, typed graph expansion, calibrated gateNecessary-set coverage and abstention targets pass
R3Cross-encoder and bilingual/Roman Urdu tuningPaired bilingual gap and latency budget pass
R4Precedent retrieval and citatorOfficial judgment projection plus effective-dated court/authority schema exists

11.1Port shape

interface IRetrieve {
  retrieve(query: QuerySpec, options: RetrievalOptions):
    Promise<GroundingContext | Abstention>;
}

interface IIndexSearch {
  lexical(q, filters, limit): RankedCandidate[];
  dense(embedding, filters, limit, searchPlan): RankedCandidate[];
  definitions(terms, filters, limit): RankedCandidate[];
  graph(seeds, edgeAllowList, filters, limit): RankedCandidate[];
}

11.2Definition of done

  • No path can call generation without a passing bundle; contract test proves the boundary.
  • Every displayed citation resolves to an official stored source and exact citable unit.
  • Replay reconstructs the same candidate ranks from pinned corpus/index/model versions.
  • All quality targets pass overall and by declared jurisdiction/language strata; critical legal-filter errors are zero in the locked set.
  • Load test meets the existing latency/cost budget with cold-cache and degraded-mode runs.
  • Known schema dependencies—search projection, judgment embeddings and authority matrix—are migrated before their modes are enabled.
RPrimary
sources

References

  1. Constitution of Pakistan, consolidated text — Articles 189 and 201 and the current constitutional court structure. National Assembly of Pakistan, amended through 21 Nov 2025. Official PDF.
  2. Constitution (Twenty-Seventh Amendment) Act, 2025 — source amendment creating the Federal Constitutional Court and substituting the binding-precedent provisions. National Assembly of Pakistan. Official Gazette PDF.
  3. The Judicial System of Pakistan — official institutional overview and court structure; historical descriptions must be read subject to later constitutional amendments. Supreme Court of Pakistan. Official PDF.
  4. General Clauses Act, 1897 — commencement, effect of repeal, re-enacted references, Gazette publication and continuity/amendment of subordinate instruments. Pakistan Code, Ministry of Law and Justice. Official PDF.
  5. pgvector — HNSW filtering, iterative scans, binary quantization, reranking and exact-search recall monitoring. Official repository.
  6. PostgreSQL 17 full-text search controls — query constructors, ts_rank/ts_rank_cd and normalization flag semantics. Official documentation.
  7. ParadeDB full-text search and filtering — BM25 indexing, tokenizer/filter configuration and predicate pushdown. Official overview; filtering.
  8. Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods — Cormack, Clarke & Büttcher, SIGIR 2009; original RRF method and constant. Author-hosted paper.
  9. Sentence Transformers CrossEncoder training — second-stage reranking architecture and evaluation workflow. Official documentation.
  10. BEIR — Thakur et al., 2021; heterogeneous evaluation showing BM25 as a robust baseline and the effectiveness/cost of reranking. Paper.
  11. Multilingual E5 Text Embeddings — Wang et al., 2024; multilingual contrastive embedding research supporting direct multilingual retrieval candidates. Paper.
  12. MIRACL — Zhang et al., TACL 2023; native-speaker relevance judgments across 18 languages and multilingual retrieval evaluation methodology. It does not include Urdu, so it is methodological evidence, not local validation. Paper.
  13. LegalBench-RAG — Pipitone & Alami, 2024; 6,858 expert-annotated legal query/answer pairs and character-span retrieval evaluation emphasizing minimal relevant context. Paper; official code.
  14. Legal RAG Bench — Butler & Butler, 2026; end-to-end factorial evaluation supporting retrieval as a major determinant of legal RAG quality. Recent preprint; used as supporting evidence only. Paper.
  15. Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks — Geifman & El-Yaniv, NeurIPS 2017; risk–coverage framing for calibrated abstention. Paper.
  16. Local architecture evidence — Document 01, 02, 03, 03a and 03b: invariants, official-source corpus policy, measured capacity, bitemporal schema, typed legal graph, interfaces and performance envelope.

Part 05 — Generation and Grounding

05Layer L4

Generation and Grounding

A constrained legal explanation engine: the model proposes atomic, evidence-addressed claims; code resolves the law, verifies support, preserves uncertainty, and releases only a complete answer that survived every gate.

Version 1.0Date 30 Aug 2026Layer L4Provides IGenerateRequires IRetrieve · ICorpusRead · ILLMProvider · IInferenceFigures 4
↑ Contents
§1Mandate
& invariants

The model writes language; it does not decide truth

L4 accepts a sealed GroundingContext from Document 04 and returns a VerifiedAnswer or a typed GenerationAbstention. It cannot search, broaden scope, repair a failed retrieval gate, infer authority from model memory, or call a domain service.

Inherited ruleExecutable L4 consequence
INV-1The model emits request-local evidence handles only. Citation labels, dates, URLs, reporter references and quoted text are resolved from L2 after generation.
INV-2Abstention never enters L4. Verification failure produces a typed answer failure; there is no general-knowledge fallback.
INV-3Persist context, prompt artifact, provider response, every transformation and verdict so a stored answer is byte-replayable.
INV-4No output contains a chunk ID. Public provenance ends at a provision or judgment paragraph plus source offsets/pages.
INV-5The answer repeats jurisdiction, forum, asOf, knowledge/corpus revision and coverage limits; none may be rewritten by the model.

1.1Release bars

Claim/span support ≥0.97; citation resolution 1.00; material-claim support recall 1.00; no wrong-date, wrong-jurisdiction or invented-source event in the critical set; advice-register violations 0; persisted answers byte-replayable 100%; end-to-end p50/p95 below 1.5/4 seconds; average cost ≤$0.005.

What “replay” means. Hosted generation is stochastic and provider aliases drift. Exact replay means returning and inspecting the stored provider response and verified artifact with all pinned inputs—not asking a model to regenerate identical bytes. Anonymous mode intentionally retains none of those bodies; QA-12 privacy overrides durable replay for that session.

§2Precedents
& boundary

Learn from legal AI without inheriting its claims

The useful precedent is not a vendor slogan. It is a checkable design pattern: stable legal identity, linked primary sources, treatment evidence, atomic attribution, lawyer-built evaluation and visible limits.

System / projectPattern adoptedWhat Nizam-e-Qanoon adds or rejects
Lexis+ / Shepard’sAnswers link into authoritative legal sources and expose citation-treatment signals.Adopt source-first verification; reject any inference that linked citations alone prove the adjacent claim.
Westlaw / CoCounselLegal workflows grounded in a curated research corpus with source links.Adopt inspectability and task profiles; keep Pakistani authority/time/territory as explicit data, not proprietary model behaviour.
CourtListener / RECAPCitation lookup and graph APIs separate source identity from generated prose.Adopt deterministic resolution; add official-source restrictions, bitemporal provisions and Pakistan’s effective-dated authority matrix.
Harvard Caselaw Access ProjectMachine-readable case law and open API/bulk access.Adopt corpus openness as a goal; do not mistake availability for binding effect or current treatment.
EUR-Lex ELIStable human- and machine-readable identifiers, including article-level legal identity.Adopt canonical legal-unit identity; preserve local instrument/provision identifiers and source provenance.
LegalBench / LegalBench-RAGLegal-professional task design and precise source-span retrieval evaluation.Adopt lawyer-led, task-stratified evaluation; build a Pakistan-specific Urdu/English benchmark rather than importing scores.

A preregistered Stanford evaluation found that leading proprietary RAG legal-research tools still produced hallucinations in 17–33% of tested responses. This document therefore follows ADR-6: measured attributed generation, never “hallucination-free.”

2.1Layer boundary

  • L3 decides whether evidence is sufficient and supplies applicable, typed evidence. L4 cannot retrieve.
  • L4 phrases and verifies claims. It may summarize a supplied finding but may not create a legal status.
  • L5 owns precedent treatment/good-law classification, deterministic calculators, clause selection and procedure tables. L5 may call L4; L4 never calls L5.
  • L6 owns sessions, persistence, public API and SSE. It serves exact-citation lookup directly and never sends it through generation.

The current Constitution’s post-2025 authority relations make this boundary essential. The generator receives an AuthorityFinding; it never derives “binding,” “controlling,” “overruled” or “good law” from court names or prose.

§3Typed
contracts

Generate a proposition graph, not a paragraph

Free-form paragraphs mix supported and unsupported clauses under one citation. The model instead produces small atomic claims whose evidence can be checked independently.

type GenerationRequest = {
  requestId; task: "legal_answer" | "provision_explainer" |
                   "judgment_summary" | "draft_phrase";
  context: GroundingContext; contextDigest;
  language: "en" | "ur"; readingLevel: "plain" | "professional";
  register: "legal_information"; riskClass; schemaVersion; anonymous;
}

type AtomicClaim = {
  claimId; text;
  support: { handle: EvidenceHandle; role:
    "primary" | "definition" | "qualification" | "counterauthority" }[];
  epistemic: "source_stated" | "conditional_inference" | "uncertain";
  riskTags: RiskTag[];
}

type DraftBlock = {
  blockId; kind: "short_answer" | "rule" | "conditional_application" |
    "qualification" | "conflict" | "procedure" | "coverage_limit";
  required: boolean; claims: AtomicClaim[];
}

Evidence handles are request-local aliases such as E1, dynamically allow-listed in the JSON Schema. They are not public IDs and the model cannot invent a valid handle. additionalProperties:false, bounded arrays/strings and a pinned JSON Schema 2020-12 dialect make malformed output a typed failure, not an invitation to “repair” prose.

3.1Verified output

type VerifiedAnswer = {
  answerId; requestId; task; language; readingLevel;
  scope: { jurisdiction; territory; forum; asOf; knowledgeAsOf; corpusVersion };
  blocks: VerifiedBlock[]; conflicts: ResolvedConflict[];
  coverageLimits: CoverageLimit[]; escalation?: Escalation;
  disclaimer: DisclaimerId; artifactDigest; pipelineVersions;
}

type VerifiedBlock = {
  blockId; kind; claims: VerifiedClaim[];
  citations: ResolvedCitation[]; verdict: "pass";
}

IGenerate.answer(context, style) remains the public compatibility wrapper. The general internal port becomes generate(GenerationRequest) → VerifiedArtifact | GenerationAbstention so L5 can request a judgment summary or safe phrase without violating the dependency graph. This is a proposed correction to Document 01, not a silent interface change.

§4Trust
pipeline

One-way trust, with code on both sides of the model

4.1Prompt compiler

Compile in this order: immutable policy and output schema; task/scope; evidence manifest; evidence bodies; conflict/coverage findings; user question. User and corpus text are separately delimited and labelled DATA_ONLY. The provider has no tools, search, database access, network action or secret. The prompt asks for concise claims and support handles, never chain-of-thought.

Official does not mean instructional. A court PDF or Gazette can contain text that resembles an instruction, and ingestion errors can expose hidden/bidirectional characters. Retrieved text never gains instruction priority. L1 sanitizes markup; L4 rechecks control characters, isolates bidirectional runs, constrains output and verifies the result.

§5Provider
port

A provider is a replaceable language component

interface ILLMProvider {
  complete(req: ProviderRequest): Promise<ProviderCompletion | ProviderFailure>;
  capabilities(): { schema; snapshot; retention; region; maxContext };
}

ProviderRequest = {
  messages; jsonSchema; schemaVersion; modelSnapshot;
  maxTokens; temperature; deadline; prefixCacheKey;
}
  • Vendor SDK imports exist only in generation/providers/. Each adapter maps the same request and failure taxonomy.
  • Choose a pinned hosted small model for normal explanation and a qualified reasoning tier for complex multi-source scenarios. Selection is by locked-set quality, Urdu parity, latency, retention and price ceiling—not a leaderboard.
  • Use low variance and structured decoding, but never call the output deterministic. JSON shape correctness does not imply semantic correctness.
  • One failover is permitted only to an independently qualified pinned snapshot. No recursive retries, silent “latest” alias, or model that skipped the same safety evaluation.
  • The self-hosted generator is a benchmark/batch/sovereign deployment profile, not the pilot hot path. ADR-2 puts fine-tuning into retrieval/reranking; no generator LoRA is required for MVP.

5.1Admission and privacy

An adapter is enabled only after documenting retention/training terms, data region, incident process, snapshot semantics, rate limits and deletion behaviour. Send no account/profile fields and redact names, CNIC, phone, address or other facts irrelevant to the legal issue. If sensitive traffic has no approved provider, serve current verified artifacts/search or abstain; never downgrade confidentiality.

5.2Budget

Normal output is 4–7 atomic claims, approximately 600 output tokens, with a compact evidence window capped by a configured input budget. Static policy/schema/few-shot prefixes use provider prefix caching. The local NLI batch remains roughly 40 ms for five claims under the inherited estimate. Provider network time dominates, but verification is never skipped to recover the 4-second p95.

§6Citation
& claims

The database, not the model, names the law

A citation is a resolved relationship between a claim and an official, versioned legal unit. It is not decorative text at the end of a paragraph.

// model output
{ claimId: "C2", text: "...", support: [{handle:"E3", role:"qualification"}] }

// request-local handle map; never exposed publicly
E3 -> { legalUnitId, sourceVersionId, allowedOffsets, contextDigest }

// renderer fetches at the pinned revision
ResolvedCitation {
  legalUnitId; sourceVersionId; displayLabel; shortTitle;
  validity; jurisdiction; officialSourceUrl; sourceSha256; sourcePages;
  matchedOffsets; status; authorityFinding?; treatmentCoverage?;
}
  • An unknown, duplicated, out-of-bundle or wrong-version handle rejects the claim and raises defect telemetry.
  • The model cannot output a citation-shaped string, URL, statute date, reporter reference or verbatim quote. If a quote is needed, it requests an allowed span and the renderer slices stored text exactly.
  • Every material atomic claim has at least one supporting relation. A multi-source conclusion cites every source necessary for the conjunction.
  • Support and relevance are separate: each cited item must actually contribute. Extra citations cannot launder an unsupported proposition.

6.1Answer order

Permanent scope and corpus coverage; concise conditional answer; governing rule; required definitions/provisos/exceptions/delegated instruments; conditional application to user-stated facts; conflict/unknowns; neutral next steps and referral. Deadlines, custody/liberty risks and non-operative status surface before background. User allegations remain “facts as stated,” never findings.

No chain-of-thought record. The proposition/evidence graph is the auditable reasoning surface. Hidden model reasoning is neither legal authority nor reliable provenance and is not requested, stored or shown.

§7Verification
cascade

Atomic verification, then an answer-level veto

TierChecksFailure
T0JSON Schema, size/Unicode bounds, allowed block kinds and evidence handles; no URLs/HTML/citation-shaped strings.Whole completion rejected as SCHEMA_INVALID; no repair prompt
T1Exact quote offsets; numbers, dates, durations and amounts; identity/version/as-of; jurisdiction; negation; shall/may; exception/proviso; required evidence roles.Claim rejected with deterministic reason
T2Local multilingual NLI over the atomic claim and its cited premises; contradiction/neutral/low score fails. Each citation also tested for necessity.Claim rejected; NLI is a filter, never proof
T3Independent adversarial verifier tries to falsify liability, limitation/deadline, eligibility, custody, authority/conflict, eviction, family-status and irreversible-transfer claims.unsupported or ambiguous rejects the claim
T4Register, policy, whole-answer coverage/coherence, conflict and escalation checks.Drop optional context or fail complete answer

A missing optional background claim may be dropped. Failure of the direct answer, governing rule, required qualification/exception, conflict disclosure or procedural precondition produces ANSWER_INCOMPLETE_AFTER_VERIFICATION. “Partially supported legal proposition” is never a shippable verdict; only an explicit coverage-limit block may describe uncertainty.

§8Legal
safety

Preserve legal force, not just meaning

Generator mayGenerator may not
Faithfully paraphrase a supplied operative ruleInfer commencement, repeal, territorial reach or invalidation
State a conditional: “If X is established, the provision states Y”Find facts, decide credibility, predict an outcome or guarantee relief
