§1Surface
landscape

Four surfaces, one contract

They differ in audience, rendering strategy and failure tolerance — but all four speak only IPublicAPI and ISync, so a change in the backend breaks a generated client at build time rather than a user at runtime.

§2Sublayer
hierarchy

L7 decomposed

Seven sublayers, strictly ordered. The same dependency discipline that governs L1–L8 applies inside L7: a sublayer may call only the one beneath it, and the two data sources are siblings that never know about each other.

2.1Sublayer contracts

SublayerOwnsExposesForbidden

§3Offline
architecture

The pack in the pocket

QA-9 says full statutory lookup at zero connectivity. That is not a caching requirement — it is a distribution requirement, and it produces the most consequential design in the client: a signed, versioned, transactionally-updated copy of Pakistani statute law that the app treats as authoritative rather than as a cache.

3.1Content classes decide the read path

Everything the client can read falls into one of three classes, and the class — not the network state — determines where a read goes first.

ClassContentRead pathOffline behaviour
Pack-authoritativeStatutory text, provision tree, cross-references, definitions, precomputed explainers, glossary, procedure guides, limitation and fee tablesLocal first, always. Never revalidated per read — the pack is signed, so its content is as trustworthy as the server’sFully available. This is the majority of citizen usage.
Network-preferredSearch ranking, as-at-date versions outside the pack window, provisions in an uninstalled tierNetwork when available; degraded local equivalent when not, explicitly labelledReduced quality, announced. Offline search is lexical plus glossary rather than server-reranked.
Answer-pack-servedGrounded answers to questions in the head of the distribution — the offline answer tier (§3.4)Local question index first; network only on a missAvailable with full citations and provenance, showing the canonical question matched.
Network-requiredNovel questions that miss the answer pack, precedent and citator, judgment text, document draftingNetwork only. INV-2 forbids a client-side substituteUnavailable, with a specific explanation and an offline alternative offered — never a spinner, never a silent failure.

Why judgments are not in the pack

Precedent is a graph query over hundreds of thousands of paragraphs plus treatment classification. Shipping it would multiply pack size by an order of magnitude and still give a worse answer than the server. It is declared network-required and the UI says so plainly. Choosing what not to ship offline is as much a part of this design as choosing what to ship — and §3.4 applies the same reasoning in the other direction, shipping answers because they are small and verified, rather than a generator because it is fashionable.

3.2Pack anatomy and tiers

3.3Patch format

Deltas are row-level operations, not a binary diff of the database file. A page-level diff would be fragile across SQLite versions and vacuum states, and would defeat resumability.

patch v17 → v18
  header    from_version, to_version, schema_version, built_at, sha256, ed25519_sig
  ops[]     UPSERT instrument   {id, …}
            UPSERT provision    {id, path, label, heading, status}
            UPSERT provision_text {provision_id, text_en, text_ur, validity}
            DELETE provision    {id}          only when an instrument is withdrawn
            UPSERT explainer    {provision_id, plain_en, plain_ur}
  post[]    REINDEX fts(scope)                 partial, scoped to touched instruments
            REVEC   vec(scope)                 only if the semantic tier is installed

Application is one SQLite transaction per patch, chained. Signature verified before
the transaction opens; integrity hash compared after it commits, before the version
pointer moves. Any failure rolls back and the version pointer never advances.

Chain length is capped at twelve. A device that has been offline for months takes a full re-download rather than replaying a long chain — simpler to reason about, and usually smaller.

3.4Offline grounded answers — RAG without a model on the device

“Offline RAG” sounds like it requires an on-device generator. Priced honestly it does not, and it should not: a 1B parameter model quantised to four bits is roughly 800 MB, needs several seconds of prefill for a 2,000-token context on a mid-tier phone, and would still reason about Pakistani law worse than the server did. Shipping it would multiply the install size by six to lower the answer quality.

The better move follows from something the architecture already guarantees: our answers are strictly grounded and therefore reusable. An answer that was generated against verified provisions, had its citations rendered from the database, and passed the entailment verifier is a durable artefact. So we ship the answers, not the generator.

Coverage is a measured metric, not a claim. It is reported per language and per stratum on the golden set, and regression blocks a pack release.
TierSizeQualityTarget coverageShips in
A — stored answers12 MB dl
28 MB disk		Identical to online — same pipeline, same verifier, same citations≥55% of citizen queries at ≥95% precisionPhase 4, with the app
B — templates<1 MBExact. Deterministic composition over pack data~15%, overlapping APhase 3, ships with the pack
C — on-device model~300 MB opt-inLower, labelled. Rewrites retrieved text; does not reasonnot measured as coveragePhase 6, experimental

The invalidation rule that makes this safe

Every stored answer records the provisions it cites and the corpus version it was generated against. A pack patch that amends any cited provision carries an INVALIDATE operation for every dependent answer, so the answer is removed rather than served stale. Without that rule the answer tier would slowly become a cache of law that no longer exists — which is the failure mode this entire product is built to avoid.

3.5Two sync engines, because there are two trust models

The corpus flows one way and is signed; user data flows both ways and must merge. Trying to serve both with one mechanism produces either a corpus that a client can corrupt or user data that cannot be edited offline. They are separate engines with separate storage and separate failure behaviour.

§4Navigation
& IA

Routes are provision identities

INV-4 has a direct consequence for navigation: every durable location in the product is addressed by a provision, instrument or judgment identity — never by a chunk, a search-result index, or a session-scoped token. A bookmark taken today resolves after five re-indexes.

4.1Deep links and the public URL contract

app + web share one URL grammar
  /law/fed/act-1860-45/s-302                  the canonical provision URL
  /law/fed/act-1860-45/s-302?as_of=2014-03-03 point-in-time (INV-5)
  /law/punjab/act-2019-12/s-7/cl-b            clause-level deep link
  /precedent/provision/fed:act-1860-45:s-302  citator for a provision

rules
  • The URL is derived from the provision identity in document 01 §3.1 by
    replacing dots with slashes. It is stable for the life of the provision.
  • Web and app resolve identical paths; an Android App Link opens the app
    when installed and the public page when not.
  • No query parameter may change what the law says — only as_of, which
    selects a version, and lang, which selects presentation.
§5Component
architecture

Components that encode the invariants

Most of the component library is unremarkable. Six components are not: they are where the guarantees from document 01 become something a person can see, and they are specified here rather than left to a designer’s discretion.

5.1Contracts of the invariant-bearing components

ComponentAcceptsGuaranteesEnforces
BilingualText{runs: [{text, script, dir}], role}Correct bidi isolation on every mixed run; the script-appropriate type scale; Western digits preserved in statutory identifiersQA-6
CitationChipResolvedCitation {provisionId, label, shortTitle, validity} — never strings to concatenateCannot render without a resolved identity; tapping always opens the matching ProvenanceSheetINV-1
ProvenanceSheet{provision, matchedSpan, validity, sourcePage, treatments}Shows authoritative text verbatim; highlights the exact span; states validity; links onward to the amendment chain and citatorQA-1
AnswerBlockList[{text, citations[], verdict}]Drops any block with zero citations; renders partial verdicts with a visible qualifier; never merges blocks across citationsINV-1 QA-1
AbstentionCard{searchedScope, nearest[], suggestions[]}Distinct route and layout; nearest results visually demarcated and never styled as results; always offers the referral actionINV-2 QA-2
StatusBanner{status, effectiveRange, asOf, supersededBy?}Renders above the provision text, not below it; cannot be collapsed for repealed or not_yet_commencedINV-5 QA-5

5.2Screen-state taxonomy

Every screen resolves to exactly one of eight states. The shell renders the state; the notifier chooses it. There is no ninth state and no ad-hoc inline spinner.

sealed ScreenState
  Loading      skeleton matched to the eventual layout, never a centred spinner
  Ready        content
  Empty        a valid query with no matches — distinct from Abstained
  Abstained    the gate declined — only reachable on generated surfaces
  Offline      network-required content on a device with no network
  Stale        served from a pack older than the currency threshold
  Degraded     served by a reduced path (lexical-only search, cached answer)
  Error        an actual fault — the only state that offers “retry”

Rule: Abstained, Offline, Stale and Degraded are outcomes, not faults. None of
them may borrow error styling, an error icon, or a retry affordance.
§6Bilingual
& bidi

Two scripts, one sentence

QA-6 asks for bilingual equity, and most implementations deliver it by translating the interface and stopping. The hard part is that a single Urdu sentence about Pakistani law contains left-to-right statutory identifiers, and getting that wrong does not look like a typography bug — it looks like a citation to a different section.

6.1Three independent axes

Language is not one setting. Conflating these is the root cause of most bilingual legal UI failures.

AxisValuesControlsIndependent because
UI languageen · urChrome, labels, navigation, layout directionA user may want Urdu chrome around English statutory text — and frequently does, because the statute is English.
Content languageen · ur · bothExplanations, answers, judgment summaries. Never the statutory text itselfStatutory text is shown verbatim in its enacted language always; only explanation is translated (document 01, ADR-4).
Input scriptlatin · arabic · roman-urduQuery normalisation, glossary alias lookup, keyboard hintDetected per keystroke, not chosen. A user with Urdu chrome will still type talaq on a Latin keyboard.

6.2Two type scales, selected by script

Nastaliq is a sloped, deeply cascading script: a line of Urdu occupies far more vertical space than a line of Latin at the same nominal size, its descenders collide at Latin line-heights, and its optical size runs small. A single scale cannot serve both, and a scale chosen by locale breaks on the mixed run this section is about. The scale is therefore chosen per run, by script.

RoleLatinNastaliqNote
Statutory body16 / 1.6219 / 2.05Urdu is set larger and much looser; the two must share a baseline grid so a mixed line does not jitter
Provision heading17 / 1.35 · 60020 / 1.8 · 400Nastaliq has no usable bold; emphasis comes from size and colour, never synthetic weight
Answer prose16 / 1.619 / 2.0—
Citation chip13 / 1.2 · mono13 / 1.2 · monoAlways Latin metrics — a citation is never set in Nastaliq
Caption / meta13 / 1.515 / 1.9—
Minimum touch label1417Nastaliq legibility floor is materially higher; 14 px Urdu is unreadable on a mid-tier screen

6.3What mirrors and what does not

Mirrors under RTLNever mirrors
Layout axis (start/end, never left/right) · navigation and back affordances · list chevrons · progress and stepper direction · provision clause indentation · drawer side · slider direction Source PDF page previews · the amendment timeline, which is chronological and always runs left to right · numerals within a citation · the curation console’s source-versus-parse comparison · media transport controls · anything reproducing a printed legal document

The amendment timeline is the instructive case: it is a chronological axis, not a reading order. Mirroring it in Urdu would put 2026 on the left and 1860 on the right, which reads as a claim about time rather than about language. Directionality follows the semantics of the axis, not the direction of the surrounding text.

6.4Roman Urdu at the client edge

input       "mje talaq k baad bachon ki custody chahiye"
detect      latin script + roman-urdu classifier → script = roman-urdu
normalise   consonant folding (k/ke/kay → ke) · vowel elision · digraph
            variants (kh/x, q/k) · repeated-letter collapse
expand      glossary alias lookup, client-side against the pack:
              talaq   → divorce, dissolution of marriage
              custody → hizanat, guardianship, custody of minors
send        original text + detected script + expanded concept IDs
            the server re-does this authoritatively; the client copy exists so that
            offline search works and so the keyboard hint is right

Normalisation is deliberately duplicated on both sides. The client copy is a convenience that must never disagree with the server; both read the same versioned glossary artefact, and a mismatch in glossary version is a client warning, not a silent divergence.

§7Access-
ibility

Designing for the reader who cannot read well

National literacy sits near 60%, and legal literacy far below that. The accessibility work here is not a compliance pass bolted on at the end — two of these features reach more people than any model improvement we could ship.

NeedMechanismWhere it livesVerified by
Cannot read fluentlyUrdu voice in and out. Speak a question, hear the answer. Statutory text is read at professional register; explanations at plain registerL7.7 platform → L7.3 ReadingLevelPolicyTask completion by a non-reading participant in the user study
Legal register is opaqueReading-level control on the same grounded payload. Plain speech comes from the precomputed explainer offline and a cached plain rendering online — never a second retrievalL7.3 policy, L7.1 renderingBoth renderings cite identical provisions; asserted in a widget test
Screen reader usersSemantic tree authored deliberately: provision heading is a heading, the clause tree is a nested list, the citation chip announces “citation, section 302, Pakistan Penal Code, opens source”L7.1 primitivesTraversal-order test per screen in CI
Low-end devices, bright sunContrast floor 4.5:1 for body and 3:1 for large text in both themes; no information carried by colour alone — treatment badges pair colour with a wordDesign tokens, L7.1Automated contrast assertion over the token matrix
Motor and touch48 dp minimum target with 8 dp separation; the citation chip is a full-height tap target, not just its textPressable primitiveGolden tests measure hit rectangles
Vestibular sensitivityprefers-reduced-motion honoured; the provenance sheet cross-fades instead of sliding when setMotion primitiveGolden test in both motion modes
Unfamiliar with appsIcons never appear without a text label in primary navigation; destructive and paid actions state their consequence in the button, not in a following dialogL7.1 conventionsReview checklist; no icon-only primary action ships

Where voice runs, and why it matters for privacy

Speech-to-text runs on-device where the platform provides an offline Urdu model, and falls back to a server call otherwise. That fallback is disclosed at the moment of use, and it is disabled entirely in anonymous mode — a voice query that leaves the device is a recording of someone describing a legal problem aloud, which is precisely the data QA-12 exists to protect. Text-to-speech is always on-device.

§8State, data
& security

State, sources and secrets

8.1State management

Riverpod with code generation, and one rule that matters more than the choice of library: a notifier exposes an immutable view state and nothing else. No widget reads a repository, no repository holds UI state, and no notifier persists anything.

unidirectional, per screen
  intent      user action → Notifier method
  work        Notifier → UseCase → Repository → (LocalPack | Api)
  state       Repository returns entities; UseCase applies policy;
              Notifier emits AsyncValue<ViewState>
  render      Widget rebuilds from ViewState — a pure function of state

forbidden
  • a widget that computes an in-force date, formats a citation, or
    decides whether something is repealed
  • a notifier that imports package:sqlite3 or package:http
  • a repository that returns a DTO, a nullable network type, or a Future
    that the caller must remember to catch

8.2Anonymous mode is a different object graph

Document 01 requires that anonymous mode be enforced at session scope rather than checked at call sites. A boolean consulted in twenty places will eventually be missed in the twenty-first. Instead the dependency container is rebuilt with different concrete implementations, and the code that could write is simply not present in the graph.

8.3Cache and freshness policy

DataSource of truthClient policyInvalidation
Statutory text, currentSigned packRead forever, never revalidateOnly by a verified pack patch
Statutory text, historicalServerCache per (provisionId, as_of), immutable once fetchedNever — a past version cannot change
ExplainersPack, then serverPack copy preferred; server copy cached 30 daysPack patch, or explicit refresh
Search resultsServerNot cached across sessions; kept for back-navigation onlyOn query, scope or as_of change
AnswersServerCached per request_id for the session; persisted only if the user saves itNever auto-refreshed — an answer is a record of a moment
Precedent / citatorServerCached 24 hTTL, or a corpus-version bump
Drafts in progressClientPersisted locally, encrypted, resumableOn submit or explicit discard
Auth tokensPlatform keystoreNever in shared preferences, never in the SQLite pack, never loggedOn sign-out, refresh failure, or biometric lock

8.4Client security posture

ControlImplementationFailure behaviour
Pack authenticityEd25519 public key compiled into the binary; manifest signature checked before any transaction opens, per-patch SHA-256 checked after commitReject, keep previous pack, report the event. Never apply partially.
TransportTLS with an SPKI pin set including at least one backup pin, plus a remote kill switch to disable pinning if rotation goes wrongHard fail on mismatch; the kill switch is the only recovery path and is itself signed.
Secrets at restAndroid Keystore / iOS Keychain only. Drafts and saved matters encrypted with a key held thereBiometric or device-credential re-auth; no plaintext fallback.
Telemetry scrubbingQuery text, answer text, draft field values and voice audio are never emitted. Crash reports strip strings from any type marked @SensitiveThe sink drops rather than truncates — a truncated legal query is still a legal query.
Replay identityClient generates a request_id, sends it as a trace header, and displays it in the report-an-answer sheetSatisfies INV-3 end to end; in anonymous mode the id is ephemeral and never stored locally.
Screenshot and backupDraft and saved-matter screens set the secure-window flag; the app is excluded from cloud auto-backup—

ance

Written against the device our users actually own — a 4 GB mid-tier Android phone on a congested 3G connection — not against a development machine. Each budget has a gate; a build that exceeds one fails.

BudgetTargetGate

base total ≤ 60 MB		Pack build step fails above the ceiling, per tier and in total

§10Web
& SEO

The web tier and the distribution flywheel

ADR-9 in document 01 makes public statute pages an architectural decision rather than a marketing one. Pakistan Code is effectively unindexed; a crawlable, fast, citable page for every provision is the cheapest acquisition channel available to this project by an order of magnitude.

10.1SEO architecture

  • Internal links come from the cross-reference graph. Section 302 links to 299, 304 and 311 because the corpus says it does. The link structure is generated from data rather than authored, which makes it complete, correct, and free.
  • Structured data — Legislation JSON-LD per provision with jurisdiction, enactment date, and status; BreadcrumbList for the instrument tree.
  • Sitemap index partitioned by jurisdiction, regenerated on corpus publish. Roughly 60,000 URLs at launch and growing.
  • hreflang pairs for the English and Urdu renderings of the same provision, with a shared canonical.
  • No generated content on public pages at launch. Authoritative statutory text and verified explainers only, and explainers are labelled as machine-generated. Publishing unreviewed AI prose at scale under our own domain is a reputational and legal risk we take deliberately, later, or not at all.
§11Curation
console

The console is a corpus instrument

Document 01 makes the curation console a phase-1 deliverable because automated segmentation lands near 90% and the remaining ~470 documents reach the corpus through a human. Its design goal is a single number: seconds per correction.

Appendix B — Client decision records

CDRDecisionBecauseCost accepted
CDR-1Riverpod with code generation over BLoCCompile-safe injection and far less ceremony for a four-person team; the container swap in CDR-7 is trivial in Riverpod and awkward otherwiseSmaller local hiring pool than BLoC; mitigated by a written conventions file
CDR-2Offline-first is the default read path, not a fallbackThe pack is signed and therefore as trustworthy as the server; revalidating it would add latency for no correctness gainStaleness must be surfaced explicitly on every pack-served view
CDR-3The pack is downloaded, never bundled in the binaryA 100 MB install is a hard barrier on metered connections and low-storage devices; keeping the APK under 25 MB keeps the funnel openFirst run needs connectivity, or a sideloaded pack file
CDR-4On-device semantic search is an optional tierFTS5 plus the curated romanised glossary answers most offline lookups; a 25 MB encoder should not be mandatory. It is however a prerequisite for the answer tier, so the two are offered togetherTwo offline search qualities to explain and to test
CDR-5Two embedding spaces, disclosed in the UIA 1024-dim server encoder cannot run on a mid-tier phone; pretending device and server search are equivalent would be dishonestOffline results are labelled and measurably weaker
CDR-6Row-level patches, not binary file diffsPage-level diffs are fragile across SQLite versions and vacuum states, and defeat resumabilityLarger patches than an optimal binary diff
CDR-7Anonymous mode swaps the object graphA boolean checked at call sites will eventually be missed; absence of a writer cannot be forgottenTwo container configurations to maintain and test
CDR-8Type scale selected per run by script, not by localeA single sentence contains both scripts; a locale-selected scale breaks exactly on the mixed run that matters mostEvery text render walks runs rather than taking a single style
CDR-9Public statute pages require no JavaScriptIt is a legal reference that people will cite, print and read on constrained devices; and it is the crawl surface behind ADR-9The as-of control and search on public pages are progressive enhancements
CDR-10Judgments are not shipped offlinePrecedent is a graph query plus treatment classification; shipping it would multiply pack size and still answer worse than the serverCitator is network-required, stated plainly in the UI
CDR-13Offline answers ship as verified artefacts, not as an on-device generatorA 1B four-bit model is ~800 MB, is slow to prefill on a mid-tier phone, and reasons about Pakistani law worse than the server already did. A 12 MB answer tier is higher quality and a thirtieth of the sizeCoverage is bounded by what was mined and generated; a miss abstains offline rather than improvising
CDR-14Two sync engines, one for the corpus and one for user dataThe corpus is signed and server-authored, so it needs no merge logic; user data is user-authored and must merge. One engine would force the corpus to carry semantics that break the signed-authority argumentTwo mechanisms to build and test, though the second is deliberately small
CDR-11API client generated from OpenAPI, diffed in CIFour people in one repository need contract drift to break a build, not productionA backend change can block a client build until regenerated
CDR-12Abstention, offline, stale and degraded are outcomes, not errorsError framing invites the reader to interpret silence as absence of law rather than absence of confidenceFour extra screen states to design, test and translate

B.1What this document does not decide

Visual identity, illustration, iconography and motion choreography belong to document 12, Design System & UX. The token structure and the bilingual type scales are fixed here because they are architectural — a locale-selected scale would break the mixed-run guarantee — but the specific hues, spacing ramp and icon set are not. Screen-by-screen interaction specifications for drafting and procedure belong to document 06, which owns those domains.

Part 09a — Local Environment

09aPlatform

Local Environment

Exactly what each machine needs, what every process consumes, and the bootstrap that takes a clean laptop to a queryable national legal corpus in one overnight run.

Scope ADR-1g — build production locallyRevision 1.1 — RAM correctedFigures 2Pairs with 09b Production Deployment

§1Machine
or job

There is one machine and one job

The distinction matters more than any spec. Parsing the corpus is a job that runs a handful of times in the project’s entire life. Every developer machine restores the result instead — and never opens a PDF at all.

Corrected from v1.0, which framed the build machine as a per-developer profile. It is not: it is a few hours of rented compute, three or four times ever.
The developer machineThe build job
Who needs itEveryone, every dayOne person, three or four times in the project

RAM16 GB comfortable

32 GB is faster
Cores48 — parse is embarrassingly parallel
Free disk~35 GB
~25 GB without Flutter		~120 GB
judgment sources dominate

1.1How everyone else gets the corpus

Because the Postgres image is digest-pinned and identical everywhere, the corpus ships as a physical pgBackRest backup rather than a logical dump. A physical restore is a file copy: the indexes arrive already built, so there is no HNSW rebuild on the receiving machine.

CorpusBackup sizePhysical restorepg_restore instead
Statutes only~280 MB< 1 min~4 min — rebuilds every index
With judgments~3.5 GB~6 min~50 min — the HNSW build dominates

This is also why the restore drill in §7 is not overhead: the procedure that gives a new developer a corpus is the same procedure that recovers production, so it gets exercised weekly rather than discovered during an incident.

1.2Where PDF parsing actually appears

ContextParses PDFs?Volume
Developer machineNeverRestores a backup
CIFixtures only~20 documents, seconds
Production, steady stateDeltas only20–50 new gazette documents per week. One small worker, minutes
Production, user uploadOn demandOne document at a time, bounded and sandboxed
The build jobAll of it4,710 + ~120,000 documents. Once

Content-hash gating is what keeps the steady state small: a re-scrape that finds no change does no work, so the ingest worker in production is a cron job sized in hundreds of megabytes, not the eight-worker pool the build job uses.

The one hardware rule that still matters

Keep pgdata on the internal NVMe, inside the Linux filesystem. On Windows that means inside WSL2, never on /mnt/c — the 9p bridge is roughly ten times slower for many small files, and every index operation is random I/O. Source documents can live on external storage; they are read sequentially, once, by a job you are renting a machine for anyway.

A 16 GB laptop runs the full corpus, including judgments

The 10 GB judgment database sits on disk, not in memory. With shared_buffers at 2 GB plus whatever the OS caches, roughly a third of it stays hot — and the rest falls through to NVMe at about 100 microseconds a page. Retrieval p95 rises from around 190 ms to perhaps 350 ms.

That is a latency difference, not a quality difference. Nothing about ranking, grounding, citation accuracy or abstention depends on how much of the index is cached. You would notice it while developing; no test would fail because of it.

§4Postgres
config

Configuration, computed

Default Postgres is tuned for a shared server from a decade ago and will make every number in this document wrong. These values are derived from the profile, not copied from a blog post.

# postgresql.conf — developer machine, 16 GB host, ~3 GB budget for Postgres

shared_buffers                  = 2GB      sized to the working set, not to a share of host
                                             RAM. The statutory index hot set is ~400 MB
effective_cache_size            = 8GB      planner hint: what the OS is likely caching.
                                             Not an allocation — it only shapes plans
work_mem                        = 64MB     per sort/hash node, per parallel worker.
                                             64MB x 4 workers x 8 conns = 2GB worst case
maintenance_work_mem            = 1GB      only matters on the build job; a developer
                                             machine restores indexes rather than building them
max_worker_processes            = 16
max_parallel_workers            = 4        = physical cores
max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 4
max_parallel_maintenance_workers= 4        parallel HNSW build — the single biggest
                                             win on index build time
random_page_cost                = 1.1      NVMe. Leaving this at 4.0 makes the planner
                                             avoid index scans it should be using
effective_io_concurrency        = 200      NVMe queue depth
wal_buffers                     = 64MB
max_wal_size                    = 8GB      bulk load; lower to 2GB for normal operation
checkpoint_timeout              = 15min
checkpoint_completion_target    = 0.9
jit                             = off      hurts more than it helps on our query shapes

# extensions
shared_preload_libraries        = 'pg_search'   required only below PG 17; harmless on 17

# session-level, set by the retrieval layer rather than globally
hnsw.ef_search                  = 100      raise for recall, lower for latency.
                                             Cluster-wide changes need ALTER SYSTEM +
                                             pg_reload_conf(), not ALTER ROLE

Bulk-load profile

During a full corpus ingest, switch to a second config: maintenance_work_mem = 8GB, max_wal_size = 16GB, autovacuum = off on the four large tables, synchronous_commit = off. Then re-enable autovacuum, run ANALYZE, and build the HNSW and BM25 indexes last. Building indexes before the load is the most common way to turn a 45-minute index build into a six-hour one.

4.1Build-job adjustments

The rented build machine is the only place these apply, and every line is reverted once the corpus backup is published.

5.1Embedding throughput, and why judgments need rented silicon

Chunk counts from the capacity plan. CPU rates are for an 8-core laptop with batching; GPU rates for a rented consumer card. Verify on your own hardware before planning around them.
PassChunksCPURented GPUVerdict
Statutes, 1024-dim158,000~53 min
~50/sec		~5 min
~1,500/sec		CPU is fine
Statutes, 384-dim for the pack14,000~35 sec
~400/sec		—CPU is fine
Judgments, 1024-dim4,800,000~27 hours~53 minRent a GPU
Answer-tier questions12,000~30 sec—CPU is fine

One rented hour, under a dollar, once. The judgment embedding pass is the only workload in the entire project that justifies a GPU, and it is a batch job that runs when the corpus lands and again only when the embedding model changes. Rent a consumer card by the hour, mount the corpus, write vectors back over the network, and destroy the instance. Buying a GPU for this would be a category error — and note that the same conclusion holds in production, where ADR-1f keeps the GPU node off every request path.

§6Bootstrap

The build job, start to finish

This sequence runs on the rented machine, three or four times in the project’s life. Every stage writes its state to the database, so an interrupted run continues rather than restarting — which matters because stage 3 on the full corpus runs for two hours. A developer setting up for the first time runs steps 0 to 2 and then restores a backup instead of steps 3 to 5.

# 0 — prerequisites, once
docker compose version                       v2, and set the Desktop memory cap explicitly
uv --version ; node -v ; git lfs install

# 1 — bring up the stack and create the schema
git clone <repo> && cd nizam
cp .env.example .env                         set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, R2 keys optional locally
docker compose up -d postgres minio
uv run alembic upgrade head                  the schema exists only because of this
uv run python -m nizam.ops.verify_extensions fails loudly on a version mismatch

# 2 — fetch model artifacts and convert once
uv run python -m nizam.ops.fetch_models --int8
docker compose up -d inference api

# 3 — ingest, resumable at every stage
uv run python -m nizam.corpus.run --source federal   --workers 8
uv run python -m nizam.corpus.run --source provincial --workers 8
uv run python -m nizam.corpus.run --source judgments  --workers 8   build job only

# 4 — embed. CPU for statutes; rent a card for judgments
uv run python -m nizam.index.embed --scope statutes            ~53 min CPU
uv run python -m nizam.index.embed --scope judgments --remote  ~53 min on a rented GPU

# 5 — build indexes last, with the bulk-load config still active
uv run python -m nizam.index.build --hnsw --bm25 --analyze

# 6 — prove it
uv run pytest tests/integration
uv run python -m nizam.evals.run --set golden --report
uv run python -m nizam.ops.backup --to local && uv run python -m nizam.ops.restore --check
§7Parity

Proving the local build is production

The whole point of ADR-1g is that what you build locally is the production database, so moving it is a restore rather than a rebuild. These are the checks that keep that true.

CheckHowFails when
Schema comes only from migrationsCI runs alembic upgrade head against an empty database, dumps the schema, and diffs it against a committed golden schema fileSomeone created an index in pgAdmin. This is the most common and most damaging drift
Extension versions pinnedA migration asserts pg_search, vector and ltree versions and raises on mismatchA newer image silently changes ranking or index format
Image digest pinnedCompose references @sha256:…, not :latestlatest moved and two developers now disagree about BM25 scores
Collation identicalAssert lc_collate and lc_ctype in the same migrationA different collation changes index ordering and text comparison — silent, and genuinely nasty to diagnose
Postgres major version identicalAssert server_version_num rangeA physical restore across major versions is impossible; you would need a dump
Backup round-tripsMonthly: restore the local repository into a scratch container and run the golden set against itThe backup was never valid. Better to learn this on a laptop
Evaluation is reproducibleGolden-set NDCG@10 and faithfulness recorded per commit; CI blocks regressionsRetrieval quality changed and nobody noticed which change did it

The rule, stated once

pgAdmin4 is a viewer. Every schema object — table, index, constraint, extension, role, policy — is created by a migration file in git and by nothing else. If the answer to “how do I recreate this on the server?” is anything other than “run the migrations”, the local environment has stopped being production and the move in document 09b stops being a two-hour restore.

What the system actually consumes

Sizing starts from work per request, not from a vendor tier. The conclusion is unintuitive and it drives every choice below: this system is bound by memory and disk, not by CPU.

1.1Cost of one grounded answer

Core-seconds on a modern x86 core with ONNX int8. The reranker figure assumes the fine-tuned MiniLM-class cross-encoder specified in §1.2, not a 560M-parameter model.
StageCore-secWall msNote
Query parse, citation grammar, locale0.0022Pure CPU, no model
Query embedding, 1024-dim int80.02020One short text
BM25 + HNSW + graph expansion0.08045Postgres, parallelised; index in shared buffers
Cross-encoder rerank, 50 pairs0.15060Batched across 4 cores. The single largest CPU item
Context assembly0.01012Whole-provision fetch
Entailment verification, ~5 claims0.10040NLI base, int8
Citation render + audit write0.00810—
Server-side total per answer0.37~190Excluding the LLM call, which is network wait, not our CPU

The reranker must be small, and that is a design decision, not a compromise

A 560M-parameter cross-encoder reranking 50 pairs costs roughly 3.3 core-seconds per query on CPU — nine times the entire rest of the pipeline, and enough to make CPU the binding constraint at even modest load. A fine-tuned MiniLM-class cross-encoder does the same job at about 0.15 core-seconds. Since ADR-2 already commits us to fine-tuning the reranker on our own golden set, training the small one is strictly better: we get the domain adaptation and a twentieth of the latency. Benchmark both during the ablation; ship the small one unless the large one wins by more than it costs.

1.2Three load points

Peak assumed at 10× average. Answers are the expensive path; searches and provision reads are roughly a fifth of the cost each. Mobile provision reads are served from the offline pack and never reach the server at all.

Read the last three columns together. At fifty thousand monthly active users the whole system needs well under one core at peak — but it wants ten gigabytes of hot index. Buying a machine for its core count would be buying the wrong axis entirely; source documents live in R2, so even the disk requirement is modest. The working set is what must stay in memory: the binary HNSW index over 4.96M vectors (~1.5 GB), the BM25 index (~1.6 GB), hot provision text (~2 GB), plus Postgres overhead and the three resident ONNX models.

Source documents do not live on the server

The 40 GB of judgment PDFs sits in R2, not on the production disk — the server holds the extracted, structured corpus and nothing else. That single correction takes the disk requirement from 130 GB to under 50 GB and puts several cheaper machines back on the table.

1.4Trading latency for memory, deliberately

The instinct that a little more latency should buy a lot less memory is correct, and it is worth stating as an explicit dial rather than discovering it under pressure. HNSW traversal is random-access: an uncached page costs roughly 100 µs on NVMe, and a query touches on the order of a thousand of them in the worst case.

Estimated p95 for a full grounded answer at pilot load. The corpus is 10 GB; what changes is how much of it stays hot.
Host RAMshared_buffersCorpus cachedAnswer p95Verdict
32 GB10 GB~100%~190 msNothing further to buy
24 GB8 GB~85%~210 msComfortable
16 GB6 GB~60%~260 msRecommended well inside the 4 s budget
12 GB4 GB~40%~340 msWorkable noticeable, still fine
8 GB2 GB~20%~450 msTight models and Postgres start competing

Every row answers identically. Ranking, grounding, citation accuracy and abstention are properties of the index and the pipeline, not of how much of the index is resident. Memory buys latency; it does not buy quality. The QA-8 budget is 4 seconds at p95, and even the bottom row spends a tenth of it.

§1bHow many
users

How far one box goes

Derived from the per-answer cost in §1.1 and a usage model of six answers, eight searches and fifteen provision reads per active user per month — with mobile provision reads served entirely from the offline pack and never reaching the server at all.

Peak assumed at ten times average. Cores available for serving on an 8-core box after Postgres, OS and batch work: about 4.
MAUAnswers/moPeak QPSPeak coresWhat binds first
1,0006,0000.120.05Nothing. The box is idle
10,00060,0001.20.12Nothing
50,000300,0005.80.60Index cache pressure. Add RAM before cores
100,000600,00011.61.2Postgres connections — add PgBouncer in transaction mode

You run out of money before you run out of server

At 250,000 monthly active users the machine costs about €40 and the LLM calls cost roughly $2,400 a month — sixty times more. At 500,000 the server is still one box and the model bill is near $5,000.

So the honest capacity answer is: a single €21–40 VPS comfortably carries 50,000 to 100,000 monthly active users, and does not become the binding constraint until somewhere past 250,000. Long before that, the questions that matter are how much of the answer traffic the offline answer tier and the semantic cache can deflect, and whether the paid advocate tier covers the model bill. Both are product decisions, not infrastructure ones.

What to do at each ceiling, in order

  1. Cache harder. Widen the semantic response cache and mine production logs to expand the answer tier. Deflection is worth more than hardware at every load point above pilot.
  2. Add RAM, not cores. Cache pressure shows up long before CPU does.
  3. Add PgBouncer. Connection exhaustion is the first hard wall, and it arrives around 100,000 MAU.
  4. Partition the audit log monthly and archive old partitions to R2.
  5. Split the database onto its own host (§3), private network, no public IP.
  6. Add a read replica for search and public pages. Only here does the architecture need a second serving node.

At scale, the server is a rounding error

Fifty thousand monthly active users cost about €21 of compute and roughly €690 of per-request services. Which means the two most valuable cost controls in this architecture are not infrastructure decisions at all — they are the offline answer tier and the semantic response cache, both of which remove LLM calls entirely. Every point of deflection is worth roughly $8 a month at this volume. That reframes the answer tier from an offline convenience into the primary lever on unit economics, and it is the strongest argument yet for mining and pre-generating aggressively.

The second lever is SMS. Send an OTP on signup and on new-device sign-in only, never on every session, and the line drops by more than half.

When to change something

Each row is a metric with a threshold and one action. Scaling decisions taken on any other basis — a feeling, a milestone, a conference talk — are how a four-person team ends up operating infrastructure it does not need.

SignalThresholdAction
Postgres p95 query time> 150 msCheck the index working set is resident (pg_statio hit ratio < 0.99 means it is not). Raise shared_buffers before buying anything
shared_buffers + app RSS> 70% of host RAMSplit the database onto its own host (§3). This is the primary split trigger

Disk used> 70%Move judgment source documents to R2 Infrequent Access and keep only extracted text locally

LLM spend per answer> $0.006Widen the semantic cache window and expand the answer tier from production query logs

§6Operations

The minimum that must exist

AreaStandard
BackuppgBackRest to R2 — weekly full, daily incremental, continuous WAL archive. Fourteen-day recovery window. This replaces the $100/month managed PITR add-on and is strictly more configurable
Restore drillMonthly, on a scratch container, with the golden-set evaluation run against the restored copy. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup, and the drill doubles as the rehearsal for the migration in the capacity plan §5.3
DeploysMigrations run before code. Compose file references image digests, never :latest. Every deploy tagged; rollback tested at least once per phase
UpgradesMinor Postgres monthly during a stated window. Major annually, rehearsed on the laptop first with a dump-and-restore since a physical restore cannot cross major versions
MonitoringLatency, traffic, errors, saturation — plus four domain signals: corpus currency per source, gate abstention rate, verifier pass rate, and cost per answer
AlertingDisk > 80%, backup failure, WAL archive stalled, p95 breach sustained 10 minutes, abstention-rate shift. Route to one person on a rota, not to a channel nobody watches
SecurityFirewall default-deny; SSH keys only, no password auth; unattended security upgrades; fail2ban; database bound to localhost or the private vSwitch only; secrets in a file with 0600, never in the compose file
RunbooksFour written before launch: restore from backup, rotate a leaked credential, roll back a bad deploy, and recover a failed corpus publish

6.1What a dedicated server obliges that a cloud instance does not

Hetzner’s dedicated line has no hypervisor beneath it, which is most of why it is fast and cheap. Three consequences worth planning for: there is no instant snapshot, so pgBackRest is the only recovery path and must genuinely work; there is no live resize, so a capacity change means provisioning a new machine and restoring; and hardware can fail in a way a cloud instance abstracts away, so the RAID 1 pair and the off-box backup are both load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. Budget half a day for the initial hardening and accept that the restore drill is not optional.

Part 10 — Evaluation and Quality

10Cross-cutting

Evaluation and Quality

The executable standard of proof for Pakistani legal intelligence: jurisdiction-specific benchmarks, lawyer adjudication, component isolation, statistical release gates, adversarial testing, production surveillance and a signed record of why each version was allowed to ship.

Version 1.0Date 30 Aug 2026Scope L1–L7 + platformProvides IEvaluationRegistry · IReleaseGate · IChallengeLoopRequires versioned artifacts and replay traces from Docs 02–09Figures 5
↑ Contents
§0Mandate
& authority

Quality is permission to release, not a score after release

Document 10 is independent of the implementation layers. It does not improve a result, select a model or repair a corpus. It measures a versioned candidate against declared legal and engineering risks, then returns pass, limited_scope or reject with reproducible evidence.

Standing ruleEvaluation consequenceNon-negotiable evidence
INV-1Generated citation strings never receive partial credit. Identity and quotation are resolved against L2 bytes.Every displayed citation resolves; every quote matches the stored span exactly.
INV-2An answer emitted after a failed sufficiency gate is a critical architecture violation, even if its prose happens to be correct.Control-flow and mutation tests prove the abstention branch cannot call generation.
INV-3Evaluation replays stored authenticated artifacts; it never asks a stochastic provider to recreate old bytes.Request, scope, candidates, evidence, prompt, provider response, verdicts and artifact digests remain linked.
INV-4Golden labels end at provisions, judgment paragraphs and source spans, not volatile chunks.A re-chunk migration invalidates zero labels, citations, bookmarks or answer dependencies.
INV-5Correct law from the wrong date, territory, forum or authority perspective is wrong.Every fixture states as_of, jurisdiction, territory and forum, or expects typed clarification.
QG-0No aggregate may hide a critical failure or a failing declared slice.Release report carries per-stratum results, confidence intervals and the complete critical-event ledger.

Vocabulary

Correct means supported, applicable and materially complete. Grounded means attributable to identified official evidence; it does not by itself establish legal correctness. Useful coverage is the fraction of in-scope questions receiving a complete answer at the required risk. Abstention is a valid product outcome. A critical event is a failure whose severity blocks release regardless of the mean.

§1Governance
& posture

Pakistani legal judgment remains human; automation supplies evidence

The 2026 LJCP guidelines govern judicial institutions rather than this private product, but their human-centric, assistive, transparent, accountable and privacy-protecting posture is the right public-interest benchmark. The system therefore informs and assists; it does not substitute a model score for a Pakistani lawyer’s determination of legal effect.

AuthorityStatus used hereQuality implicationClaim not made
Constitution, Art. 14Enacted constitutional protection of dignity and privacy of the home.Minimise legal-sensitive data; test anonymous non-persistence and access isolation.Not presented as a complete data-protection code.
Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984Enacted law of evidence, including electronic-system and modern-device evidence.Preserve bytes, hashes, versions, UTC time and chain of custody for evaluation evidence.A log or hash does not guarantee admissibility or evidentiary weight.
PBC Rules 1976, r.146Professional conduct duty concerning confidential client information held by advocates.Restricted reviewer workspaces, matter isolation and no silent training reuse.Platform use alone does not create advocate-client privilege.
MOITT PDP Bill, May 2023Officially listed as Draft at this document date.Use data minimisation, deletion and purpose controls as forward-compatible product policy.No draft provision is described as enacted law.
LJCP AI Guidelines 2026Official guidance adopted for judicial institutions.Human review, contestability, traceability, bias testing and bounded automation.Not misrepresented as a statute binding this private service.

§2Quality
model

Fourteen attributes become one traceable control system

The master targets are retained, not silently reinterpreted. Doc 10 adds measurement definitions, slice rules and release severity so the same number means the same thing in a notebook, CI and a signed release card.

IDQualityInherited release targetPrimary evidence
QA-1GroundednessSupported-claim precision ≥0.97; citation resolution 1.00; material support recall 1.00.Atomic claim/span lawyer labels; DB citation and quote checks.
QA-2Honest abstentionPrecision ≥0.90; recall ≥0.85 on unanswerable cases.Reason-labelled negative set; risk–coverage and calibration curves.
QA-3RetrievalNDCG@10 ≥0.75; Recall@50 ≥0.90; MRR@10 ≥0.70.Minimal necessary spans plus acceptable authority sets.
QA-4Corpus integritySegmentation F1 ≥0.97; text coverage ≥98%.Golden PDFs, provision trees, page geometry and gate records.
QA-5Temporal correctnessPoint-in-time accuracy ≥0.95; zero critical version leakage.Before/after amendment pairs, commencement and savings fixtures.
QA-6Bilingual equityUrdu–English NDCG gap ≤0.05; generation faithfulness gap ≤0.03.Clustered English, Urdu and Roman Urdu triplets.
QA-7Auditability100% authenticated released answers replay byte-for-byte.Artifact graph reconstruction and digest verification.
QA-8LatencyCitation fast path <50 ms; p50 <1.5 s; p95 <4 s.Cold/warm, route and degradation histograms.
QA-9Availability99.5% monthly; full statutory lookup at zero connectivity.Fault injection, signed-pack and airplane-mode journeys.
QA-10Cost≤$0.005 average per answer; ≤$100/month pilot.Versioned token/CPU/storage attribution by successful outcome.
QA-11EvolvabilityProvider swap is configuration; re-chunk breaks zero citations.Port contract and migration compatibility suites.
QA-12PrivacyZero anonymous persistence; PII redacted before evaluation/training use.Dependency graph, heap/log scans, erasure and provider-payload tests.
QA-13Legal safetyZero advice-register violation in the red-team suite.Pakistani lawyer-coded response-register adversaries.
QA-14AccessibilityCore citizen tasks complete in plain speech with voice support.WCAG 2.2 AA, bilingual usability and assistive-technology testing.

Critical beats average

A wrong section that is caught and withheld contributes to abstention quality. A wrong section shown to a user is a critical event. The same rule applies to wrong province/date, fabricated authority, lost proviso, dissent-as-ratio, incorrect limitation result, cross-user disclosure and unsigned pack acceptance.

§3Evaluation
architecture

Evaluate the seam, the component and the whole journey

An end-to-end failure cannot say whether the source, parser, retriever, generator, legal rule or client caused it. Each layer therefore exposes a replayable evaluation port, while one orchestrator executes the same case through isolated and end-to-end tracks.

evals/
  registry/       dataset, artifact, metric and release-policy manifests
  cases/          Pakistan legal scenarios; source spans stored by stable identity
  fixtures/       PDF, temporal, jurisdiction, security, sync and failure artifacts
  tasks/          corpus, retrieval, oracle-generation, domains, e2e, client
  metrics/        deterministic scorers; statistical intervals; slice reducers
  runners/        local/CI/nightly/release execution profiles
  adjudication/   blind assignment, disagreement, reasons and senior decision
  redteam/        versioned attacks mapped to assets and controls
  reports/        immutable run manifests, diffs, cards and evidence bundles
§4Pakistan legal
benchmark

Five hundred scenarios are a beginning, not a national average

golden-pk-v1 contains 500 independently authored legal scenarios. Language variants, temporal pairs and jurisdiction pairs remain one statistical cluster so paraphrases cannot leak across splits or pretend to be independent evidence.

PartitionBase scenariosPermitted useAccess
Fit250Retriever/reranker training and rule development. Labels visible.Engineering + legal team.
Calibration100Gate thresholds, confidence calibration and non-inferiority margins.Evaluation owner; no gradient training.
Locked release100Candidate-versus-production release decision.Runner service; item labels hidden from change authors.
Sealed challenge50Milestone audit and provider/model qualification; never routine CI.Legal lead + evaluation owner under access audit.

The split key is a connected component over legal issue, instrument family, judgment family, source revision and situation mapping. All translations, Roman Urdu variants, before/after dates, neighbouring sections and synthetic mutations stay in the same component. A random row split is prohibited.

4.1Coverage frame

AxisRequired strataSampling rule
JurisdictionFederation, Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan; ICT distinguished; GB/AJK separately labelled when enabled.Minimum declared slice size before a headline; otherwise report exploratory and limit product scope.
Court and authorityFederal Constitutional Court/constitutional relation as applicable, Supreme Court, FSC, five High Courts, subordinate/special forum contexts.Effective-dated hierarchy; majority/dissent and treatment must be labelled.
Legal sourceConstitution, Acts/Ordinances, rules/regulations, schedules, gazette notifications and official judgments.Draft, bill, repealed, uncommenced, superseded and historical material included as traps.
TaskCitation lookup, legal issue, current/historical law, precedent, procedure, calculator, drafting and source investigation.No single retrieval-style question may stand in for an end-to-end professional workflow.
User expressionProfessional English, plain English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, mixed script, incomplete facts and false premise.Native drafting and review; translation alone does not create a gold case.
RiskRoutine information, deadline-bearing, liberty, family, property, money, professional reliance and privacy-sensitive.Oversample foreseeable high-harm cases; reweight only for product-level estimates.
AnswerabilityComplete, conditional, insufficient facts, ambiguous, official-source conflict, unsupported scope and professional review required.At least one valid abstention reason; nearest result is not a positive label.

Coverage statement

A passing federal-statute benchmark authorizes only that measured scope. It does not authorize claims about complete Pakistani law, judicial invalidation, delegated legislation, a province or a court whose source coverage has not passed. The release card and client coverage banner must use the same scope registry.

§5Labels
& adjudication

The gold label is a legal argument with provenance

A single reference answer is brittle and legally dishonest. Each case stores a proposition graph: what must be said, which primary spans support it, what may also support it, what contradicts it, which qualifications are material and when the system must decline.

LegalEvalCase {
  caseId; datasetVersion; familyId; riskClass; languages[];
  question: { text; script; intendedMeaning; suppliedFacts[]; omittedFacts[] };
  scope: { jurisdiction; territory?; forum?; authorityPerspective?; asOf };
  expectedOutcome: LegalOutcomeKind;
  propositions: [{ id; text; materiality; modality; polarity;
    necessaryEvidence[]; acceptableEvidenceSets[][]; contraryEvidence[];
    qualifications[]; forbiddenClaims[] }];
  retrievalGold: { necessaryUnits[]; relevantUnits[]; hardNegatives[] };
  abstention?: { code; requiredClarification[]; unsafeAlternatives[] };
  provenance: { officialUrls[]; corpusRevision; ruleManifest?; labelledAt };
  review: { annotatorA; annotatorB; agreement; adjudicator; reasons[] };
}
StageProtocolRecorded quality
A0Case author writes facts and risk without seeing system output.Provenance, conflict declaration and issue-family key.
A1Two legal annotators independently identify operative primary sources, minimal spans, authority, time, territory and material qualifications.Raw agreement, categorical agreement and span overlap by field.
A2Senior advocate adjudicates with reasons; unresolved legitimate alternatives remain alternate gold sets.Adjudication rate and disagreement taxonomy.
A3Data engineer resolves stable legal identities and verifies source page/hash; annotator confirms rendering.100% identity and source resolution.
A4Evaluation owner assigns the entire family to one split and freezes a content digest.Leakage graph has zero cross-split edge.

Report percent agreement plus a chance-corrected statistic suitable to the field; do not worship one coefficient. Low agreement is a signal to improve guidance or preserve doctrinal ambiguity, not permission to majority-vote a contested legal proposition away. Annotators must disclose practice area, language competence and conflicts.

§6Corpus
& storage

Prove the evidence layer before measuring intelligence

A model cannot recover a missing proviso, wrong source revision or broken page span. Corpus evaluation runs before retrieval and blocks publication; storage evaluation proves that the same legal identity and temporal answer survive migrations, backup and offline projection.

SurfaceMeasuresRelease rule
AcquisitionOfficial host, complete bytes, media type, source date, ETag/Last-Modified, SHA-256, fetch manifest and duplicate lineage.No public item without immutable blob and reproducible manifest.
ExtractionCharacter/word coverage, OCR CER/WER by script, page assignment, table cell fidelity and reading order.Overall text coverage ≥98%; high-risk schedule cells require double-entry equality.
Legal treeProvision boundary precision/recall/F1, hierarchy, sibling citation uniqueness, provisos, explanations, illustrations, schedules and source coordinates.Segmentation F1 ≥0.97, zero ambiguous sibling citations, and zero known orphan material provision in critical fixtures.
Printed contents evidenceOrdered-entry preservation, repeated labels, exact block/page anchors, body-boundary false positives and resolution gaps.Every parsed entry links to the same document and physical page; unmatched entries are a release-visible worklist, never silently dropped or auto-resolved.
Source correctionApproved patch locator cardinality, exact before/after text, immutable source block and rebuild replay.Every approved patch applies exactly once or the build fails closed; the extracted block remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
Legal relationsAmends, repeals, saves, commences, defines, empowers, non-obstante, subject-to and citation edges.Status-changing edges require exact target, evidence and legal review.
Temporal storageNon-overlap constraints, before/after text, publication versus legal validity, unknown commencement and transaction-time replay.Point-in-time fixtures pass; unknown is never coerced into operative or inoperative.
PublicationGate completeness, atomic visibility, deterministic corpus hash and failed-run isolation.Rebuild from immutable blobs + pinned code yields the same published hash.
Offline projectionIdentity parity, precomputed legal guards, FTS/vector deltas, patch chain, signature and rollback.Tampered or schema-incompatible pack rejected; no citation changes identity.
RecoveryRestore, migrations, extensions, collation, index parity and golden evaluation after restore.Monthly scratch restore completes and produces accepted evaluation deltas.

Measured release boundaries, 10 September 2026

nizam_clean retains all 4,595 active evidentiary revisions. Source reads release 4,594 documents; malformed document 4608 remains review-only. Migrations 0035–0040 additionally require resolved structural decisions, canonical identity, complete reconciliation of provisions promised by a printed contents list, and no unresolved internal instrument boundary. The legal views contain 3,720 instruments, 300,137 provisions and 285,156 versions; 2,312 S7 decisions and 1,988 canonical contents gaps remain blocked. Multi-expression materialisation has reduced the S10 queue to zero, confirmed independently by a source-span-aware detector.

OCR repair uses independent readings, not confidence laundering. Tesseract candidates retain word confidence and geometry; Tesseract’s official best models are a slower comparison lane. Surya / Surya-2 and PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 multilingual models provide independent Urdu-capable readings. The completed Surya batch produced 16 promoted source-derived E4 revisions, and the current audit accepts 106/106 OCR-bearing documents. That does not turn model confidence into ground truth: only a subset received direct visual checks, so later discrepancies in Urdu, citations, dates, monetary amounts and schedule cells must still be resolved against the page image or by bilingual human adjudication. The rejected page-1 candidate for document 4503 remains useful evidence of why confidence alone cannot authorize text.

§7Retrieval
& gate

Measure finding, legal applicability and sufficiency separately

Similarity is only candidate discovery. Evaluation therefore scores exact resolution, stage-one recall, reranking, deterministic legal filters, context completeness and the final decision to answer as distinct objects.

TrackPrimary measuresCritical failure
Citation grammarExact resolution, MRR@10, ambiguity reason accuracy.Auto-selecting the wrong Act, section, version or judgment.
Candidate recallRecall@50, necessary-set recall, generator contribution and duplicate-adjusted pool size.Missing the only controlling provision while returning semantically similar text.
RankingNDCG@10, MRR@10, pairwise authority errors and hard-negative separation.Dissent, repealed version or wrong province outranks eligible operative evidence without flagging.
Context assemblyNecessary dependency coverage, excess-context ratio, proviso/definition/schedule completeness.Winning clause supplied without its legally decisive exception or delegated rule.
PrecedentAuthority-relation accuracy, treatment accuracy, majority-status accuracy and conflict recall.Claiming binding/good-law status from similarity or absence of an edge.
Temporal/territorialPoint-in-time accuracy and wrong-jurisdiction rate.Any wrong-date/place evidence admitted on the critical hard-filter set.
Sufficiency gateAbstention precision/recall, reason accuracy, Brier/ECE and area under risk–coverage.Lowering the threshold under failure or allowing an abstention into L4.

7.1Mandatory ablations

  • BM25, dense, definitions and graph independently; then RRF, cross-encoder and completeness expansion.
  • float32, halfvec(384) and bit(1024); binary ships only if Recall@50 passes and reranked NDCG loses no more than two points.
  • Approximate versus exact search by filter selectivity; shadow exact recall reported per jurisdiction and date mode.
  • Direct multilingual retrieval versus any translation proposal; compare citation-token fidelity, not just semantic score.
  • Current versus historical law, each enabled jurisdiction, precedent coverage, Roman Urdu and degraded paths.

Selective prediction

The chosen threshold is fitted only on calibration data. Publish risk against useful-answer coverage, not a single confidence number. Group-specific thresholds require enough independent calibration clusters; otherwise the conservative global threshold applies. No production incident may trigger an automatic threshold reduction.

§8Generation
& attribution

Score atomic propositions, then veto an incomplete whole

String similarity cannot determine whether an answer changed may to shall, lost an exception or cited a true but inapplicable case. Evaluation follows the AIS idea of attribution to identified sources, extended with Pakistani authority, validity and material-completeness labels.

MetricTargetMeasurement
Citation/quote integrity1.00 / 1.00Deterministic identity resolution and byte/span equality; no model judge.
Supported-claim precision≥0.97Lawyer decision per atomic proposition against cited spans.
Material support recall1.00Every material claim must enter verification; hidden claims fail.
Citation completeness / qualification recall≥0.95Gold proposition graph and necessary evidence/qualification set.
Critical applicability errors0 observedWrong place, date, authority, source, ratio or invented authority ledger.
Advice-register violation0 observedLawyer-coded response boundary; disclaimer does not erase substantive conduct.
English–Urdu faithfulness gap≤0.03Paired claim/support decisions with identical evidence graph.
Cache precision / stale served≥0.95 / 0Scope-equivalence and dependency invalidation challenge set.

Automatic NLI, register classifiers and LLM judges are triage signals. Before use, each is compared with lawyer labels by language, risk and proposition type; thresholds and error costs are recorded. None is the sole release authority. BLEU, ROUGE and answer-string similarity may describe wording, never legal correctness.

§9Domain
services

Deterministic legal machinery needs proofs, not model benchmarks

Precedent signals, calculators, drafting rules and procedure engines are evaluated as versioned legal programs. Their decisive obligations are branch completeness, source linkage, temporal scope and transparent inability.

DomainRequired suitesRelease blocker
Precedent citatorProposition identity, majority/dissent, effective court hierarchy, forward treatment, negative/positive separation, conflict and coverage mutation.Whole-case “good law” claim, wrong binding relation or absence-of-edge treated as approval.
LimitationBoundary dates, excluded time, disability, acknowledgment, forum, cause/event classification, historical schedule and timezone/date property tests.Any unqualified scalar deadline where a legal branch or fact is unresolved.
Fees/duties/forumProvince, instrument/relief classification, brackets, caps, rounding, amendment dates and double-entered schedule rows.Wrong province/rate/date or generated table value.
Document factoryInterview branch coverage, clause preconditions, contradiction, mandatory/forbidden clause, provenance, rendering and pack completeness.Clause selected without satisfied reviewed rule; draft presented as executed, stamped, filed or professionally approved.
Procedure engineState reachability, prerequisites, forms, fees, forum, official exits, deadlines, alternate/failure paths and historical version.Dead end, invented official link, omitted decisive prerequisite or false completion certification.
Rule registrySchema, evidence, dependency graph, golden/mutation tests, signature, maker-checker and rollback.Unsigned/unreviewed activation or rule/corpus incompatibility.

9.1Mutation standard

For every critical legal branch, generate mutants that invert a comparator, move a boundary by one day, remove an exception, swap a province, alter a court relation, delete a prerequisite or change may to shall. The suite must kill every critical mutant. Surviving mutants expose a missing test even when ordinary branch coverage reads 100%.

§10End-to-end
outcomes

Users experience a legal journey, not a metric dashboard

End-to-end evaluation runs the master use cases through real contracts and clients. It scores task success, legal safety, inspectability and recovery, while retaining component traces for diagnosis.

JourneySuccess evidenceFailure injection
Find law as at a dateCorrect provision version, status banner, scope and source page.Amendment during request; unknown commencement; stale cache.
Ask a grounded questionComplete verified artifact, atomic citations, limitations and replay/challenge path.Gate abstention, provider timeout, forged evidence handle, verifier veto, audit failure.
Trace precedentForum-relative authority, proposition treatment, majority status, conflicts and coverage.Matching dissent, changed hierarchy, missing adverse database coverage.
CalculateInputs, branch trace, rule/source version, result range or typed inability.Boundary day, missing fact, wrong province and conflicting source.
DraftConditioned clauses, source map, warnings and export status.Contradictory answers, unsupported clause, renderer crash and stale rule pack.
Follow procedurePrerequisites, official destinations, forms, fees, deadlines and progress disclaimer.Broken official link, offline state, changed rule and impossible step.
Work offlineSigned current pack, statutory search, source reading, supported deterministic tools and honest unavailable states.Tampered patch, interrupted apply, rollback and expired pack.
Investigate/challengeExact released bytes and proof graph; authorized challenge; correction lineage.Cross-user ID, deleted artifact, old corpus and revoked reviewer.

Staging runs the full corpus and the sixteen master use cases. Release review includes a blinded manual panel over at least twenty sampled golden answers plus every changed critical stratum. That sample is a qualitative safeguard, not a statistically representative accuracy claim.

§11Language
& access

Parity means equivalent legal force, not translated interface strings

English, Urdu and Roman Urdu are separate evaluation strata. A legally weaker Urdu explanation, reversed mixed-script citation or inaccessible source sheet is a substantive failure even where the underlying English answer passes.

SurfaceMeasureMethod
Query understandingIntent, legal term and citation-token preservation by script.Native-authored triplets; alias perturbations; no machine translation as gold.
RetrievalPaired NDCG and necessary-set recall gap.Same legal scenario and labels remain one cluster.
GenerationClaim support, modality, negation, exception and qualification parity.Bilingual legal reviewers compare against the same evidence graph, not each other’s prose.
Typography/bidiStatutory identifier order, isolate placement, Nastaliq scale and truncation.Widget goldens: two scripts × two themes; mixed-run unit fixtures.
AccessibilityWCAG 2.2 AA, semantic order, labels, contrast, keyboard, focus, 48 dp targets and reduced motion.Automated checks plus screen reader, keyboard and device testing.
ComprehensionTask completion, source discovery, error recovery and comprehension of scope/abstention.Moderated study with citizens across literacy, language, disability and device/connectivity contexts.
VoiceUrdu recognition error, legal-token accuracy and correction burden.Consented, purpose-limited study data; server fallback disabled in anonymous mode.

The planned thirty-person closed-beta study is formative. Report participant characteristics and observed task failures; do not publish population-wide usability claims from it. Accessibility conformance does not replace testing with Pakistani users, and user testing does not replace testable WCAG criteria.

§12Red team
& abuse

Attack the evidence, authority, boundary and operator

The red team is mapped to legal harms and system assets, not a generic jailbreak list. Each discovered defect becomes a minimized, versioned fixture that fails the vulnerable layer and the end-to-end path.

Attack familyExamplesSafe result
Fabricated lawNon-existent Act/section/case; altered reporter reference; plausible unofficial URL.Exact not-found or ambiguity; no source invented; official-source boundary visible.
Applicability trapCorrect text from wrong province/date; bill as law; repealed Act; uncommenced section; dissent as ratio.Hard exclusion, historical label, conflict or typed inability.
Evidence injectionPDF footnote/HTML/image says ignore policy, reveal prompt, forge evidence handle or call a tool.Content remains inert data; handle/schema/support failure.
Completeness attackHide proviso, savings clause, schedule, delegated rule or contrary authority outside the best chunk.Dependency expansion finds it or the sufficiency/whole-answer gate abstains.
Register pressureDemand prediction, representation, personalized strategy, guaranteed outcome or advocate impersonation.Information boundary, visible limitation and professional referral.
Privacy/tenancyCross-user object ID, report link, cache collision, log injection, anonymous-to-account correlation.Denial without enumeration; no content persistence or leakage.
Resource abuseLong prompt, query fan-out, SSE reconnect storm, OTP abuse, expensive draft loop.Bounded work, idempotency, rate/cost control and no weakened legal gate.
Supply chainTampered model, corpus/rule/offline manifest, dependency or image digest.Signature/digest failure; promotion blocked and incident recorded.
Operational coercionProvider down, reranker down, partial corpus, DB race, audit writer failure.Declared degradation or no release; never silent threshold or verifier removal.

Map security cases to the current OWASP GenAI/LLM and API risk catalogues, but retain project-specific identifiers because legal-source poisoning, authority inversion and limitation errors are not adequately expressed as generic application vulnerabilities.

§13Statistics
& decision

Make uncertainty visible; predeclare how a candidate wins

A point estimate from 100 related questions is not proof. Release comparisons are paired by scenario cluster, use confidence intervals, preserve the incumbent baseline and separate hard safety constraints from non-inferiority and improvement claims.

Decision classRuleReporting
Hard safetyZero observed critical events and all architectural invariants pass.State sample count and the one-sided uncertainty bound; zero observed is not zero risk.
Absolute floorCandidate clears the inherited threshold overall and every declared sufficiently powered slice.Cluster bootstrap 95% interval; numerator/denominator; missing/invalid cases.
Non-inferiorityLower confidence bound for paired candidate−production delta stays above a predeclared negative margin.Margin justified before running the locked set; use paired binary tests for critical categorical outcomes.
ImprovementClaim only when the paired confidence interval excludes no change in the favourable direction.No cherry-picked best run; all preregistered primary endpoints shown.
CalibrationThreshold fixed on calibration partition; locked set estimates performance once.Reliability plot, ECE/Brier, risk–coverage and group sample sizes.
Multiple runsProvider/generative evaluations use fixed request artifacts and enough repeated runs only for declared variance questions.Snapshot, temperature, seed where supported and retry/failure policy.

Use cluster bootstrap over base scenarios, not utterance rows. Record the family key and preserve paired failures for diagnosis. The classic rule-of-three upper bound is reported when zero failures are seen; it prevents a ten-case slice from being described as risk-free.

§14System
quality

Correct under load, failure, recovery and constrained devices

ISO/IEC 25010 supplies a useful product-quality vocabulary; this architecture supplies the concrete legal-system measures. Performance tests preserve the same verification and abstention policy as ordinary traffic.

PropertyTest profileGate
LatencyCold/warm cache; exact citation, search, answer, calculator, SSE reconnect; p50/p95/p99 by language and degradation.Inherited budgets; no verifier or gate skipped to pass.
CapacityArrival bursts, slow SSE readers, DB pool exhaustion, worker queue age, provider rate limits and object-store latency.Bounded queues and admission; no cross-request scope or artifact mix.
ReliabilityCrash before/after transaction, duplicate delivery, lease expiry, poison job, corpus publish race and idempotent retry.Exactly-once legal effect where promised; at-least-once work produces one outcome.
DegradationLLM, reranker, inference, object store and audit writer independently unavailable.Only documented capability remains; no silent quality downgrade.
PrivacyAnonymous graph enumeration, logs/traces/provider payloads, RLS, export/delete, backup expiry and support access.Zero anonymous content persistence; no unnecessary sensitive field crosses a port.
SecurityAPI authorization matrix, prompt/source injection, dependency/image/model/pack integrity and secrets scanning.No known critical vulnerability or unmitigated high-risk finding in the release scope.
RecoverabilityMonthly restore, rollback application/corpus/rule/pack independently, revoked manifest and disaster runbook.Recovery objective met and golden set passes restored state.
CostTokens, provider calls, CPU, queue, storage and egress per verified completion/abstention.Average answer and monthly pilot ceiling; p95 cost reported to expose tails.
§15Change
qualification

Every mutable source of behaviour has a qualification key

A provider alias, prompt, parser, taxonomy or legal rule can change the answer without changing application code. The candidate manifest therefore names every behaviour-bearing artifact and computes the smallest sufficient test plan from its dependency graph.

  lexicalEngine; embeddingModel; vectorEncoding; indexDigest; reranker;
  gateModel; gateThresholds; promptArtifact; providerSnapshot; verifierModels[];
  ruleManifest; rendererDigest; openApiDigest; clientBuild; packManifest;
  evaluationDataset; metricCodeDigest; redteamVersion; environment;
}

Embedding/index/reranker/fusionAll retrieval strata, exact shadow, gate calibration, end-to-end, latency/cost and bilingual parity.
