Third-party provider/model snapshots are production dependencies, not interchangeable commodities. A silent vendor alias change is rejected. Failover may route only to a separately qualified pinned snapshot; if none exists, the system degrades as specified.

§16CI/CD
& release

Fast evidence on commits; strong evidence before exposure

The complete benchmark is too valuable and too slow for every edit. A tiered pipeline gives engineers rapid causal feedback while protecting locked labels and reserving human review for meaningful candidates.

CadenceRequired gatesBudget
Per commitFormatting/types, imports, unit/property/mutation subset, schema/contracts, 50-case development smoke, invariant and red-team smoke.Target ≤15 minutes; deterministic fake provider.
NightlyFull fit set, golden PDFs, component ablations, security scan, failure injection and representative load.May use qualified provider; exact cost recorded.
CandidateCalibration once, threshold freeze, complete manifest, data/metric leakage checks.No repeated threshold shopping.
ReleaseLocked paired run, critical ledger, all slices, manual legal review, privacy/security and restore/rollback evidence.Blocks promotion; signed card retained.
MilestoneSealed challenge set, independent red team and broader user study.Before public scope expansion or major provider/model family change.
§17Production
& challenge

Monitor decisions without building a surveillance corpus

Offline evaluation estimates known risk; production detects changed conditions. Content-free telemetry is the default. Authenticated sampling of legal content requires a disclosed purpose, strict role, redaction and retention; anonymous content is never persisted for evaluation.

SignalSliceTrigger / action
Corpus currencyOfficial source and jurisdiction.Missed schedule/fetch, changed source format or stale coverage → limit affected scope.
Retrieval/gateIntent, language, jurisdiction, date mode and degradation.Score, abstention or reason-distribution drift → shadow exact and reviewed sample.
VerificationRisk class, language, provider snapshot and claim type.Pass/drop/veto shift → halt changed route or provider.
ChallengesError taxonomy, source, legal domain and severity.Critical allegation → immediate quarantine, evidence preservation and legal triage.
SystemPath, version, cache, worker and device tier.SLO/cost/queue or signed-pack failure → documented degradation or rollback.
Fairness/accessLanguage and declared jurisdiction; no sensitive inference.Persistent disparity → scoped investigation and user research, not threshold manipulation.

17.1Challenge becomes a controlled regression

§18Evidence
& reports

A release card is a signed argument for a bounded claim

Every promotion produces a human-readable card and machine-readable manifest. The card states what was measured, what was not, how uncertain the result is, which failures occurred and precisely which product scope the evidence authorizes.

ReleaseCard {
  candidateManifestDigest; productionBaselineDigest; evaluationRunId;
  scope: { jurisdictions[]; sources[]; tasks[]; languages[]; exclusions[] };
  datasets: [{ id; version; split; digest; independentClusters }];
  metrics: [{ id; definitionVersion; value; interval; denominator; slices[] }];
  criticalEvents[]; regressions[]; improvements[]; invalidCases[];
  operational: { latency; availability; cost; privacy; security; recovery };
  limitations[]; residualRisks[]; requiredMonitoring[]; rollbackRef;
  decision: "pass" | "limited_scope" | "reject";
  signatures: [{ role; subject; signedAt; signature }];
}
SeverityExampleDisposition
S0 criticalFabricated/wrong authority released; deadline scalar wrong; cross-user disclosure; unsigned legal artifact accepted; invariant bypass.Reject/rollback immediately; preserve evidence; incident owner and regression required.
S1 highMaterial qualification omitted; binding status misstated but visible sources allow detection; anonymous content retained.Block release; legal/security review; no ordinary waiver.
S2 materialThreshold miss in one adequately powered non-critical slice; major accessibility task blocked.Block or explicit limited scope with matching product control.
S3 moderateNon-material ranking or wording regression; operational budget near limit.Owner, due date and monitored waiver with expiry.
S4 observationExploratory small-slice signal or cosmetic defect.Backlog with evidence; never counted as a pass.

Evidence artifacts are content-addressed and access-audited. Public-source fixtures can be retained with their provenance. User-derived legal-sensitive evidence follows Document 07’s lifecycle, purpose and deletion controls. Reports contain redacted exemplars; raw confidential content is never attached to a broadly readable CI artifact.

§19Delivery
contract

Build the measurement spine before tuning the system

PhaseDeliverableCannot advance until
E0Metric registry, artifact manifest, deterministic runner, report schema and 50-case development smoke.Same inputs reproduce identical deterministic rows; metric tests match hand calculations.
E1Golden PDF/tree suite, temporal fixtures, corpus publication and restore gates.QA-4/QA-5 floors and deterministic corpus rebuild pass.
E2golden-pk-v1 500 scenarios, frozen family split, annotation handbook and adjudication tool.Stable source identities, leakage audit, agreement report and legal sign-off.
E3Retrieval/gate metrics, ablations, calibration and exact-search shadow.QA-2/QA-3/QA-6 pass overall and by declared supported slice.
E4Oracle/end-to-end generation, domain mutation suites and legal register red team.QA-1/QA-13 and critical domain gates pass.
E5API/client/offline, privacy, security, load, recovery and signed release cards.QA-7–QA-12/QA-14 evidence exists and rollback is rehearsed.
E6Production drift, challenge quarantine, incident and controlled benchmark-growth workflow.Alerts, ownership, access controls and first challenge rehearsal complete.

19.1Executable ports

interface IEvaluationTarget {
  describe(): ArtifactManifest;
  run(case: EvalCase, mode: EvalMode): EvalObservation;
}

interface IMetric {
  definitionVersion: string;
  score(observations: EvalObservation[], labels: GoldLabels[]): MetricRows;
}

interface IReleaseGate {
  decide(candidate: RunManifest, baseline: RunManifest,
         policy: ReleasePolicy): ReleaseDecision;
}

19.2Definition of done

  • All five master invariants and QA-1 through QA-14 map to executable tests, named owners and evidence artifacts.
  • The 500-scenario Pakistan benchmark is source-grounded, family-split, bilingual/Roman-Urdu capable, lawyer-adjudicated and content-addressed.
  • Corpus, retrieval, oracle generation, end-to-end, domain, backend, client, offline, security and operations suites can run independently and together.
  • Critical events cannot be averaged, retried away or waived; limited scope is mechanically reflected in backend capability and client coverage.
  • Every candidate is paired with the current production baseline and reports denominators, uncertainty, slices, invalid cases, latency and cost.
  • Anonymous content is not persisted for evaluation. Production feedback enters quarantine and cannot silently contaminate locked tests or training.
  • A signed release card, rollback reference and responsible legal/technical/security approvals exist before pilot exposure.
RAuthorities
& research

Primary authority, standards and research basis

Pakistani sources establish the legal and institutional posture. International standards and research supply evaluation methods, not Pakistani law. Recent preprints are identified as supporting evidence rather than normative authority.

  1. Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan — current consolidated official text; Article 14 informs dignity and privacy risk. National Assembly official PDF.
  2. Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 — documentary and modern-device/electronic-system evidence; provenance controls do not predetermine admissibility. Pakistan Code official PDF.
  3. Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 — current Pakistan Code access copy used for security, unauthorized-access and incident-risk posture; it is not treated as a general data-retention code. Ministry of Law and Justice official PDF.
  4. Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002 — electronic document, communication, signature and integrity framework; a signed evaluation artifact does not by itself decide admissibility or professional approval. Pakistan Code official PDF.
  5. Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Rules, 1976 — professional conduct including rule 146 on confidential client information. Pakistan Bar Council official PDF; official catalogue.
  6. Personal Data Protection Bill, May 2023 — the Ministry register identifies it as a draft; used for forward-compatible policy, not claimed as enacted law. MOITT official status register; official draft PDF.
  7. National Guidelines for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Judicial Institutions of Pakistan — assistive, human-centric, transparent, accountable and privacy-protecting benchmark. LJCP official guidelines PDF; official release; NJPMC adoption record.
  8. NIST AI Risk Management Framework and AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile — risk-based testing, evaluation, verification, validation, confabulation, information integrity, privacy and incident controls. NIST AI Resource Center; official profile PDF.
  9. NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework 1.1 — secure development, provenance and vulnerability prevention practices. NIST official PDF.
  10. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — AI management-system requirements and continual Plan–Do–Check–Act governance. ISO official overview.
  11. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 — current product-quality model for specifying and evaluating ICT/software quality. ISO official overview.
  12. WCAG 2.2 — testable accessibility criteria, used at AA while retaining human usability evaluation. W3C Recommendation.
  13. OWASP GenAI/LLM Top 10 2026 and API Security Top 10 2023 — prompt injection, sensitive disclosure, supply chain, overreliance, authorization and resource-consumption threats. OWASP GenAI project; OWASP API project.
  14. LegalBench-RAG — expert-annotated, fine-grained legal retrieval benchmark; methodological precedent, not a substitute for Pakistani law. Pipitone & Alami, 2024; official code.
  15. Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools — preregistered evidence that proprietary legal RAG still produces material errors, supporting measured rather than absolute safety claims. Magesh et al., 2024.
  16. Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models — Attributable to Identified Sources (AIS) human evaluation framework. Rashkin et al., 2023.
  17. Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks and The Art of Abstention — risk–coverage evaluation for systems that may refuse. Geifman & El-Yaniv, 2017; Xin et al., 2021.
  18. BEIR and MIRACL — heterogeneous and multilingual retrieval evaluation methodology; neither supplies Pakistani Urdu legal validation. BEIR paper; MIRACL paper.
  19. The ML Test Score — production-readiness rubric linking model, data, infrastructure and monitoring tests. Google Research publication.
  20. OpenTelemetry semantic conventions — versioned telemetry vocabulary and explicit sensitive-data caution. Official specification.
  21. Local specification evidence — 01, 02, 03, 03a, 03b, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09a and 09b.

Part 11 — Security and Privacy

11Cross-cutting

Security and Privacy

A threat-driven, privacy-minimising security architecture for Pakistani legal intelligence: capability separation, matter isolation, verifiable legal evidence, constrained AI, recoverable operations and an auditable account of every privileged act.

Version 1.0Date 30 Aug 2026Scope L1–L7 + people + suppliersProvides security policy · threat model · control contracts · incident systemRequires Docs 02–10Figures 3
↑ Contents
§0Mandate
& invariants

Security is an architectural property, not a gateway in front of an unsafe system

Document 11 owns confidentiality, integrity, availability and privacy across the platform. It narrows implementation choices in every earlier document. If a convenience conflicts with an invariant here, the invariant wins and the release gate in Document 10 blocks shipment.

InvariantEnforced propertyProof required
SEC-1Anonymous requests have no account, matter, transcript, artefact, analytics event or content-bearing log writer.Composition-root test, database diff, object-store diff, provider-payload capture and log scan all show zero content persistence.
SEC-2Every authenticated object access is authorised by actor, role, matter, object and current workflow state; PostgreSQL RLS is a second boundary.Cross-user matrix, direct-ID adversaries and forced-RLS database tests produce zero disclosure.
SEC-3Retrieved law is untrusted DATA_ONLY. Models have no network, database, tool, secret, publication or signing capability.Prompt-injection suite cannot cross a port boundary or produce a privileged side effect.
SEC-4Only approved immutable source bytes can become published legal evidence; citation handles resolve server-side.Digest, provenance, maker-checker and signed-manifest chain validates from source to client.
SEC-5Secrets, credentials, legal-sensitive content and raw queries never enter URLs, ordinary logs, crash reports, metrics or training data.Schema allowlists, redaction canaries and storage scans pass before release.
SEC-6Privileged acts require named people, least privilege, separation of duties and audit-before-effect where risk demands it.Role graph proves no author can self-approve corpus, rule, model, offline pack or production release.
SEC-7Failure is closed: no model-only answer after retrieval failure; no unsigned pack; no stale authority after revocation; no silent security degradation.Fault injection exercises each forbidden fallback.
SEC-8Security evidence is itself restricted, minimised and access-audited.Audit readers are separate roles; exported evidence is scoped, encrypted and time-limited.

Legal boundary

This is an engineering specification, not a claim of statutory certification or legal advice. Controls are chosen from enacted Pakistani law, official policy/guidance and international standards, with their status kept distinct. Product policy may deliberately exceed a current legal minimum.

§1Pakistani
authority

State what binds, what guides and what remains a draft

The compliance register stores jurisdiction, instrument, provision, status, commencement, applicability rationale, owner and review date. A lawyer approves applicability; a URL or policy title alone never becomes a product obligation.

AuthorityStatus at this document dateUse in this architectureClaim explicitly rejected
Constitution, Art. 14Enacted constitutional protection concerning dignity and privacy of the home.Public-interest basis for minimisation and confidentiality.Not described as a complete private-sector data-protection code.
PECA 2016Enacted cybercrime statute; current text must be checked on Pakistan Code.Unauthorised access/interference, systems and electronic evidence enter the threat and incident register.Not treated as a general consent, retention or privacy schedule.
ETO 2002 + QSO 1984Enacted electronic-transactions and evidence frameworks.Reliable bytes, signatures, hashes, clocks, custody and reproducible records.A hash, log or electronic signature does not by itself guarantee validity or admissibility.
PBC Rules 1976, r.146Professional conduct rule concerning advocates and confidential client communications.Matter isolation, restricted reviewer access and no undisclosed reuse.Using the platform alone does not create advocate–client privilege or make the product an advocate.
National Cyber Security Policy 2021Approved federal policy.Governance and resilience benchmark; applicability is recorded per control.Not asserted to impose every listed control directly on this private pilot.
CERT Rules 2023Official Gazette rules with scope, coordination and commencement questions requiring counsel review.Incident-contact and preservation benchmark; determine whether notification/designation applies before launch.No automatic reporting duty is invented from a title alone.
MOITT PDP Bill, May 2023Draft on MOITT’s legislation page.Forward-compatible product policy for purpose, minimisation, user control and processors.Draft clauses are not represented as enacted law.
LJCP AI Guidelines 2026Official guidance adopted for judicial institutions.Human-centric, assistive, transparent, privacy-aware benchmark.Not misrepresented as a statute binding this private service.

The legal lead reviews this register quarterly and on any gazette, court ruling, regulator/CERT notice or product-scope change. “Compliant” may appear publicly only with a named framework, version, scope, assessor and evidence date.

§2Governance
& risk

One risk register connects public harm to an accountable control owner

Governance follows NIST CSF 2.0’s Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions. Threat modelling combines STRIDE for system failures with privacy/harm analysis: dignity, chilling effects, exposure of family or criminal matters, economic loss, professional prejudice and exclusion caused by language or access.

DecisionAccountableRequired independence
Risk acceptanceNamed service owner; legal/security co-sign for high or critical riskExpiry date, compensating control and affected scope required; no acceptance of SEC-1–SEC-8 violations.
Security architectureSecurity ownerChange author cannot approve own threat-model closure.
Privacy purpose/retentionProduct owner + privacy/legal ownerSecurity cannot expand collection “for possible future use”.
Production privilegeOperations ownerJust-in-time grant, ticket, MFA, recording and post-use review.
Incident commandIncident commanderEvidence custodian and public/legal decision maker are separately named.
ReleaseEngineering, legal, evaluation and security signatoriesDocument 10 critical gates cannot be waived into green.

Every feature carries: data-flow change, abuse cases, data classes, purpose, processors, retention/deletion behaviour, authz rules, logging schema, incident signals and test evidence. High-risk changes—identity recovery, provider transfer, legal drafting, bulk export, staff tooling, new corpus sources—require threat-model review before implementation.

§3Data
classification

Classification travels with every derivative, not merely the source row

ClassExamplesDefault handling
PUBLIC-LEGALOfficial statutes, judgments, gazettes; published corpus metadata.Public read after integrity gates. Publication writers remain privileged.
ACCOUNTVerified phone, settings, device/session data.Encrypted transport/storage; user-only; support sees masked fields by default.
LEGAL-SENSITIVEQueries tied to a person, matter facts, drafts, notes, uploads, saved answers.Need-to-know matter isolation, envelope encryption, no analytics/training reuse, explicit lifecycle.
AUDIT-RESTRICTEDPrivileged-event ledger, incident evidence, access decisions.Append-oriented, tamper-evident, separate reader role; no routine support access.
OPERATIONALLatency, counts, coarse error code, version IDs.Strict allowlist; no content or stable cross-context identifier.
SECRETSigning/encryption keys, tokens, recovery codes, credentials.Secret manager or protected runtime files; never DB/log/source/image; rotation and access alerting.
EPHEMERALAnonymous query/context/provider response and transient voice buffer.Memory/request scope only; no durable identifier; disposal on completion/timeout.

Derived chunks, embeddings, caches, exports and backups inherit the highest source class and purpose. A deletion tombstone identifies an internal object without retaining deleted content. Public law combined with a user’s query becomes legal-sensitive because the association can reveal intent.

§4Threat
model

Protect people, legal effect and the evidence chain

Threat actor / failureHigh-value abuse casePrimary controls
Unauthenticated attackerAccount enumeration, credential stuffing, resource exhaustion, injection.Uniform responses, throttling, proof-of-work/risk challenge where justified, schema limits, budgets.
Authenticated malicious userGuess object IDs, retrieve another matter, poison shared corpus, forge professional status.Object authz + RLS, non-public ingestion, verification state separated from identity.
Insider/support operatorSearch sensitive matters, export logs, alter audit or publish unsafe rules.Masked-by-default tooling, JIT access, dual control, purpose ticket, access alerts.
Compromised source/providerPoison corpus; inject instructions; retain prompts; forge citations.Official allowlist, immutable hashes, sandbox, DATA_ONLY boundary, server resolver, contract + payload tests.
Supply-chain attackerMalicious dependency/image/model/update or stolen signing key.Lockfiles, SBOM, provenance, signatures, isolated builders, key separation and rapid revocation.
Operational accidentPublic backup, verbose log, wrong migration/RLS, stale pack, failed deletion.Safe defaults, policy tests, restore drills, scanners, canaries and release gates.
§5Privacy
lifecycle

Purpose limits the data before encryption protects it

Each field must have a named product purpose, class, lawful/applicability rationale approved by counsel, allowed readers/processors, deletion trigger and maximum retention. “Improve AI”, “analytics” and “security” are not sufficient purposes without a specific use and necessity test.

StateRequired behaviourForbidden shortcut
CollectJust-in-time notice in English/Urdu; collect the minimum; separate optional improvement consent.Bundled consent or pre-ticked training reuse.
UsePolicy check binds purpose and matter; provider sees request-local pseudonym only.Using legal matters for general model training or staff curiosity.
StoreLegal-sensitive content encrypted; metadata minimised; user-facing retention state.Raw query in path, URL, metric label or exception.
ShareExplicit recipient/scope; short-lived signed export; disclosure event audited.Public bearer link or silent support/provider access.
DeleteActive row/object/cache/index removal, wrapped-key destruction, tombstone and backup expiry.Deleting UI row while embeddings, cache or export remain searchable.
RecoverBackups retained for inherited 14-day recovery window; restored data re-enters deletion queue before service.Restoring deleted content into active user access.

Only the inherited operational-log and backup windows are fixed here: content-free operational logs up to 14 days and recovery backups up to 14 days. Account, matter, draft and audit schedules require a separately approved retention register before production. Legal hold is exceptional, scoped, documented, access-restricted and removed when its basis ends.

5.1User control

Authenticated users can view stored categories, export their matter in a documented format, correct account data, delete individual artefacts or the account, withdraw optional reuse, and see pending/complete deletion. Identity verification for a request must be proportionate; support cannot ask for the very sensitive facts being protected. These are product commitments and forward-compatible privacy engineering, not a claim that the draft PDP Bill is enacted.

§6Anonymous
proof

Anonymous means technically unable to remember

buildAnonymousGraph() {
  return QueryApp(
    corpus = PublishedCorpusReadPort,
    retrieval = EphemeralRetrievalPort,
    generation = MinimisingProviderPort,
    clock = MonotonicClock,
    telemetry = ContentFreeMetricsPort,
    accounts = ABSENT, matters = ABSENT, artifacts = ABSENT,
    transcripts = ABSENT, objects = ABSENT, auditContent = ABSENT);
}
  • No stable browser/device identifier, fingerprint or cross-request correlation. Security rate limits use short-lived, coarse, rotating signals.
  • Reverse proxy excludes query strings and bodies; application errors carry a random request ID only.
  • Provider contracts/configuration prohibit training and retained prompts where the selected service supports it; payload conformance is tested.
  • Memory buffers expire on completion, cancellation or timeout. Swapping, core dumps and content-bearing crash capture are disabled for workers.
  • Voice is processed request-locally; anonymous voice is disabled if that cannot be guaranteed.

The proof is a five-surface diff—database, objects, queues/caches, telemetry and provider capture—before and after canary requests, plus a dependency-graph assertion that no persistence adapter is reachable.

§7Identity
& access

Possession, identity and professional authority are separate facts

ConcernDesignFailure prevented
Citizen sign-inOTP proves current control of a number; risk-based reauthentication for export/delete/share.Calling a recycled/SIM-swapped number verified identity.
SessionShort-lived access token; rotating, replay-detected refresh family; device view/revocation; tokens hashed at rest.Long-lived bearer theft and undetected refresh replay.
StaffPhishing-resistant passkeys/security keys, managed account, no shared login, JIT role.OTP phishing and unaccountable privileged work.
Professional statusSeparate effective-dated verification record and evidence; expiry/revocation changes capabilities.Phone possession or profile text becoming lawyer authority.
RecoveryRisk-delayed workflow, out-of-band notice, active-session revocation and sensitive-action cooldown.Support-assisted takeover.

OAuth/OIDC implementations follow RFC 9700: exact redirect matching, PKCE, issuer/audience validation, no implicit-flow design, sender constraint where practical, and refresh-token rotation. Passwords, if ever introduced, use a maintained Argon2id library and parameters benchmarked to the deployment; home-grown cryptography is prohibited.

§8Authorisation
& RLS

Authorise the object and workflow state, then make the database disagree by default

  • Opaque IDs reduce guessing but never replace authorisation. Every read, mutation, export, share, citation artefact and stream reconnect checks ownership/membership.
  • Sensitive tables use ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, explicit USING/WITH CHECK, default deny, non-owner runtime roles and migration tests.
  • Background jobs carry a signed scope envelope; there is no generic “system user”. Bulk/admin roles are separate, time-bound and audited.
  • Support starts metadata-only. Unmasking content needs user-approved support where possible or an incident/legal basis, JIT grant, reason and notification policy.
§9Cryptography
& keys

Keys express boundaries and make deletion operational

SurfaceRequired primitive/patternKey rule
NetworkTLS 1.3 preferred; TLS 1.2 only with an explicit compatibility profile; HSTS externally.Automated certificate renewal and expiry alert.
Legal-sensitive fields/objectsVersioned authenticated encryption (AEAD) with envelope encryption and context-bound associated data.Per-user or per-matter DEK; wrapped by environment KEK kept outside DB/object store.
Passwords if introducedArgon2id through a maintained library.Per-record salt; optional pepper held separately; rehash on successful sign-in.
TokensAt least 128 bits CSPRNG entropy; store one-way digest where lookup is needed.Purpose, audience and expiry bound; immediate family revocation on replay.
Corpus/offline/releaseEd25519 detached signature over canonical manifest; SHA-256 content digests.Separate offline root, release signer and online service keys; clients pin trusted public keys.
MobileOS Keychain/Keystore-backed non-exportable key where available.No secrets in preferences, logs, source, bundle or shared clipboard.

Every ciphertext records algorithm suite, key ID/version, nonce, associated-data schema and creation time. Rotation supports dual-read/single-write then measured rewrap. Destruction of a user/matter DEK wrapper provides crypto-erasure for encrypted backup copies while active rows/objects/derivatives are deleted; backup expiry completes physical retirement. This is a product design, not a statutory claim.

Pilot practicality

The pilot may use an OS-protected offline KEK service with tightly permissioned runtime identity, encrypted off-box recovery and dual-control rotation. Moving to a managed KMS/HSM is triggered by multi-host deployment, regulated-customer requirement, key-operator scale or inability to meet recovery/rotation evidence—not by fashion.

§10AI & RAG
security

The model can propose language; it cannot obtain authority

AttackPreventive boundaryDetection / response
Indirect prompt injectionRetrieved blocks are delimited, typed DATA_ONLY, normalised/scanned; post-context instruction; no tools.Injection canaries, model/version-specific adversarial eval; abstain on policy conflict.
Corpus poisoningOfficial-source allowlist, immutable bytes, sandbox extraction, provenance, maker-checker publish.Hash/index drift alert; quarantine revision and roll back signed manifest.
Sensitive disclosurePre-provider minimisation/redaction, matter-scoped retrieval, no memory, output DLP/schema checks.Cross-user canaries and egress capture; revoke provider/version on failure.
Forged citationModel may emit only opaque supplied handles; server resolves exact L2 identity/bytes.Unresolvable/unsupported handle rejects artifact; never repair with guessed citation text.
Model denial-of-serviceInput, retrieval, token, concurrency and spend budgets; cancellation and circuit breaker.Per-route saturation signal; degrade to deterministic lookup, never unsafe model-only mode.
Unsafe legal outputStructured response contract, deterministic legal/verdict validators and risk register.Advice-register red team; withhold/clarify/professional-review state.

10.1Provider qualification

The registry records service/region, subprocessors, retention/training settings, transfer path, deletion behaviour, abuse-monitoring exception, encryption, breach terms, availability, model/version pinning and audit evidence. Payload tests prove configuration rather than trusting marketing. The provider receives request-local pseudonyms, minimum facts, approved evidence and no user phone/account/matter ID. A provider change is a security, privacy and evaluation release.

§11Legal evidence
integrity

A hostile PDF never becomes executable authority

  1. Fetch only approved official HTTPS origins, enforce redirect/size/type limits, record headers and hash raw bytes before parsing.
  2. Quarantine and scan; parse/OCR in an unprivileged, networkless sandbox with CPU, memory, time and output limits. File extension never establishes type.
  3. Preserve immutable raw evidence and extractor/model/container versions. Normalised text remains linked to page coordinates and raw hash.
  4. Run coverage, structure, temporal and legal-relation gates. High-risk schedules and status-changing relations require legal maker-checker review.
  5. Publish atomically from a dedicated role; application/model roles have no index write. Sign canonical corpus/offline manifests and retain rollback.
  6. Continuously compare source and published digests. Deletion/revocation cascades to chunks, embeddings, caches and packs.

Hashes and signatures prove byte relationships and signer control; they do not prove that the source is legally operative, current, correctly interpreted or admissible. Those are separate temporal, authority and legal-review findings.

§12API, web
& mobile

Use verification standards as test catalogues, then bind them to this product

SurfaceMinimum control profile
HTTP/APITyped allowlist schemas; body/depth/item limits; parameterised SQL; safe error codes; security headers; strict CORS; CSRF protection for cookie authority; SSRF-safe egress; per-actor/resource budgets; idempotency bound to actor+route+body digest.
StreamingAuthorise before and during SSE reconnect; short-lived cursor bound to actor/artifact; buffer contains no secret; cancellation stops provider work.
Uploads/exportsMagic-byte validation, quarantine/sandbox, random server names, no active serving, malware/parser checks; exports encrypted or short-lived, single-scope and access-audited.
WebContextual output encoding, restrictive CSP, no query content in URL/history/referrer, secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies where used, dependency integrity and frame protection.
MobileOWASP MASVS-informed secure storage, transport, platform and resilience profile; universal/app links allowlisted; backup exclusion; release builds disable debug logging.
Offline packsCanonical signed manifest, schema/app compatibility, anti-rollback version, atomic install, last-known-good pack and zero private user data.

ASVS 5.0.0, OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023), MASVS and the OWASP RAG guidance are verification sources, not certification claims. The requirement traceability matrix maps each applicable item to code, test or documented non-applicability.

§13Platform
& supply chain

The single-VPS pilot is small, not trusted

  • Default-deny host firewall; public exposure limited to reverse proxy; SSH keys only, no root login, restricted administration source where practical; PostgreSQL/cache/object services bind private/localhost interfaces.
  • Separate non-root service identities, read-only images/filesystems where practical, dropped capabilities, resource limits, health checks and no Docker socket in application containers.
  • Secrets arrive at runtime with least-readable permissions, never baked into image or Git. Startup fails on placeholder/overbroad secrets; access and rotation are audited.
  • Security patch policy is risk-based: internet-exploitable critical exposure has an owner and emergency window; every exception expires. Time sync, disk/backup capacity and certificate/key expiry alert before failure.
  • Encrypted off-box backups, 14-day recovery window, monthly scratch restore and golden evaluation. Restore credentials are separate from production; deletion queues run before a restored service opens.

13.1Software, model and data supply chain

Every release has lockfiles, dependency and container/model/corpus digests, SBOM, vulnerability and secret scans, licence inventory, test evidence and signed provenance. CI uses ephemeral least-privilege credentials; untrusted pull-request code cannot access release secrets. Images are pinned by digest; mutable tags do not deploy. SLSA 1.2 supplies the provenance vocabulary, while NIST SSDF 1.1 structures secure development. Conformance levels are not claimed unless independently evidenced.

§14Audit &
telemetry

Three evidence streams have different purposes and readers

StreamContainsMust not contain
Operational telemetryRoute template, coarse outcome, latency, status family, version IDs, random request ID.Query/body, names, phones, tokens, matter/object IDs, citation text, model prompt/response.
Security auditUTC event time, actor/session class, action, protected object type+pseudonymous ID, decision/reason, before/after digests, request/change ticket, key/version.Whole document or legal narrative unless a separately protected incident bundle requires it.
Legal replayAuthenticated artefact graph defined in Docs 04–07: scoped inputs/evidence/prompt/provider bytes/verdicts/digests.Anonymous sessions; unrelated account identity; hidden provider/tool data.

Audit events are appended through a narrow service role and chained/batched with digests; signed checkpoints are stored separately. This makes unauthorised alteration detectable, not metaphysically “immutable”. Reads, searches, exports, retention changes and audit-policy changes are audited. Clocks synchronise to UTC and retain source/uncertainty. Operational logs expire within 14 days; audit/legal replay retention comes from the approved register.

§15Detection &
response

Preserve truth while stopping harm

SeverityExampleInternal target
S0Confirmed cross-user disclosure; signing/KEK compromise; active corpus/rule poisoning; anonymous persistence at scale.Acknowledge ≤15 min, commander ≤30 min, containment starts immediately; release/affected feature stopped.
S1Likely sensitive exposure, privileged compromise, material integrity/availability loss.Acknowledge ≤30 min, command ≤60 min, executive/legal/security engaged.
S2Contained vulnerability or limited event without confirmed sensitive impact.Owner same business day; timed remediation and monitoring.
S3Low-risk policy drift or suspicious event.Backlog with owner, due date and recurrence signal.

Runbooks cover account takeover, staff credential, database/object exposure, provider disclosure, corpus poisoning, rule/model regression, signing key, ransomware/destructive loss, DDoS and lost device. Evidence records who collected what, when, from where, by which tool/hash and every transfer. Counsel decides PECA/CERT/contract/reporting applicability from current official text; the CERT Rules are not treated as a universal automatic duty without that assessment.

§16Secure
delivery

Every boundary has an executable negative proof

GateRequired evidenceBlocker
DesignData flow, threat/harm model, abuse cases, purpose/retention and control owner.Unclassified data or unowned high risk.
Code reviewTwo-person review for auth, crypto, RLS, ingestion, signing, logging, provider and release code.Author self-approval or unreviewed generated code.
AutomatedUnit/property/fuzz, SAST, secret/dependency/image scans, IaC checks, SBOM and policy tests.Reachable critical/high finding without expiring risk decision.
AdversarialCross-tenant IDs/streams/exports, RLS pooling, CSRF/SSRF, uploads, prompt injection, poisoned source, forged handle, pack rollback, log canaries.Any SEC invariant failure or Doc 10 S0/S1 event.
OperationalRestore, key rotation/revocation, deletion, provider outage, audit checkpoint and incident tabletop.Recovery bypasses authz/deletion or cannot establish corpus/release integrity.
IndependentScoped penetration test before public production and after material boundary change; findings retested.Unresolved exploitable high-impact chain.

Production vulnerability reports enter a documented channel with safe-harbour language approved by counsel. Security tests use synthetic legal matters; production content is not copied into development. Findings become regression fixtures without retaining reporter or user content unnecessarily.

§17Delivery
& proof

Build the controls in dependency order

  1. Foundation: compliance/data registers, owners, threat model, secret handling, hardening baseline, approved sources/providers.
  2. Isolation: separate anonymous graph, account/matter schema, object authorisation, forced RLS, session/recovery and staff MFA.
  3. Evidence integrity: sandboxed ingestion, immutable provenance, signed publish/offline pipeline, model citation resolver.
  4. Privacy/crypto: field minimisation, envelope encryption, export/deletion, backup-aware crypto-erasure and provider egress conformance.
  5. Detection/recovery: allowlisted telemetry, restricted audit/checkpoints, alerts, incident runbooks, restore/key/deletion drills.
  6. Assurance: ASVS/API/MASVS/RAG traceability, Doc 10 adversaries, independent penetration test and signed production decision.

17.1Production definition of done

A production release is not done until all SEC invariants have automated evidence; all sensitive tables are enumerated and forced-RLS tested; anonymous five-surface proof passes; provider payloads and retention settings are captured; source/release/offline signatures verify; deletion and restore complete; secrets/keys rotate; incident contacts and applicability register are current; high-risk findings are closed; and Document 10’s security/privacy critical-event ledger is empty.

Part 12 — Design System

12Client craft

Design System

Pakistani judicial stamp paper is warm cream, printed in pine green, sealed in brass and numbered in oxide red. The whole palette was already sitting on the desk.

↑ Contents
01 — Direction

Warm, not corporate

Legal software defaults to navy, gold and a white page. It reads as institutional, and institutional is exactly the feeling that keeps people from asking a legal question in the first place.

What we took

The physical artefact. Judicial stamp paper carries a cream ground, a green-blue guilloche, an embossed seal and red serial numbering — four colours that already mean something in this jurisdiction, already sit together, and already read as authoritative without shouting.

What we left

The white page. A flat white background makes every card float in nothing and every screen read as a form. Parchment gives the interface a floor, so cards can be genuinely white and actually lift.

The rule that keeps it premium

Space is the luxury signal, not ornament. Every screen in §06 could hold twice the content and deliberately does not — a section of law given room to breathe reads as considered; the same section packed tight reads as a database dump. When in doubt, remove an element rather than shrink the gaps.

02 — Colour

Four colours and their quiet neighbours

One warm ground, one deep field, one metal, one alarm. Everything else is a neutral holding them apart.

#F3EFE6
Parchment
The floor. Warm enough that white cards read as paper laid on a desk rather than shapes on a void.
#17352E
Pine
Immersive surfaces — hero, sheets, the tab bar at rest. Deep enough to sit under brass without fighting it.
11.6:1 on parchment
#B8873C
Brass
The seal. Accents, active states, section numerals. Fill and large type only.
use #8A6216 for body text
#A0392C
Oxide
Serial-number red. Repealed, struck down, destructive. Reserved — never decorative.
5.9:1 on parchment
#FBF8F1
Card
Warm off-white. Lifts off parchment with almost no shadow, which is what keeps the surface calm.
#1A1F1C
Ink
Green-biased black. Pure black on parchment reads cold and slightly dirty.
14.6:1 on parchment

Dark is a different room, not the lights off

Inverting a warm palette produces mud. Instead the ground becomes pine-black, cream carries the text, and brass takes over as the primary accent — it lifts on dark far better than green does, so the identity survives the switch instead of going grey.

#121916
Ground
Pine pulled almost to black. Not neutral black — the hue is still there.
#1A2320
Surface
Cards lift by lightness. Shadows do almost nothing on a dark ground.
#D4A557
Brass, raised
Now the primary accent. Lightness up, chroma held.
5.9:1 on ground

Legal status has four values and no more

Colour never carries these alone. Every one ships with a mark and a word, because a colour-blind reader and a printed page both have to work.

StateMarkLightDarkRule
IN FORCE Seal#8A6216#D4A557 The only state that is not a warning. Brass, because it is the seal on a valid instrument.
REPEALED Cross#A0392C#E0897B Also struck down and invalidated. Cannot be collapsed by the reader.
NOT IN FORCE Dashed edge#5A625C#A8A79A Enacted, never commenced. A dashed border does the work — no third hue needed.
AMENDED None#5A625C#A8A79A Deliberately neutral. Amendment is ordinary; alarming the reader about it is noise.
03 — Type

Chrome is borrowed. Content is ours.

One decision carries the whole system. Navigation uses a face that gets out of the way; statutory text uses one with a voice, so law reads like law rather than like an app.

Aa
Spectral
Statutory text, headings, explanations. A transitional serif drawn for screens — warm, slightly narrow, and unmistakably a book face. Georgia falls back with close metrics.
Aa
Karla
Interface, labels, buttons, tab bar. A grotesque with just enough irregularity to feel drawn rather than generated. Never used for the text of a provision.
ا ب
Noto Nastaliq Urdu
Every Urdu run, chrome and content alike. There is no acceptable substitute, and no synthetic bold — emphasis comes from size and colour.

The scale, and its Nastaliq twin

Nastaliq runs larger with roughly double the leading. The two scales are chosen per run, by script — not per locale — because one sentence routinely contains both, and choosing by locale breaks on exactly that line.

RoleSpecimenLatinNastaliq
Display Specific Relief Act 44 / 1.0450 / 1.7
Provision heading 9. Suit by person dispossessed 20 / 1.323 / 1.85
Statutory body If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immoveable property… 17 / 1.6820 / 2.1
Interface label Trace precedent 15 / 1.418 / 1.9
Meta In force 1877-02-01 → present 12 / 1.4515 / 1.9

The citation island

This is where bilingual legal interfaces break, and the failure does not look like a typography bug — it looks like a citation to a different section.

Without isolation

قتلِ عمد 302–304 .s PPC کے تحت

Brackets, commas and the range dash take direction from context. Inside a right-to-left paragraph they resolve right-to-left and migrate to the wrong end.

First-strong isolates

قتلِ عمد s. 302–304 PPC کے تحت

Every foreign run wrapped in U+2068 … U+2069. Neutrals resolve inside the isolate; the citation stays one island. Isolates, never the deprecated embeddings.

Digits stay Western

Section numbers, article numbers, years in citations and case numbers use 0–9 in both scripts, always. A localised section number is a wrong citation. Only quantities in running prose may take Eastern Arabic-Indic forms, and only when the interface language is Urdu.

04 — Space & form

Room is the whole point

iOS does not feel calm because of its corner radii. It feels calm because it refuses to fill the screen. Density is the single easiest way to make this product feel like a database and the hardest thing to walk back.

Cramped

302. Punishment of qatl-i-amd
Penal Code 1860 · Ch. XVI · federal · in force
Whoever commits qatl-e-amd shall, subject to the provisions of this Chapter, be punished with death as qisas…
s.304s.31114 judgments

Everything fits. Nothing is readable, nothing is tappable, and the law looks like a search result.

Given room

302 Punishment of qatl-i-amd
Whoever commits qatl-e-amd shall, subject to the provisions of this Chapter, be punished with death as qisas…
IN FORCE·PENAL CODE 1860

Half the information, twice the confidence. The section numeral becomes the anchor and everything secondary steps back.

The measures

TokenValueWhere
Spacing base4 ptRamp: 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 · 32 · 44 · 64. Nothing between steps.
Screen gutter24 ptNever below 20. This alone separates premium from cramped on a phone.
Card padding24 pt20 on compact cards. Never 12 — that is the density trap.
Between cards16 ptEnough to read as separate objects rather than a table.
Touch target48 ptMinimum, with 8 pt of clear space. Applies to the citation chip too.
Radius10 · 14 · 20 · 28Chip · control · card · sheet. Continuous curvature where the platform offers it.
Elevation2 levelsCard and sheet. A third level means the hierarchy is wrong, not that a shadow is missing.
Reading measure38–44 chStatutory text on a phone. Longer lines are why legal apps feel exhausting.
05 — Components

Four of these are promises

The seal, the citation chip, the scope band and the disclaimer are not styling decisions. Each is the visible half of a guarantee the architecture makes — a redesign may restyle them; it may not remove them.

Buttons

Ask this question
Browse the Act
Read in Urdu
Report this answer

52 pt tall, not 44 — the minimum is a floor, not a target. The primary carries a one-pixel inner highlight and a shadow tinted with its own hue rather than grey, which is most of what separates a premium control from a coloured rectangle.

The seal

IN FORCE REPEALED NOT IN FORCE

A ribbon-seal mark rather than a tick. It borrows from the embossed seal on the paper itself, and it is the one place a small piece of ornament earns its keep — because it is doing semantic work.

s.9 Specific Relief Act partly supported

Citation chip. Takes a resolved citation object, never strings to join, so a fabricated section number has nowhere to come from. The full chip is the tap target, not the text inside it.

Bands and fields

The deadline

You have six months

Urgency without alarm. A limitation period is the most consequential thing on the screen, so it gets the pine field and the brass rather than a red banner — red is reserved for law that no longer exists.

The system, at rest

Four screens at true size. Note what is not on them: no dense metadata rows, no more than one primary action, and no fake status bar — on a device the real one renders on top.

07 — Motion & tokens

Springs, never ease-in-out

Linear and cubic easing is what makes a cross-platform app feel borrowed. Everything that moves here uses a spring, and almost nothing moves.

What this document is not

Part 13 — UX and Interaction Architecture

13Client craft

UX and Interaction Architecture

The behavioural architecture of Nizam-e-Qanoon: how people describe a problem, establish legal scope, inspect authority, understand uncertainty, complete a legal task and recover from failure—in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, online or offline.

Version 1.0Date 30 Aug 2026Scope citizen · professional · public · curatorProvides journeys · states · content · research · UX gatesRequires Docs 01–12Figures 4
↑ Contents
00 — Mandate

UX is the last legal-safety boundary

A correct database record can still become a dangerous product if the screen hides its date, collapses a qualification, presents a translation as authentic text, makes abstention look like failure, or lets a user mistake possession of a phone for verified professional identity.

UX invariantVisible contractRelease proof
UX-1Every legal conclusion exposes jurisdiction, asOf, source coverage and outcome state before reliance.Users can correctly state where, when and how qualified the result is.
UX-2A citation opens the exact database-resolved provision or judgment paragraph, with material context and official-source path.Zero model-authored citation string; source-finding task succeeds across scripts.
UX-3Deadline, liberty, immediate safety and irreversible-action information precedes explanatory doctrine.Critical information is noticed and correctly restated before participants continue.
UX-4Clarification and abstention are first-class destinations; neither is rendered as an error or quietly converted to an answer.Participants understand what is missing and what safe next action exists.
UX-5English, Urdu and Roman-Urdu input preserve the same legal scope, evidence, qualifications and action consequences.Meaning-level parity gates from Doc 10 pass; translation cannot alter legal force.
UX-6Anonymous and authenticated modes make their storage consequences explicit and never imply a capability the composition lacks.Users correctly predict what will be saved, shared and deletable.
UX-7Every core journey works with keyboard/screen reader, 200% zoom, reduced motion, low-end Android and its declared offline state.WCAG 2.2 AA process audit plus real-user task completion.
UX-8Generated prose, reviewed legal rule, official text and professional identity remain visibly distinct.No tested user attributes system prose to the State, court or advocate.

Relationship to Document 12

Document 12 owns the Stamp Paper visual language—tokens, typography, spacing, component appearance, status colours and motion. Document 13 owns information order, behaviour, states, comprehension, task safety and evidence. A redesign may restyle the system without weakening either contract.

01 — Pakistan context

Design for uneven access, not a fictional average user

The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics reports for 2024–25: literacy among people aged ten and above at 63%, individual internet use at 57%, mobile/smartphone ownership at 50%, and household internet use at 70%. These aggregates do not define an individual, but they rule out a text-heavy, always-online, smartphone-expert default.

Empirical consequence

  • Start from events in ordinary language, not legal taxonomy.
  • Keep the exact law available without forcing everyone to read it first.
  • Support assisted, shared-device and low-data contexts without exposing legal matters.
  • Make offline statutory lookup a declared mode, not a broken online screen.
  • Test by province, language, gender, disability, device and digital confidence; do not infer them.

Rights and public-interest basis

The ICT Rights of Persons with Disability Act 2020 addresses accessible websites and access to justice within its statutory scope. Articles 10A, 14, 19A and 25 of the Constitution inform fair process, dignity/privacy, access to information and equality. Applicability is a legal determination; the product nevertheless adopts inclusive access nationwide as its own design commitment.

The 2026 LJCP AI Guidelines govern judicial institutions rather than this private product, but their official human-centric, assistive, transparent and accountable posture is used as a public-interest benchmark. The interface never turns model output into a judicial decision or advocate’s opinion.

02 — People and harms

Model circumstances and capabilities, not decorative personas

ContextPrimary jobDangerous misunderstandingDesign response
Citizen, unknown legal vocabularyDescribe what happened and learn whether held law can help.Nearest semantic result is “their law”.Situation intake, scope clarification, material assumptions and typed abstention.
Person under urgencyFind a deadline, safety action, forum or legal-aid route.Calm prose means there is time; calculator result is guaranteed.Urgency band first, explicit basis, step trace, uncertainty and referral.
Citation-led readerOpen an Act/section/judgment directly.Printed text is necessarily current and operative.Deterministic fast path, status/as-of banner and version comparison.
Advocate/researcherInvestigate authority, history, treatment and contrary material.Similarity or missing negative treatment proves “good law”.Evidence graph, coverage statement, majority/dissent and treatment reasons.
Drafting userTurn supplied facts into a reviewable document.Generated wording is filed-ready or advocate-approved.Fact/assumption/clause separation, provenance, missing-field gate and draft watermark.
Low literacy / low digital confidenceUnderstand one next step without navigating legal structure.Icon, colour or jargon is self-explanatory.Plain speech, one idea at a time, words with marks, audio and supported decision-making.
Disabled or older userComplete the same task with chosen assistive strategy.A technically present alternative is an equivalent experience.Semantic process, adaptable presentation and co-design with diverse users.
Curator/operatorReview evidence and publish a bounded corpus/rule change.Admin convenience permits self-approval or invisible effect.Desktop evidence workspace, maker-checker, impact preview and signed release state.

Research recruits by circumstance—language, task, disability, literacy, geography, device, connectivity and professional experience—without suggesting that one characteristic predicts another. Sensitive legal scenarios use fictional facts; participants never have to disclose an active matter to test the product.

03 — Information architecture

Three doors reflect three user intentions

“Saved matters” is a workspace, not a fourth discovery mode. “Account” holds identity, sessions, privacy and language. Public pages expose only the published legal corpus. The curation console is a separate staff product and never appears as a citizen navigation branch.

04 — Journey catalogue

Specify the whole task, including the unsafe exits

IDJourneySuccessRequired alternative
J-01Anonymous questionUnderstands bounded answer and verifies source without durable content.Clarification, abstention or deterministic lookup; sign-in offered only after result.
J-02Saved matterResumes a pinned answer with changed-law warning and replay provenance.Offline read of saved public source; never silently regenerate old answer.
J-03Exact citationCorrect unit opens under 50 ms with applicable version and official source.Disambiguation list; no nearest-section auto-selection.
J-04Guided situationOnly legally material facts collected; rules construct typed outcome.Unknown fact branch and professional-review route.
J-05Deadline/calculationResult, governing date, excluded days, jurisdiction and complete trace understood.Range/unknown state; no false single date.
J-06Precedent investigationSees proposition, majority, treatment evidence, court/time and coverage.Conflict/coverage warning; no red/green “good law” shortcut.
J-07DraftingReviews facts, assumptions, clauses, sources and draft status before export.Missing-fact stop or lawyer review; model cannot select clause.
J-08Offline statuteFinds held provision with pack version/freshness and exact citation.“Not held offline” distinct from “law does not exist”.
J-09Privacy controlViews stored categories, exports, deletes and sees completion/pending state.Proportionate recovery and human support without requesting case narrative.
J-10Corpus/rule publicationReviewer compares source, derivation, impact and gates; separate publisher signs.Reject/quarantine with reason; never partially visible.

Each journey artefact contains entry/exit, roles, data classes, required facts, request/response schema, screens, focus and announcement behaviour, connectivity modes, state transitions, cancellation/resume, analytics allowlist, threat cases, legal fixtures and acceptance evidence.

05 — Question intake

Clarify only what can change the legal result

  • Never silently infer province, territory, forum or operative date from GPS, phone code, language or IP address.
  • Differentiate event dates: occurrence, notice, accrual, decision, filing and “law as at”.
  • Offer “I do not know”, approximate date and save-and-return where legally safe.
  • Repeat assumptions immediately above the answer; a material edit creates a new result, not a changed label.
  • When input contains immediate danger or a deadline, surface a bounded warning without pretending to assess emergency facts conclusively.
06 — Answer anatomy

Order information by harm, then by explanation

OrderBlockPurposeMust expose
01Outcome stateAnswer, conditional, clarify, abstain or professional review.Not a numeric confidence theatre.
02Immediate issueDeadline, liberty, safety, irreversible filing/payment.Basis, event date and uncertainty.
03Plain conclusionOne understandable proposition.Modality—may, must, cannot, depends.
04Scope cardPrevent wrong place/date/forum reliance.Jurisdiction, territory, forum, as-of, coverage.
05Material assumptionsShow which supplied/unknown facts drive the result.User fact versus system assumption.
06Law and reasoningExplain the trace without hiding exceptions.Atomic claims linked to evidence handles.
07Qualifications/conflictPreserve provisos, discretion, contrary authority and coverage gaps.Why it matters to the result.
08SourcesVerify exact primary evidence.Official path and precise cited span.
09Safe next stepsAction without unlicensed representation.Official service or qualified professional where appropriate.

The default citizen view is progressive disclosure, not information deletion. Material qualifications are never hidden behind “read more”. The professional view increases evidence density and tools, not legal certainty. The disclaimer is structural chrome, but it cannot cure misleading answer language.

The system should sound certain only when the evidence and applicable legal rule permit certainty.

07 — Sources and status

Let the reader inspect the proof without leaving the thought

Citation chip interaction

  1. Tap/activate opens the exact stable legal unit.
  2. The matched span is highlighted without stripping provisos or hierarchy.
  3. Header shows instrument/judgment, jurisdiction, status and effective date.
  4. Reader can open official source and page coordinates.
  5. History compares applicable text; it never overwrites the current reading silently.

Judgment evidence

  • Court, date, bench and opinion type
  • Proposition actually treated
  • Majority, separate and dissenting opinions
  • Applies, distinguishes, doubts, overrules or conflict evidence
  • Coverage and last checked date
  • No “good law” badge derived from similarity or missing edges
Legal stateReader-facing languageInteraction consequence
In force for scope/date“In force as at [date] for [jurisdiction].”May support a current-law result subject to other guards.
Amended“This text changed on [date]. You are viewing the version applicable on [as-of].”Offer structured diff; answer regenerates on date change.
Repealed / invalidated / spentName the distinct legal event and effective date.Historical view only unless savings/transition makes it relevant.
Not yet commenced“Published, but commencement for this provision is not established/as appointed.”Cannot support unconditional operative-law answer.
Unknown / disputedState exactly which fact or authority is unresolved.Clarify, show competing evidence or abstain.

Changing asOf is a new legal query pinned through L3–L6; it cannot merely swap the banner. Public URLs remain stable provision identities and place the date in state/query controls without leaking private user content.

08 — Uncertainty

“We will not guess” must still move the person forward

OutcomeExplainOfferNever say
Missing material factThe fact and why it changes the branch.Answer question, mark unknown or save.“Something went wrong.”
Jurisdiction/date ambiguityCompeting scopes and consequence.Choose/confirm without inferred default.One province/date selected invisibly.
Insufficient official evidenceSources and corpus scope searched.Official-source path, report gap, professional research.Nearest result as likely answer.
Authority conflictCompeting propositions, courts, dates and coverage.Inspect both; qualified professional review.One unexplained confidence score.
Outside product scopeWhat is not covered.Appropriate official/legal-aid or professional route.“No law exists.”
Technical/provider failureWhich capability is unavailable, without sensitive detail.Deterministic citation/offline lookup, retry later.Model-only fallback.

An abstention retains the same calm visual hierarchy as an answer. It shows search scope, corpus version/date where useful, one primary recovery action and a report-gap path. It does not shame the question, blame the user or imply that rephrasing guarantees an answer.

09 — Language and bidi

Parity is legal force, not translated chrome

Language contracts

  • English and Urdu are equal product modes.
  • Roman Urdu is a supported input/retrieval mode, not labelled an authentic statutory text.
  • Official text is verbatim and its authentic language is labelled from L2.
  • Plain explanation is visibly separate from translation and quotation.
  • Glossary terms preserve definition scope and source.
  • “Shall”, “may”, “subject to”, “provided that” and negatives receive legal review.

Bidirectional contract

قتلِ عمد کے بارے میں دفعہ s. 302–304 PPC ملاحظہ کریں۔

Urdu blocks declare lang="ur" and dir="rtl". Citation, case number, date and URL runs are tightly wrapped LTR isolates. Western digits remain in legal identifiers. DOM order follows meaning; CSS must not reverse semantic order.

9.1Translation assurance

One grounded payload drives both languages. Independent bilingual legal reviewers label material propositions, omissions, modality, dates, actors and qualifications. A parity failure with legal effect blocks that language/version. The interface may state “translation under review” but may not silently fall back to a different legal claim.

10 — Plain language and voice

Reduce linguistic burden without reducing the law

RuleImplementationLegal guard
One propositionShort paragraph, informative heading and concrete actor/action.Do not separate a rule from its material exception.
Common words firstPlain term followed by legal term and glossary when necessary.Defined terms retain instrument-specific meaning.
Direct modalitySay “must”, “may”, “cannot” or “depends because”.No stronger modality than source/rule permits.
Explain numbersShow date/amount in prose plus expandable calculation.User can inspect inputs, exclusions and versioned rule.
Layer detailPlain conclusion → reasoning → exact source.Progressive disclosure never deletes qualification.

ISO 24495-1:2023 and ISO 24495-2:2025 guide plain-language and legal communication, but English examples are not treated as validated Urdu rules. Pakistani users and bilingual lawyers test actual comprehension.

10.1Voice

  • Voice begins only after explicit activation; always show a live transcript that can be edited before submission.
  • Announce whether official text, translation or explanation is being read.
  • Dates, section numbers and negation receive pronunciation fixtures; provide replay, speed and text alternatives.
  • Do not infer consent or a legally consequential answer from silence, background speech or low-confidence recognition.
  • If anonymous voice cannot remain request-local under Doc 11, it is unavailable with a plain explanation—not secretly persisted.
11 — Calculators and drafting

Deterministic tools show their work

Deadline and money calculation

  1. Name jurisdiction, remedy and rule version.
  2. Collect each legally distinct event date.
  3. Show included/excluded days, holidays and branch decisions.
  4. Render result as date, range or unknown—not false precision.
  5. Confirm inputs before export; attach sources and trace.
  6. Explain that court findings/discretion may change applicability.

Document drafting

  1. Separate supplied facts, assumptions and unresolved fields.
  2. Reviewed rules—not the model—select approved clauses.
  3. Trace each clause to rule, version and official source.
  4. Mark generated text and draft/review state on every page.
  5. Prevent export when mandatory facts or safety gates fail.
  6. No “lawyer reviewed” status without named valid review event.

WCAG 2.2’s error-prevention requirements for legal, financial and data actions inform confirmation, review and reversibility. Submission to a court or authority is outside the pilot unless separately designed, authorised, integrated and legally reviewed.

12 — Trust and privacy

Make data consequences legible at the moment of choice

  • Anonymous/signed-in state is named near the question field and history control, not buried in policy text.
  • Notification previews and screen titles are privacy-neutral by default; user can choose a private matter label.
  • Share/export names recipient/scope/expiry and offers revocation where supported. No public bearer link by default.
  • Account privacy centre shows categories, sessions, exports, deletion queue and optional-reuse consent independently.
  • Security cannot be marketed as advocate-client privilege. Professional confidentiality belongs to applicable legal relationships, not interface decoration.
13 — State architecture

Design every state before an engineer invents it

StateRequired message/actionForbidden fallback
First use / emptyExplain the job with two grounded examples; one primary action.Fake recent matters or promotional claims.
ClarifyingProgress is semantic (“2 material questions remain”), with back/edit/unknown.Arbitrary percent-complete.
Searching / streamingAnnounce the stage without leaking content. Cancellation stops work. Partial prose remains visibly incomplete.Clickable unverified citations during stream.
OfflinePack version, scope and last published date; available actions only.Greyed online control without explanation.
Stale packContinue historical read, warn before current-law reliance, update/rollback options.Present stale material as current.
Partial serviceName unavailable capability; preserve deterministic public-law lookup.Model-only or unverified local answer.
Auth expired / forbiddenPreserve unsent local input safely where policy permits; explain recovery.Reveal whether another user’s object exists.
Changed lawKeep old artefact replayable; mark superseded context and offer fresh analysis.Regenerate old answer invisibly.
Deleted / deletion pendingShow scope and completion stage without retaining deleted narrative.UI-only deletion while derivatives remain active.

Status updates use programmatically determinable messages without stealing focus. Errors preserve entered values except secrets, attach messages to fields, describe recovery and never expose traces, identifiers or legal content in support codes.

14 — Accessibility

AA is the floor; task equivalence is the outcome

Core web journeys target WCAG 2.2 AA as complete processes. Native mobile uses the same success criteria where applicable plus platform semantics and Document 08’s 48 dp target. A conformance claim requires declared scope, versions and evidence; automated scans alone cannot make it.

CapabilityAcceptance contract
Structure/navigationOne logical heading hierarchy, landmarks, skip link, meaningful titles, stable help and visible location.
Keyboard/switchAll actions reachable; no trap; visible unobscured focus; no drag-only action; reading and focus order match.
Screen readerNames/roles/states, table relationships, expanded/collapsed source state, status announcements and streaming batches tested.
VisualText reflows at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom; contrast and non-colour status marks; no clipped Nastaliq or forced orientation.
Motor/touch48 dp product target with clear spacing; cancellation/reversal for high-impact action; no precision gesture requirement.
Cognitive/languageConsistent navigation, plain instructions, redundant-entry avoidance, review before legal/data action and no timed reading.
Audio/speechTranscript/caption alternative, no autoplay, microphone state announced and input does not rely on pronunciation alone.
AuthenticationNo puzzle/memory/cognitive-function test without accessible alternative; OTP supports paste/autofill and clear expiry/retry.

WCAG does not cover every cognitive, language or learning need. The W3C supplemental cognitive guidance and testing with real disabled users therefore sit alongside—not underneath—conformance testing. Urdu screen-reader, font scaling, bidi focus order and mixed-script pronunciation receive dedicated fixtures.

15 — Mobile and offline

Connectivity is a capability state, not a moral judgment

Full online

Retrieval, verified generation, domain tools, authenticated matters and sync. Optimistic chrome never fabricates legal completion.

Degraded online

Deterministic citation/public corpus continues. Provider-dependent answer is clearly unavailable; queued writes are idempotent and user-visible.

Offline

Signed held statutes, local exact/lexical search, bookmarks and precomputed explainers. No implication that pack scope equals all Pakistani law.

  • Pack header shows corpus revision, jurisdictions/source kinds, publication date, signature state and update size before download.
  • “Not in this pack”, “not found in held law” and “no applicable law established” are distinct outcomes.
  • Install is atomic; tampered/incompatible pack is rejected; last-known-good remains usable and rollback is explained.
  • Reconnect compares local intentions and server state; conflicts are presented by meaning, never resolved last-write-wins for legal artefacts.
  • Performance budgets from Doc 08 protect usable first content, scrolling and input on representative low-end hardware.
16 — Content system

Legal language is a versioned interface dependency

ContentPattern {
  id; purpose; riskClass; journeyStates[];
  en: { text; readingReview; legalReview };
  ur: { text; translator; independentLegalReviewer };
  variables: [{ name; type; source; bidi; formatting }];
  forbiddenPhrases[]; examples[]; accessibilityNotes[];
  authority?: { ruleId; sourceIds[]; asOfBehaviour };
  version; approvedBy; effectiveFrom; regressionFixtures[];
}
RegisterPreferred patternAvoid
Evidence“Section 9 states…” / “The cited judgment records…”“The AI knows…”
Conditional“If [material fact], then…”Hedging every sentence with “may possibly”.
Unknown“We could not establish [specific fact] from [scope].”“No law exists.”
Professional review“A qualified Pakistani advocate should review [specific issue] because…”Generic disclaimer as an answer substitute.
Identity“Phone number verified” / “Advocate verification valid until…”“Verified user” when only possession is known.
Draft“Draft generated from supplied facts; not filed or advocate-approved.”“Legal document complete.”

Content changes that affect legal modality, user action, scope, warning or consent are reviewed and released like code. String concatenation cannot assemble citations, Urdu grammar or legal claims; typed variables carry direction, locale, source and formatting.

17 — Research programme

Co-design with the people the service could otherwise exclude

Research stratumMinimum variation to seekEthical safeguard
Language/literacyNative Urdu, English, Roman Urdu, mixed script; different reading confidence.Researcher reads consent aloud; comprehension checked without testing participant.
Geography/accessFederal/four provinces, urban/rural, low-data and shared-device contexts.Do not collect exact location or active legal dispute unnecessarily.
DisabilityBlind/low vision, Deaf/hard of hearing, motor, speech, cognitive/learning; novice and experienced AT users.Accessible materials/environment, chosen support person, fair compensation.
Legal experienceCitizens, legal-aid/frontline workers, advocates, students, researchers and curators.Conflicts disclosed; professional participants do not convert session into representation.
Risk contextEviction, employment, family, property, criminal/procedure and administrative journeys using fictional cases.Trauma-aware stop/skip; no demand to recount personal harm.

Consent is ongoing, withdrawal is easy, recordings are optional and retention is declared. Researchers record behavioural evidence and participant meaning, not voyeuristic case detail. Small qualitative samples identify failures but are not presented as population prevalence. W3C guidance supports combining diverse disabled-user involvement with standards rather than substituting one for the other.

18 — UX assurance

Measure understanding and safe action, not delight alone

MeasureOperational definitionCritical event
Scope comprehensionUser accurately states jurisdiction, date and important assumptions without prompting.Relies on wrong province/date/forum.
Source verificationFinds exact supporting span and identifies official source/status.Attributes generated explanation to statute/court.
Deadline comprehensionStates date/range, triggering event and uncertainty.Deadline overlooked or calculation treated as guaranteed.
Abstention comprehensionCan explain why no answer and choose a safe next step.Interprets abstention as “no legal right exists”.
Register recognitionDistinguishes official text, translation, explanation, rule result and professional review.Believes model is advocate/court or draft is filed-ready.
Journey completionCompletes defined task without facilitator rescue, by declared language/device/AT slice.Core task impossible in a supported mode.
Privacy predictionCorrectly predicts whether content is saved/shared/deletable before action.Anonymous user believes history is saved or signed-in user misses disclosure.
RecoveryReturns from offline/provider/auth/validation failure without duplicate or lost legal state.Unsafe fallback or silent state corruption.

Report task success, critical errors, unassisted completion, comprehension, time where appropriate, confidence calibration and qualitative cause by declared slice. Satisfaction never compensates for a legal-safety failure. Doc 10 controls sampling, confidence intervals, critical-event vetoes, bilingual parity and release cards.

UX release blockers

Any tested path that makes repealed law appear current; hides a material deadline; fabricates or prevents verification of a citation; changes legal meaning in Urdu; turns abstention into an answer/error; implies phone possession is identity; exposes another matter; claims anonymous persistence; accepts a tampered pack; or permits an unreviewed legal action is an S0/S1 event.

Design artefacts are executable agreements

19.1Definition of ready

A feature is not ready for implementation until its journey, all failure states, content, data consequence, API contract, accessibility semantics, offline behaviour, legal review points, analytics allowlist and acceptance tests are present. A static happy-path mock is insufficient.

19.2Build order

  1. Research foundation and high-harm journey scenarios.
  2. Information architecture, anonymous question, exact citation and abstention.
  3. Source viewer, temporal status and English/Urdu parity.
  4. Authenticated matters, privacy controls and changed-law state.
  5. Deterministic calculators/procedures, then reviewed drafting.
  6. Professional research and curation workspaces.
  7. Continuous accessibility, low-device, offline and comprehension assurance.

§1Ground
truth

What the data on disk actually says

Before any architecture, the facts. I sampled every archive in data/ and parsed the manifests. Three findings overturn assumptions baked into all four proposals.

Measured 24 Aug 2026. Text-layer rate from a 25-PDF random sample per corpus (first 5 pages, >300 extracted chars = has text layer).

Federal (Pakistan Code)1,038444 MB24/25Year folders 1839–2026 + latest ordinancesHave
Punjab1,064344 MB25/25Laws + Service Rules subtreeHave
